```cpp
// rag/agent/agent.hpp — the decision-making core of a self-learning agent.
//
//   observation ─► encoder ─► learner's Q-values ─► policy (ε-greedy) ─► action
//        ▲                         ▲
//        │                         └── learning: every step (TD + replay) or
//        │                             every episode (episodic memory)
//        └──────── reward, next observation ◄── environment
//
// The agent never sees the environment's internals: only observations, the
// action count, rewards, and the environment's feature ranges. The same
// agent learns ChainEnv and ExecutionEnv unchanged.
//
// Exploration is the price of learning: a fraction ε of decisions are random.
// ε decays as the agent gains experience, and reexplore() raises it again
// temporarily (the Trainer calls it when it detects that the world changed).
#pragma once

#include <algorithm>
#include <array>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <limits>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <vector>

#include "rag/agent/env.hpp"
#include "rag/agent/features.hpp"
#include "rag/agent/learners.hpp"
#include "rag/agent/mlp.hpp"
#include "rag/agent/rng.hpp"

namespace rag::agent {

enum class LearnerKind : std::uint8_t {
  TileQ,     // parametric: tile coding + Q-learning + experience replay
  Episodic,  // instance-based: k-NN over remembered situations (episodic control)
  // Policy gradient: a softmax policy over tile-coded logits (the actor) and a
  // tile-coded state value (the critic); the critic's TD error is the
  // actor's advantage. On-policy: exploration comes from sampling the policy
  // (epsilon only applies during reexplore()), no replay. Measured best
  // model-free learner on ExecutionEnv (EXPERIMENTS.md E5).
  ActorCritic,
  // DQN-style: an MLP (ReLU, Adam) over the features, n-step targets from a
  // target network, uniform replay of n-step transitions, one minibatch per
  // step taken (applied at episode end). Measured on ExecutionEnv: 84-89% of
  // the optimal gain at 40k episodes vs 65-69% for TileQ (EXPERIMENTS.md
  // E16); ~75x the training compute per episode, 1.7 us per decision.
  NeuralQ,
};

template <std::size_t Dims>
struct AgentConfig {
  LearnerKind learner = LearnerKind::TileQ;

  // Exploration: ε falls linearly from eps_start to eps_end over
  // eps_decay_episodes, then stays at eps_end (never 0: a world that changes
  // can only be noticed by an agent that still occasionally tries things).
  double eps_start = 1.0;
  double eps_end = 0.02;
  std::uint32_t eps_decay_episodes = 1500;

  // Parametric learner.
  std::array<std::uint32_t, Dims> bins{};  // grid cells per dimension; 0 => 8
  std::uint32_t tilings = 8;
  // Step size: alpha / (1 + episodes / alpha_decay_episodes), never below
  // alpha_min. Shrinking it averages out reward noise as experience grows;
  // the floor keeps the agent able to learn if the world changes.
  double alpha = 0.1;
  double alpha_min = 0.003;
  std::uint32_t alpha_decay_episodes = 3000;  // 0 = constant step size
  double gamma = 1.0;  // discount; 1 for fixed-horizon tasks
  double init_q = 0.0;
  // Double Q-learning (van Hasselt, 2010): two estimators, each updated
  // toward the other's value of its own best next action. Removes the upward
  // bias that max() over noisy estimates puts into every Q-learning target.
  bool double_q = false;  // measured: on ExecutionEnv, halving each estimator's updates costs more than the bias it removes
  // Advantage learning (Baird 1999; Bellemare et al. 2016): subtract k times
  // the action's advantage deficit from its target, widening action gaps
  // while keeping the optimal policy. 0 = plain Q-learning. TileQ (E19) and
  // NeuralQ (E20; there double_q means Double DQN: the online network picks
  // the next action, the target network values it).
  double advantage_learning = 0.0;
  std::uint32_t replay_capacity = 100'000;
  std::uint32_t replay_per_step = 4;  // extra updates from replayed experience per real step
  // n-step returns: targets sum n real rewards before bootstrapping from
  // Q(s_{t+n}). n = 1 is plain Q-learning; n >= the horizon is Monte Carlo.
  // (No off-policy correction: exploratory actions inside the n steps bias
  // targets toward the behaviour policy.)
  std::uint32_t n_step = 3;  // measured best of 1,2,3,5,10,20 (EXPERIMENTS.md E2)

  // Actor-critic learner (annealed by the same schedule as alpha).
  double actor_alpha = 0.03;
  double critic_alpha = 0.1;
  double temperature = 1.0;  // softmax temperature of the policy
  // Actor-critic step sizes decay as 1 / (1 + episodes / ac_decay_episodes)
  // (floor alpha_min / alpha). Measured: 3,000 (the TileQ default) shrinks the
  // actor's steps before the policy forms (-235% to 7% at 10k episodes on
  // some seeds); 10,000 gives 75-78% at 10k and 80-86% at 40k.
  std::uint32_t ac_decay_episodes = 10000;
  // How ActorCritic re-explores after a drift: 0 = epsilon-uniform actions
  // (off-policy for the actor's update), > 0 = sample the policy itself at a
  // temperature raised by this factor, decaying with the boost (stays
  // on-policy). E13.
  double ac_reexplore_temperature = 0.0;

  // Episodic learner.
  EpisodicParams memory{};
  std::array<double, Dims> kernel_width{};  // similarity length scale per dimension; 0 => 10% of the range

  // NeuralQ learner.
  std::uint32_t nn_hidden = 64;          // units in each of two hidden layers
  double nn_lr = 1e-3;                   // Adam step size
  std::uint32_t nn_batch = 32;           // minibatch per update
  std::uint32_t nn_target_sync = 2000;   // updates between target-network copies (0 = no target network)
  std::uint32_t nn_warmup = 2000;        // transitions in replay before updates start
  // Weight averaging (E24): > 0 keeps an exponential moving average of the
  // network's weights, avg += nn_polyak * (net - avg) after every update.
  // Exploring actions still use the online network (training is unchanged);
  // greedy actions, snapshots and so the deployed policy use the average.
  double nn_polyak = 0.0;

  std::uint64_t seed = 1;
};

template <Environment Env>
class Agent {
 public:
  using Obs = typename Env::Observation;
  static constexpr std::size_t A = Env::kNumActions;
  static constexpr std::size_t Dims = Env::kStateDims;
  static constexpr std::size_t kEmbed = 64;  // episodic embedding size
  using Config = AgentConfig<Dims>;
  using Memory = EpisodicMemory<kEmbed, A>;

  explicit Agent(const Env& env, Config cfg = {})
      : env_(env), cfg_(defaults(cfg)),
        coder_(Env::kLo, Env::kHi, cfg_.bins, cfg_.tilings),
        embed_(cfg_.kernel_width, cfg_.seed ^ 0xE5BEDull),
        // NeuralQ uses neither tile table: allocating them anyway costs
        // (bins + 1)^Dims cells each (2^21 x 8 tilings x 5 actions = 670 MB at
        // 21 inputs) and every snapshot copies them.
        q_(cfg_.learner == LearnerKind::NeuralQ ? TileQ{} : TileQ(coder_.size(), cfg_.tilings, static_cast<std::uint32_t>(A), cfg_.alpha, cfg_.init_q)),
        q2_(cfg_.double_q && cfg_.learner != LearnerKind::NeuralQ ? q_ : TileQ{}),
        critic_(cfg_.learner == LearnerKind::ActorCritic ? TileQ(coder_.size(), cfg_.tilings, 1, cfg_.critic_alpha) : TileQ{}),
        replay_(cfg_.learner == LearnerKind::TileQ ? cfg_.replay_capacity : 0),
        mem_(cfg_.memory),
        rng_(cfg_.seed) {
    episode_.reserve(1024);
    pending_.reserve(cfg_.n_step + 1);
    if (cfg_.learner == LearnerKind::NeuralQ) {
      Rng init(cfg_.seed ^ 0x4E4E4E4Eull);
      net_ = Mlp({static_cast<std::uint32_t>(Dims), cfg_.nn_hidden, cfg_.nn_hidden, static_cast<std::uint32_t>(A)}, init);
      target_ = net_;
      avg_ = net_;
      nscratch_.resize(net_.scratch_size());
      nreplay_.reserve(std::min<std::size_t>(cfg_.replay_capacity, 1u << 16));
    }
    apply_step_sizes();  // actor-critic step sizes from the first episode on
  }

  // ------------------------------------------------------------- decide
  // explore = true: ε-greedy with random tie-breaking (training).
  // explore = false: purely greedy, deterministic (evaluation / deployment).
  // Allocation-free.
  Action act(const Obs& o, bool explore) noexcept {
    if (cfg_.learner == LearnerKind::ActorCritic) return act_policy(o, explore);
    if (explore && rng_.uniform() < epsilon()) return rng_.below(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(A));
    std::array<double, A> q;
    std::array<bool, A> known;
    if (!explore && averaging())
      estimate_with(q_, q2_, mem_, avg_, o, q.data(), known.data());  // greedy: the averaged weights
    else
      estimate(o, q.data(), known.data());
    // Unknown actions (episodic memory only): optimistic while exploring, so
    // untried actions get tried; avoided when acting for real.
    for (std::size_t a = 0; a < A; ++a)
      if (!known[a]) q[a] = explore ? std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity() : -std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity();
    Action best = 0;
    std::uint32_t ties = 1;
    for (Action a = 1; a < A; ++a) {
      if (q[a] > q[best]) { best = a; ties = 1; }
      else if (explore && q[a] == q[best] && rng_.below(++ties) == 0) best = a;  // uniform among ties
    }
    return best;
  }

  // The learner's current value estimates (unknown actions read as 0).
  void q_values(const Obs& o, double* out) const noexcept {
    std::array<bool, A> known;
    estimate(o, out, known.data());
  }

  // Predicted return from o under the greedy policy (the critic, for ActorCritic).
  [[nodiscard]] double value(const Obs& o) const noexcept {
    if (cfg_.learner == LearnerKind::ActorCritic) {
      std::array<std::uint32_t, kMaxTilings> idx;
      coder_.encode(env_.features(o), idx.data());
      return critic_.q(idx.data(), 0);
    }
    std::array<double, A> q;
    std::array<bool, A> known;
    estimate(o, q.data(), known.data());
    double v = -std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity();
    bool any = false;
    for (std::size_t a = 0; a < A; ++a)
      if (known[a]) { v = std::max(v, q[a]); any = true; }
    return any ? v : 0.0;
  }

  // -------------------------------------------------------------- learn
  // Called after every real step.
  void observe(const Obs& o, Action a, double r, const Obs& next, bool done) {
    if (cfg_.learner == LearnerKind::ActorCritic) {
      std::array<std::uint32_t, kMaxTilings> s, s2;
      coder_.encode(env_.features(o), s.data());
      coder_.encode(env_.features(next), s2.data());
      const double target = r + (done ? 0.0 : cfg_.gamma * critic_.q(s2.data(), 0));
      const double delta = target - critic_.q(s.data(), 0);  // TD error = advantage estimate
      critic_.update(s.data(), 0, target);
      std::array<double, A> pi;
      const double temp = sampling_temperature();
      policy(s.data(), q_, pi.data(), temp);
      // grad log pi(a|s) wrt the logit of b = (1[b == a] - pi(b)) / temperature
      for (Action b = 0; b < A; ++b) q_.update(s.data(), b, q_.q(s.data(), b) + delta * ((b == a ? 1.0 : 0.0) - pi[b]) / temp);
      return;
    }
    if (cfg_.learner == LearnerKind::Episodic) {
      episode_.push_back({env_.features(o), a, r});
      return;
    }
    if (cfg_.learner == LearnerKind::NeuralQ) {
      episode_.push_back({env_.features(o), a, r});
      if (done) neural_learn_episode();
      (void)next;
      return;
    }
    if (cfg_.n_step <= 1) {
      Transition t;
      coder_.encode(env_.features(o), t.s.data());
      coder_.encode(env_.features(next), t.next.data());
      t.reward = static_cast<float>(r);
      t.action = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(a);
      t.done = done;
      learn_from(t);
      return;
    }
    // n-step: hold the last n steps; once n are pending (or the episode
    // ends), the oldest becomes a transition to the state n steps later.
    PendingStep ps;
    coder_.encode(env_.features(o), ps.s.data());
    ps.action = a;
    ps.reward = r;
    pending_.push_back(ps);
    if (done) {
      while (!pending_.empty()) emit_pending(next, true);
    } else if (pending_.size() >= cfg_.n_step) {
      emit_pending(next, false);
    }
  }

  // Called once at the end of every training episode.
  void end_episode() {
    if (cfg_.learner == LearnerKind::NeuralQ && !episode_.empty()) neural_learn_episode();
    if (cfg_.learner == LearnerKind::Episodic) {
      double g = 0;  // Monte Carlo return-to-go, computed backwards
      alignas(kCacheLine) std::array<float, kEmbed> key;
      for (std::size_t i = episode_.size(); i-- > 0;) {
        g = episode_[i].reward + cfg_.gamma * g;
        embed_.encode(episode_[i].features, key.data());
        mem_.write(key.data(), episode_[i].action, g);
      }
      episode_.clear();
    }
    ++episodes_;
    ++plastic_episodes_;
    if (boost_left_ > 0) --boost_left_;
    apply_step_sizes();
  }

  // Current TD step size: annealed, and raised during re-exploration so the
  // agent can unlearn what no longer holds.
  [[nodiscard]] double step_size() const noexcept {
    double a = cfg_.alpha;
    if (cfg_.alpha_decay_episodes)
      a = std::max(cfg_.alpha_min, cfg_.alpha / (1.0 + static_cast<double>(plastic_episodes_) / cfg_.alpha_decay_episodes));
    return a;
  }

  // ------------------------------------------------------- exploration
  [[nodiscard]] double epsilon() const noexcept {
    const double f = std::min(1.0, static_cast<double>(episodes_) / std::max(1u, cfg_.eps_decay_episodes));
    double eps = cfg_.eps_start + (cfg_.eps_end - cfg_.eps_start) * f;
    if (boost_left_ > 0) eps = std::max(eps, boost_eps_ * boost_left_ / boost_total_);
    return eps;
  }

  // Raise ε to `eps`, decaying linearly back over `episodes` episodes.
  // Also restarts step-size annealing: re-learning needs plasticity.
  void reexplore(double eps, std::uint32_t episodes) noexcept {
    boost_eps_ = eps;
    boost_total_ = boost_left_ = std::max(1u, episodes);
    plastic_episodes_ = 0;
    apply_step_sizes();
  }

  // ---------------------------------------------------------- snapshots
  // The learned state only (no replay buffer, no RNG): what a champion
  // policy needs. Restoring one makes the agent act exactly like it.
  struct Snapshot {
    TileQ q, q2;  // q: Q-values, or the actor's logits for ActorCritic
    Memory mem;
    TileQ critic;
    Mlp net;  // NeuralQ
  };
  [[nodiscard]] Snapshot snapshot() const { return {q_, q2_, mem_, critic_, averaging() ? avg_ : net_}; }

  // Act greedily as the snapshot would, without touching the learner: the
  // deployed (champion) policy and the still-learning one coexist.
  [[nodiscard]] Action act_as(const Snapshot& s, const Obs& o) const noexcept {
    std::array<double, A> q;
    std::array<bool, A> known;
    estimate_with(s.q, s.q2, s.mem, s.net, o, q.data(), known.data());
    Action best = 0;
    for (Action a = 1; a < A; ++a)
      if ((known[a] && !known[best]) || (known[a] == known[best] && q[a] > q[best])) best = a;
    return best;
  }
  void restore(const Snapshot& s) {
    q_ = s.q;
    q2_ = s.q2;
    mem_ = s.mem;
    critic_ = s.critic;
    net_ = s.net;  // the target network is training state, not policy: left alone
    if (averaging()) avg_ = s.net;
  }

  // Supervised warm start (TileQ only): regress the Q-function onto a
  // teacher's action values, e.g. the plan of a learned model, on states
  // visited in `sim` (a simulator, e.g. the model's own market, so no real
  // experience is spent) by the teacher's greedy policy, with random actions
  // at rate `eps` for coverage. Episode count, schedules and replay are
  // untouched: RL fine-tuning then starts from the teacher's knowledge, and
  // real rewards correct whatever the teacher got wrong (E7). Returns false
  // (and does nothing) for other learners.
  template <class TeacherQ>
  bool distill(const Env& sim, TeacherQ&& teacher_q, std::uint32_t episodes, std::uint64_t seed, double eps = 0.2) {
    if (cfg_.learner != LearnerKind::TileQ) return false;
    Env env = sim;
    Rng rng(seed), pick(seed ^ 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15ull);
    const double saved = q_.alpha();
    std::array<std::uint32_t, kMaxTilings> idx;
    std::array<double, A> tq;
    for (std::uint32_t ep = 0; ep < episodes; ++ep) {
      q_.set_alpha(std::max(0.005, cfg_.alpha / (1.0 + static_cast<double>(ep) / 3000.0)));
      auto o = env.reset(rng);
      for (;;) {
        coder_.encode(env_.features(o), idx.data());
        Action best = 0;
        for (Action a = 0; a < A; ++a) {
          tq[a] = teacher_q(o, a);
          q_.update(idx.data(), a, tq[a]);
          if (tq[a] > tq[best]) best = a;
        }
        const Action act = pick.uniform() < eps ? static_cast<Action>(pick.below(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(A))) : best;
        const auto st = env.step(act, rng);
        if (st.done) break;
        o = st.obs;
      }
    }
    q_.set_alpha(saved);
    if (cfg_.double_q) q2_ = q_;
    return true;
  }

  // Drop replayed experience. After the world changes, old transitions
  // describe dynamics that no longer hold, and replaying them keeps
  // teaching the agent the past.
  void forget_experience() noexcept {
    replay_.clear();
    nreplay_.clear();
    nhead_ = 0;
  }

  [[nodiscard]] std::uint64_t episodes() const noexcept { return episodes_; }
  [[nodiscard]] const Config& config() const noexcept { return cfg_; }
  [[nodiscard]] const TileQ& q_learner() const noexcept { return q_; }
  [[nodiscard]] const Memory& memory() const noexcept { return mem_; }
  [[nodiscard]] std::size_t replay_size() const noexcept { return replay_.size(); }

 private:
  struct EpisodeStep {
    std::array<double, Dims> features;
    Action action;
    double reward;
  };
  struct PendingStep {
    std::array<std::uint32_t, kMaxTilings> s;
    Action action;
    double reward;
  };

  // Softmax policy of the logits in `actor` at tiles idx (numerically stable).
  void policy(const std::uint32_t* idx, const TileQ& actor, double* pi, double temperature = 0) const noexcept {
    if (temperature <= 0) temperature = cfg_.temperature;
    std::array<double, A> h;
    actor.q_values(idx, h.data());
    const double m = *std::max_element(h.begin(), h.end());
    double z = 0;
    for (std::size_t a = 0; a < A; ++a) z += (pi[a] = std::exp((h[a] - m) / temperature));
    for (std::size_t a = 0; a < A; ++a) pi[a] /= z;
  }

  // ActorCritic's sampling temperature: raised during a re-exploration boost
  // when ac_reexplore_temperature > 0.
  [[nodiscard]] double sampling_temperature() const noexcept {
    if (cfg_.ac_reexplore_temperature <= 0 || boost_left_ == 0) return cfg_.temperature;
    return cfg_.temperature * (1.0 + cfg_.ac_reexplore_temperature * boost_left_ / boost_total_);
  }

  // ActorCritic acting: sample the policy while exploring, its mode otherwise.
  Action act_policy(const Obs& o, bool explore) noexcept {
    std::array<std::uint32_t, kMaxTilings> idx;
    coder_.encode(env_.features(o), idx.data());
    std::array<double, A> pi;
    policy(idx.data(), q_, pi.data(), explore ? sampling_temperature() : 0.0);
    if (!explore) return static_cast<Action>(std::max_element(pi.begin(), pi.end()) - pi.begin());
    if (cfg_.ac_reexplore_temperature <= 0 && boost_left_ > 0 && rng_.uniform() < epsilon())
      return rng_.below(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(A));
    double u = rng_.uniform();
    for (Action a = 0; a + 1 < A; ++a)
      if ((u -= pi[a]) <= 0) return a;
    return static_cast<Action>(A - 1);
  }

  void apply_step_sizes() noexcept {
    const double a = step_size();
    if (cfg_.learner == LearnerKind::ActorCritic) {
      const double f = std::max(cfg_.alpha_min / cfg_.alpha,
                                1.0 / (1.0 + static_cast<double>(plastic_episodes_) / std::max(1u, cfg_.ac_decay_episodes)));
      q_.set_alpha(cfg_.actor_alpha * f);
      critic_.set_alpha(cfg_.critic_alpha * f);
      return;
    }
    q_.set_alpha(a);
    if (cfg_.double_q) q2_.set_alpha(a);
  }

  void learn_from(const Transition& t) {
    td_update(t);
    replay_.push(t);
    for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < cfg_.replay_per_step && replay_.size() > 1; ++i) td_update(replay_.sample(rng_));
  }

  // Turn the oldest pending step into an n-step transition ending at `next`.
  void emit_pending(const Obs& next, bool done) {
    Transition t;
    const PendingStep& first = pending_.front();
    t.s = first.s;
    t.action = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(first.action);
    double g = 0, disc = 1;
    for (const PendingStep& p : pending_) {
      g += disc * p.reward;
      disc *= cfg_.gamma;
    }
    t.reward = static_cast<float>(g);
    t.steps = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(std::min<std::size_t>(pending_.size(), 255));
    t.done = done;
    coder_.encode(env_.features(next), t.next.data());
    pending_.erase(pending_.begin());
    learn_from(t);
  }

  static Config defaults(Config c) {
    for (std::size_t d = 0; d < Dims; ++d) {
      if (c.bins[d] == 0) c.bins[d] = 8;
      if (c.kernel_width[d] <= 0) c.kernel_width[d] = 0.1 * (Env::kHi[d] - Env::kLo[d]);
    }
    if (c.tilings == 0 || c.tilings > kMaxTilings) throw std::invalid_argument("AgentConfig: tilings in [1, 32]");
    if (!(c.alpha > 0) || !(c.gamma > 0) || c.gamma > 1) throw std::invalid_argument("AgentConfig: need alpha > 0, 0 < gamma <= 1");
    if (c.eps_start < c.eps_end || c.eps_end < 0 || c.eps_start > 1) throw std::invalid_argument("AgentConfig: need 0 <= eps_end <= eps_start <= 1");
    if (!(c.nn_polyak >= 0 && c.nn_polyak <= 1)) throw std::invalid_argument("AgentConfig: nn_polyak in [0, 1]");
    return c;
  }

  void estimate(const Obs& o, double* out, bool* known) const noexcept { estimate_with(q_, q2_, mem_, net_, o, out, known); }

  void estimate_with(const TileQ& q1, const TileQ& q2, const Memory& mem, const Mlp& net, const Obs& o, double* out,
                     bool* known) const noexcept {
    if (cfg_.learner == LearnerKind::NeuralQ) {
      const auto f = env_.features(o);
      net.forward(f.data(), out, nscratch_.data());
      for (std::size_t a = 0; a < A; ++a) known[a] = true;
      return;
    }
    if (cfg_.learner != LearnerKind::Episodic) {  // TileQ values, or ActorCritic logits
      std::array<std::uint32_t, kMaxTilings> idx;
      coder_.encode(env_.features(o), idx.data());
      q1.q_values(idx.data(), out);
      if (cfg_.double_q) {  // act on the average of both estimators
        std::array<double, A> o2;
        q2.q_values(idx.data(), o2.data());
        for (std::size_t a = 0; a < A; ++a) out[a] = 0.5 * (out[a] + o2[a]);
      }
      for (std::size_t a = 0; a < A; ++a) known[a] = true;
      return;
    }
    alignas(kCacheLine) std::array<float, kEmbed> key;
    embed_.encode(env_.features(o), key.data());
    mem.estimate(key.data(), out, known);
  }

  // One Q-learning step: target = r + γ max_a' Q(s', a'). With double_q,
  // a coin picks which estimator learns; it chooses a' and the other one
  // values it.
  void td_update(const Transition& t) noexcept {
    TileQ* learn = &q_;
    const TileQ* judge = &q_;
    if (cfg_.double_q) {
      const bool flip = rng_.next() & 1;
      learn = flip ? &q2_ : &q_;
      judge = flip ? &q_ : &q2_;
    }
    double target = t.reward;
    if (!t.done) {
      std::array<double, A> qn;
      learn->q_values(t.next.data(), qn.data());
      const auto best = static_cast<Action>(std::max_element(qn.begin(), qn.end()) - qn.begin());
      const double boot = cfg_.gamma == 1.0 ? 1.0 : std::pow(cfg_.gamma, t.steps);
      target += boot * judge->q(t.next.data(), best);
    }
    if (cfg_.advantage_learning > 0) {
      std::array<double, A> qs;
      learn->q_values(t.s.data(), qs.data());
      target -= cfg_.advantage_learning * (*std::max_element(qs.begin(), qs.end()) - qs[t.action]);
    }
    learn->update(t.s.data(), t.action, target);
  }

  Env env_;  // a copy, used only for features()
  Config cfg_;
  TileCoder<Dims> coder_;
  RandomFourierEncoder<Dims, kEmbed> embed_;
  TileQ q_, q2_;  // q2_ is used only with double_q; q_ holds the actor's logits for ActorCritic
  TileQ critic_;  // ActorCritic only
  ReplayBuffer replay_;
  Memory mem_;
  std::vector<EpisodeStep> episode_;
  std::vector<PendingStep> pending_;  // n-step window (n_step > 1)
  Rng rng_;
  // NeuralQ: online and target networks, replay of n-step transitions in feature space.
  struct NeuralTransition {
    std::array<double, Dims> s, next;
    Action action;
    double ret;         // discounted sum of up to n rewards
    double bootstrap;   // gamma^steps, or 0 if the episode ended within n steps
  };
  Mlp net_, target_, avg_;  // avg_: weight average (nn_polyak > 0)
  [[nodiscard]] bool averaging() const noexcept { return cfg_.learner == LearnerKind::NeuralQ && cfg_.nn_polyak > 0; }
  std::vector<NeuralTransition> nreplay_;
  std::size_t nhead_ = 0;
  std::uint64_t nn_updates_ = 0;
  mutable std::vector<double> nscratch_;

  // Turn the finished episode into n-step transitions, then run one
  // minibatch update per step it took.
  void neural_learn_episode() {
    const std::size_t T = episode_.size();
    const std::uint32_t n = std::max(1u, cfg_.n_step);
    const std::size_t cap = std::max<std::size_t>(1, cfg_.replay_capacity);
    for (std::size_t t = 0; t < T; ++t) {
      NeuralTransition tr{};
      tr.s = episode_[t].features;
      tr.action = episode_[t].action;
      double disc = 1.0;
      std::size_t k = t;
      for (; k < std::min(T, t + n); ++k) {
        tr.ret += disc * episode_[k].reward;
        disc *= cfg_.gamma;
      }
      if (k < T) {
        tr.next = episode_[k].features;
        tr.bootstrap = disc;
      }
      if (nreplay_.size() < cap) {
        nreplay_.push_back(tr);
      } else {
        nreplay_[nhead_] = tr;
        nhead_ = (nhead_ + 1) % cap;
      }
    }
    episode_.clear();
    if (nreplay_.size() < cfg_.nn_warmup) return;
    std::array<double, A> qn;
    for (std::size_t u = 0; u < T; ++u) {
      for (std::uint32_t b = 0; b < cfg_.nn_batch; ++b) {
        const NeuralTransition& tr = nreplay_[rng_.below(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(nreplay_.size()))];
        double y = tr.ret;
        const Mlp& judge = cfg_.nn_target_sync ? target_ : net_;
        if (tr.bootstrap > 0) {
          judge.forward(tr.next.data(), qn.data(), nscratch_.data());
          if (cfg_.double_q) {  // Double DQN: the online network picks, the target network values
            std::array<double, A> qo;
            net_.forward(tr.next.data(), qo.data(), nscratch_.data());
            y += tr.bootstrap * qn[static_cast<std::size_t>(std::max_element(qo.begin(), qo.end()) - qo.begin())];
          } else {
            y += tr.bootstrap * *std::max_element(qn.begin(), qn.end());
          }
        }
        if (cfg_.advantage_learning > 0) {  // gap-increasing target (E19), with the online network
          std::array<double, A> qs;
          net_.forward(tr.s.data(), qs.data(), nscratch_.data());
          y -= cfg_.advantage_learning * (*std::max_element(qs.begin(), qs.end()) - qs[tr.action]);
        }
        net_.accumulate(tr.s.data(), tr.action, y);
      }
      net_.step(cfg_.nn_lr);
      if (averaging()) avg_.blend_toward(net_, cfg_.nn_polyak);
      if (cfg_.nn_target_sync && ++nn_updates_ % cfg_.nn_target_sync == 0) target_ = net_;
    }
  }

  std::uint64_t episodes_ = 0;
  std::uint64_t plastic_episodes_ = 0;  // episodes since the last reexplore() (step-size annealing clock)
  double boost_eps_ = 0;
  std::uint32_t boost_left_ = 0, boost_total_ = 1;
};

}  // namespace rag::agent
```

```cpp
// rag/agent/analysis.hpp — data analysis with Eigen (optional dependency:
// libeigen3-dev; CMake target Eigen3::Eigen). E18.
//
//   least_squares()          rank-revealing weighted least squares
//                            (column-pivoting Householder QR); used to
//                            cross-check the model-based agent's hand-written
//                            normal-equations solver
//   quadratic_sensitivity()  which parameters matter: fit
//                            score ~ b0 + sum b_i z_i + sum c_i z_i^2 on
//                            standardized parameters (e.g. a tuning history)
#pragma once

#include <Eigen/Dense>

#include <cmath>
#include <cstdint>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <vector>

namespace rag::agent::analysis {

// argmin_b sum_i w_i (y_i - x_i . b)^2. Empty weights mean all ones.
inline Eigen::VectorXd least_squares(const Eigen::MatrixXd& X, const Eigen::VectorXd& y, const Eigen::VectorXd& w = {}) {
  if (X.rows() != y.size()) throw std::invalid_argument("least_squares: X and y disagree");
  if (w.size() == 0) return X.colPivHouseholderQr().solve(y);
  if (w.size() != y.size()) throw std::invalid_argument("least_squares: wrong weight count");
  const Eigen::VectorXd sw = w.cwiseSqrt();
  return (sw.asDiagonal() * X).colPivHouseholderQr().solve(sw.asDiagonal() * y);
}

struct Sensitivity {
  std::vector<double> linear;     // effect of +1 standard deviation of each parameter
  std::vector<double> quadratic;  // curvature per parameter (negative: an interior optimum)
  double r2 = 0;                  // share of the score variance the surface explains
};

// Quadratic response surface over standardized parameters (no interactions).
// rows[i] holds one trial's parameter values; scores[i] its score.
inline Sensitivity quadratic_sensitivity(const std::vector<std::vector<double>>& rows, const std::vector<double>& scores) {
  const auto n = static_cast<Eigen::Index>(rows.size());
  if (n == 0 || scores.size() != rows.size()) throw std::invalid_argument("quadratic_sensitivity: empty or mismatched input");
  const auto k = static_cast<Eigen::Index>(rows[0].size());
  Eigen::MatrixXd raw(n, k);
  for (Eigen::Index i = 0; i < n; ++i)
    for (Eigen::Index j = 0; j < k; ++j) raw(i, j) = rows[static_cast<std::size_t>(i)][static_cast<std::size_t>(j)];
  const Eigen::RowVectorXd mean = raw.colwise().mean();
  Eigen::RowVectorXd sd = ((raw.rowwise() - mean).array().square().colwise().sum() / std::max<double>(1.0, static_cast<double>(n - 1))).sqrt();
  for (Eigen::Index j = 0; j < k; ++j)
    if (sd(j) <= 0) sd(j) = 1;  // a parameter that never moved: no information, no division by zero
  const Eigen::MatrixXd z = (raw.rowwise() - mean).array().rowwise() / sd.array();
  Eigen::MatrixXd X(n, 1 + 2 * k);
  X.col(0).setOnes();
  X.middleCols(1, k) = z;
  X.rightCols(k) = z.array().square().matrix();
  Eigen::VectorXd y(n);
  for (Eigen::Index i = 0; i < n; ++i) y(i) = scores[static_cast<std::size_t>(i)];
  const Eigen::VectorXd b = least_squares(X, y);
  Sensitivity s;
  for (Eigen::Index j = 0; j < k; ++j) {
    s.linear.push_back(b(1 + j));
    s.quadratic.push_back(b(1 + k + j));
  }
  const double tss = (y.array() - y.mean()).square().sum();
  const double rss = (y - X * b).squaredNorm();
  s.r2 = tss > 0 ? 1 - rss / tss : 0;
  return s;
}

}  // namespace rag::agent::analysis
```

```cpp
// rag/agent/drift.hpp — change detection on a stream of per-episode
// "surprise" values (what happened minus what was predicted).
//
// Used by the trainer (surprise against the agent's own value estimate,
// confirmed by re-scoring the champion) and by the model-based agent
// (surprise against its plan's predicted value; E9).
#pragma once

#include <algorithm>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdint>
#include <deque>

namespace rag::agent {

// Defaults chosen by simulation on Gaussian noise: about one false alarm
// per 200,000 episodes, and a shift of 0.55 standard deviations (what the
// ExecutionEnv regime flip produces) detected after a median of ~50 episodes.
struct DriftParams {
  std::uint32_t lag = 50;         // samples held back before they join the baseline
  double allowance = 0.3;         // CUSUM k, in standard deviations: ignore shifts smaller than ~2k
  double threshold = 16.0;        // CUSUM h, in standard deviations of accumulated evidence
  double baseline_rate = 0.001;   // EMA rate of the baseline (memory of ~1000 samples)
  std::uint32_t warmup = 1500;    // baseline samples needed before alarms (also after one)
  // Also flag sustained *upward* shifts. A world that got better is a change
  // too: the old policy still earns more than before, so a one-sided test
  // stays quiet while the agent leaves the new opportunity unused (E13).
  bool two_sided = false;
};

// Flags a sustained downward shift in "surprise" (return - predicted return)
// with a one-sided CUSUM test (Page, 1954):
//     S = min(0, S + z + k),   alarm when S < -h,   z = (x - mean) / sd
// and, with two_sided, an upward one with the mirror-image statistic
//     U = max(0, U + z - k),   alarm when U > h.
// Each sample adds evidence; ordinary noise drains it back toward 0 because
// of the allowance k, while a persistent shift accumulates until it crosses h.
//
// An alarm only clears the accumulated evidence. The caller decides what it
// meant: reset() after a confirmed change (the old baseline describes a world
// that's gone; rebuilding it takes `warmup` samples), or rebase() after a
// false alarm (re-centre on recent samples and stay armed). (E13: resetting
// on every alarm, including rejected ones, left the trainer blind for 1,550
// episodes, and a real change landed in that window.)
//
// The baseline (mean, sd) is built only from samples at least `lag` old, so
// a shift is measured against the world before it, not partly against
// itself; and it has a long memory, because a noisy baseline is itself a
// source of false alarms.
class DriftDetector {
 public:
  using Params = DriftParams;
  explicit DriftDetector(Params p = {}) : p_(p) {}

  // Feed one episode's surprise; returns true on an alarm.
  bool add(double surprise) {
    held_.push_back(surprise);
    if (held_.size() > p_.lag) {  // the oldest sample graduates into the baseline
      absorb(held_.front());
      held_.pop_front();
    }
    if (baseline_n_ < p_.warmup) return false;
    const double z = (surprise - mean_) / std::sqrt(std::max(var_, 1e-12));
    cusum_ = std::min(0.0, cusum_ + z + p_.allowance);
    if (p_.two_sided) up_ = std::max(0.0, up_ + z - p_.allowance);
    if (cusum_ < -p_.threshold || up_ > p_.threshold) {
      last_up_ = up_ > p_.threshold;
      cusum_ = up_ = 0;
      return true;
    }
    return false;
  }

  // After a false alarm: keep the baseline's spread, move its centre to the
  // recent (lagged-window) samples and let the next ones refine it as a
  // fresh running mean; clear the evidence; stay armed.
  void rebase() {
    if (!held_.empty()) {
      double s = 0;
      for (double x : held_) s += x;
      mean_ = s / static_cast<double>(held_.size());
      rate_n_ = held_.size();
    }
    cusum_ = up_ = 0;
  }

  void reset() {
    held_.clear();
    baseline_n_ = rate_n_ = 0;
    mean_ = var_ = cusum_ = up_ = 0;
  }

  // Direction of the last alarm: true if returns rose above expectations.
  [[nodiscard]] bool last_alarm_was_upward() const noexcept { return last_up_; }

  // How close to an alarm (alarm at threshold), in either direction with two_sided.
  [[nodiscard]] double evidence() const noexcept { return std::max(-cusum_, up_); }

 private:
  // Exponential moving mean and variance; exact running moments while young.
  void absorb(double x) {
    ++baseline_n_;
    ++rate_n_;
    const double rate = std::max(p_.baseline_rate, 1.0 / static_cast<double>(rate_n_));
    const double d = x - mean_;
    mean_ += rate * d;
    var_ = (1 - rate) * (var_ + rate * d * d);
  }

  Params p_;
  std::deque<double> held_;
  std::uint64_t baseline_n_ = 0;  // samples absorbed (arms the detector after `warmup`)
  std::uint64_t rate_n_ = 0;      // samples in the current running mean (restarted by rebase)
  double mean_ = 0, var_ = 0, cusum_ = 0, up_ = 0;
  bool last_up_ = false;
};

}  // namespace rag::agent
```

```cpp
// rag/agent/env.hpp — the agent's world: the Environment concept and two
// environments.
//
//   ExecutionEnv  sell an inventory over a fixed horizon. Trading fast costs
//                 market impact, trading slowly risks the price moving away,
//                 and a noisy signal predicts the next price move. The agent
//                 is never told what the signal means: discovering it is the
//                 point of the exercise.
//   ChainEnv      a corridor with a known optimal policy, for exact tests.
//
// An environment is the only part of the architecture that knows the task.
// The agent sees observations, an action count, rewards, and a feature view
// of each observation scaled into known ranges (kLo..kHi).
#pragma once

#include <algorithm>
#include <array>
#include <cmath>
#include <concepts>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

#include "rag/agent/rng.hpp"

namespace rag::agent {

using Action = std::uint32_t;

template <class Obs>
struct Step {
  Obs obs;        // next observation
  double reward;  // reward for the action just taken
  bool done;      // episode over (obs is then terminal and never acted on)
};

template <class E>
concept Environment = requires(E& e, const E& ce, Action a, Rng& rng, const typename E::Observation& o) {
  typename E::Observation;
  requires E::kNumActions >= 2;
  requires E::kStateDims >= 1;
  { E::kLo } -> std::convertible_to<std::array<double, E::kStateDims>>;
  { E::kHi } -> std::convertible_to<std::array<double, E::kStateDims>>;
  { e.reset(rng) } -> std::same_as<typename E::Observation>;
  { e.step(a, rng) } -> std::same_as<Step<typename E::Observation>>;
  { ce.features(o) } -> std::same_as<std::array<double, E::kStateDims>>;
};

// ------------------------------- ChainEnv ------------------------------------
// Positions 0..length-1, start at 0, goal at length-1. Action 0 = left,
// 1 = right. Every step costs -1; reaching the goal ends the episode, as does
// running out of steps. With slip > 0 the chosen move is reversed with that
// probability. Optimal return (slip 0): -(length - 1).
struct ChainParams {
  std::uint32_t length = 10;
  std::uint32_t max_steps = 60;
  double slip = 0.0;
};

class ChainEnv {
 public:
  struct Observation {
    std::uint32_t pos;
    std::uint32_t steps;
  };
  static constexpr std::size_t kNumActions = 2;
  static constexpr std::size_t kStateDims = 1;
  static constexpr std::array<double, 1> kLo{0.0}, kHi{1.0};

  explicit ChainEnv(ChainParams p = {}) : p_(p) {}

  Observation reset(Rng&) noexcept {
    obs_ = {0, 0};
    return obs_;
  }

  Step<Observation> step(Action a, Rng& rng) noexcept {
    bool right = a == 1;
    if (p_.slip > 0 && rng.uniform() < p_.slip) right = !right;
    if (right && obs_.pos + 1 < p_.length) ++obs_.pos;
    if (!right && obs_.pos > 0) --obs_.pos;
    ++obs_.steps;
    const bool done = obs_.pos + 1 == p_.length || obs_.steps >= p_.max_steps;
    return {obs_, -1.0, done};
  }

  std::array<double, 1> features(const Observation& o) const noexcept {
    return {static_cast<double>(o.pos) / static_cast<double>(p_.length - 1)};
  }

  [[nodiscard]] const ChainParams& params() const noexcept { return p_; }

 private:
  ChainParams p_;
  Observation obs_{};
};

// ----------------------------- ExecutionEnv ----------------------------------
// Liquidate `lots` over `horizon` steps. At each step t the agent sells q
// lots at the current price S minus temporary impact (average fill price
// S - impact * q, so the step costs impact * q^2), then the price moves:
//     dS = alpha * signal_t + noise_sd * N(0,1)
// and the signal evolves as an AR(1) with persistence signal_rho. Anything
// still held after the last step is dumped at the much worse terminal_impact.
//
// Reward is the change in mark-to-market wealth (cash + inventory * S), so an
// episode's total reward is exactly cash_final - lots * S_0: minus the
// implementation shortfall against the arrival price. Higher is better.
//
// The signal says where the price is going. Selling faster when it is
// negative and slower when it is positive beats TWAP (selling evenly), but
// only an agent that has learned what the signal means can do that.
struct ExecutionParams {
  std::uint32_t lots = 100;
  std::uint32_t horizon = 20;
  double impact = 0.01;           // eta: selling q lots in one step costs eta * q^impact_exponent
  double terminal_impact = 0.05;  // leftover inventory is dumped at cost terminal_impact * rem^2
  // Alternative market forms (defaults reproduce the quadratic model exactly).
  // Used to test agents that assume the quadratic form against markets that
  // don't follow it.
  double impact_exponent = 2.0;   // e.g. 1.5: "square-root" style impact per lot
  double fixed_cost = 0.0;        // charged for every step that sells anything (fees, spread)
  // Risk aversion (Almgren-Chriss style mean-variance execution): every step
  // the agent holds I' lots through a price move, its reward is reduced by
  // risk_aversion * noise_sd^2 * I'^2, the variance that holding adds to the
  // final cash. 0 = risk-neutral. The penalty is part of the reward only;
  // cash and price accounting are unchanged.
  double risk_aversion = 0.0;
  // Permanent impact: every lot sold lowers the price by this much for the
  // rest of the episode (after the sale itself executes), so the inventory
  // still held loses permanent_impact * q * I'. Agents that model only
  // temporary impact don't have a term for it.
  double permanent_impact = 0.0;
  double alpha = 1.0;             // E[next price move] = alpha * signal
  double signal_rho = 0.7;        // signal persistence per step
  double signal_sd = 0.1;         // stationary standard deviation of the signal
  double noise_sd = 0.05;         // unpredictable part of each price move
  double start_price = 100.0;
  // Action k sells sizes[k] x the TWAP rate (lots / horizon), capped by inventory.
  std::array<double, 5> sizes = {0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0};
};

struct ExecutionObs {
  std::uint32_t t;          // steps taken so far, 0..horizon-1 while live
  std::uint32_t inventory;  // lots still to sell
  double signal;            // predicts the price move after this step's trade
};

class ExecutionEnv {
 public:
  using Observation = ExecutionObs;
  static constexpr std::size_t kNumActions = 5;
  static constexpr std::size_t kStateDims = 3;
  static constexpr Action kTwapAction = 2;  // sizes[2] == 1.0
  // features(): time and inventory as fractions, signal in standard deviations.
  static constexpr std::array<double, 3> kLo{0.0, 0.0, -3.0}, kHi{1.0, 1.0, 3.0};

  explicit ExecutionEnv(ExecutionParams p = {}) : p_(p) {}

  Observation reset(Rng& rng) noexcept {
    t_ = 0;
    inventory_ = p_.lots;
    price_ = p_.start_price;
    cash_ = 0.0;
    signal_ = p_.signal_sd * rng.normal();  // drawn from the stationary distribution
    return obs();
  }

  // Lots action `a` sells from `inventory` (deterministic, used by the DP too).
  [[nodiscard]] std::uint32_t lots_for(Action a, std::uint32_t inventory) const noexcept {
    const double rate = static_cast<double>(p_.lots) / static_cast<double>(p_.horizon);
    const auto q = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(std::lround(p_.sizes[a] * rate));
    return std::min(q, inventory);
  }

  // Execution cost of selling q lots in one step (excluding the price move).
  [[nodiscard]] double trade_cost(std::uint32_t q) const noexcept {
    if (q == 0) return 0.0;
    const double dq = static_cast<double>(q);
    const double impact = p_.impact_exponent == 2.0 ? dq * dq : std::pow(dq, p_.impact_exponent);
    return p_.impact * impact + p_.fixed_cost;
  }
  // Risk penalty for holding `held` lots through one price move.
  [[nodiscard]] double holding_penalty(std::uint32_t held) const noexcept {
    const double h = static_cast<double>(held);
    return p_.risk_aversion * p_.noise_sd * p_.noise_sd * h * h;
  }
  [[nodiscard]] double dump_cost(std::uint32_t rem) const noexcept {
    if (rem == 0) return 0.0;
    const double dr = static_cast<double>(rem);
    return p_.terminal_impact * dr * dr + p_.fixed_cost;
  }

  Step<Observation> step(Action a, Rng& rng) noexcept {
    const std::uint32_t q = lots_for(a, inventory_);
    const double cost = trade_cost(q);
    cash_ += static_cast<double>(q) * price_ - cost;
    inventory_ -= q;
    last_move_ = 0.0;
    const double drop = p_.permanent_impact * static_cast<double>(q);
    price_ -= drop;
    double reward = -cost - drop * static_cast<double>(inventory_);
    ++t_;
    if (t_ >= p_.horizon) {  // last step: dump whatever is left
      const double dump = dump_cost(inventory_);
      cash_ += static_cast<double>(inventory_) * price_ - dump;
      reward -= dump;
      inventory_ = 0;
      return {obs(), reward, true};
    }
    // The price moves while the remaining inventory is held.
    const double move = p_.alpha * signal_ + p_.noise_sd * rng.normal();
    last_move_ = move;
    price_ += move;
    reward += static_cast<double>(inventory_) * move - holding_penalty(inventory_);
    signal_ = p_.signal_rho * signal_ + std::sqrt(1.0 - p_.signal_rho * p_.signal_rho) * p_.signal_sd * rng.normal();
    // Once flat, every later reward is exactly 0, so ending early changes nothing.
    return {obs(), reward, inventory_ == 0};
  }

  std::array<double, 3> features(const Observation& o) const noexcept {
    return {static_cast<double>(o.t) / static_cast<double>(p_.horizon),
            static_cast<double>(o.inventory) / static_cast<double>(p_.lots), o.signal / p_.signal_sd};
  }

  // Accounting (tests and reporting).
  [[nodiscard]] double price() const noexcept { return price_; }
  [[nodiscard]] double cash() const noexcept { return cash_; }
  [[nodiscard]] std::uint32_t inventory() const noexcept { return inventory_; }
  // The last step's price move (market data; 0 on the final step, which has none).
  [[nodiscard]] double last_move() const noexcept { return last_move_; }
  [[nodiscard]] const ExecutionParams& params() const noexcept { return p_; }

  // Change the market's dynamics mid-life (e.g. the signal's meaning flips),
  // to test whether a learning agent notices and adapts.
  void set_alpha(double a) noexcept { p_.alpha = a; }

 private:
  Observation obs() const noexcept { return {t_, inventory_, signal_}; }

  ExecutionParams p_;
  std::uint32_t t_ = 0, inventory_ = 0;
  double price_ = 0.0, cash_ = 0.0, signal_ = 0.0, last_move_ = 0.0;
};

static_assert(Environment<ChainEnv>);
static_assert(Environment<ExecutionEnv>);

}  // namespace rag::agent
```

```cpp
// rag/agent/evaluate.hpp — policy evaluation on common random numbers.
//
// evaluate() scores a policy on fixed scenarios; compare() scores two
// policies on the *same* scenarios and reports their paired difference.
// Episode returns here have a standard deviation (~55) much larger than the
// differences between good policies, so pairing is what makes comparisons
// precise. Used by the trainer (champions, drift confirmation, the baseline
// guard) and by the model-based agent's model check.
#pragma once

#include <algorithm>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <vector>

#include "rag/agent/env.hpp"
#include "rag/agent/rng.hpp"

namespace rag::agent {

struct EvalStats {
  double mean = 0;
  double std_error = 0;
  std::uint32_t episodes = 0;
};

// Run `episodes` greedy episodes of policy(obs) -> Action on copies of
// `proto`. Episode i always uses Rng(seed + i), so two policies evaluated
// with the same seed face exactly the same scenarios (common random numbers).
template <Environment Env, class Policy>
EvalStats evaluate(const Env& proto, Policy&& policy, std::uint32_t episodes, std::uint64_t seed) {
  double sum = 0, sum2 = 0;
  for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < episodes; ++i) {
    Env env = proto;
    Rng rng(seed + i);
    auto o = env.reset(rng);
    double total = 0;
    for (;;) {
      const auto st = env.step(policy(o), rng);
      total += st.reward;
      o = st.obs;
      if (st.done) break;
    }
    sum += total;
    sum2 += total * total;
  }
  EvalStats s;
  s.episodes = episodes;
  s.mean = episodes ? sum / episodes : 0;
  const double var = episodes > 1 ? std::max(0.0, (sum2 - episodes * s.mean * s.mean) / (episodes - 1)) : 0;
  s.std_error = episodes ? std::sqrt(var / episodes) : 0;
  return s;
}

// Mean per-episode difference policy_a - policy_b on the same scenarios.
// Pairing cancels the scenario-to-scenario noise both policies share, which
// usually dwarfs the difference between them.
template <Environment Env, class PolicyA, class PolicyB>
EvalStats compare(const Env& proto, PolicyA&& a, PolicyB&& b, std::uint32_t episodes, std::uint64_t seed) {
  double sum = 0, sum2 = 0;
  for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < episodes; ++i) {
    const double ra = evaluate(proto, a, 1, seed + i).mean;
    const double rb = evaluate(proto, b, 1, seed + i).mean;
    sum += ra - rb;
    sum2 += (ra - rb) * (ra - rb);
  }
  EvalStats s;
  s.episodes = episodes;
  s.mean = episodes ? sum / episodes : 0;
  const double var = episodes > 1 ? std::max(0.0, (sum2 - episodes * s.mean * s.mean) / (episodes - 1)) : 0;
  s.std_error = episodes ? std::sqrt(var / episodes) : 0;
  return s;
}

// Every episode's return, on the same scenarios as evaluate() (episode i
// uses Rng(seed + i)): for distributions, tails and paired analyses.
template <Environment Env, class Policy>
std::vector<double> episode_returns(const Env& proto, Policy&& policy, std::uint32_t episodes, std::uint64_t seed) {
  std::vector<double> out;
  out.reserve(episodes);
  for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < episodes; ++i) out.push_back(evaluate(proto, policy, 1, seed + i).mean);
  return out;
}

// Conditional value at risk: the mean of the worst `alpha` fraction of
// outcomes (alpha in (0, 1]; e.g. 0.05 = the worst 5%). At least one
// outcome is always included.
inline double cvar(std::vector<double> returns, double alpha) {
  if (returns.empty()) return 0;
  // alpha * n rounded down, with a relative tolerance: 0.29 * 100 is
  // 28.999999999999996 in floating point, and must count 29 outcomes.
  const auto want = static_cast<std::size_t>(alpha * static_cast<double>(returns.size()) * (1 + 1e-12));
  const std::size_t k = std::clamp<std::size_t>(want, 1, returns.size());
  std::nth_element(returns.begin(), returns.begin() + static_cast<std::ptrdiff_t>(k - 1), returns.end());
  std::sort(returns.begin(), returns.begin() + static_cast<std::ptrdiff_t>(k));
  double s = 0;
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < k; ++i) s += returns[i];
  return s / static_cast<double>(k);
}

// Percentile bootstrap confidence interval for the mean of `values`
// (e.g. one score per seed): resample with replacement `resamples` times.
struct Interval {
  double mean = 0, lo = 0, hi = 0;
};
inline Interval bootstrap_mean(const std::vector<double>& values, std::uint32_t resamples, std::uint64_t seed, double level = 0.95) {
  Interval out;
  if (values.empty() || resamples == 0) return out;
  const auto n = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(values.size());
  for (double v : values) out.mean += v / n;
  Rng rng(seed);
  std::vector<double> means(resamples);
  for (auto& m : means) {
    double s = 0;
    for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) s += values[rng.below(n)];
    m = s / n;
  }
  std::sort(means.begin(), means.end());
  const double tail = (1 - level) / 2;
  const auto at = [&](double q) { return means[std::min<std::size_t>(means.size() - 1, static_cast<std::size_t>(q * static_cast<double>(means.size())))]; };
  out.lo = at(tail);
  out.hi = at(1 - tail);
  return out;
}

}  // namespace rag::agent
```

```cpp
// rag/agent/execution_dp.hpp — the optimal policy for ExecutionEnv, solved
// exactly (up to grid resolution) by backward dynamic programming.
//
// This is the yardstick for the learning agent. "It learned something" is a
// weak claim; "it captures 80% of the improvement over TWAP that the optimal
// policy achieves" is a measurable one. The DP knows the model (alpha, rho,
// impact); the agent knows none of it and must learn from rewards alone.
//
// The state is (t, inventory, signal). Rewards are mark-to-market, so the
// price level never enters: the expected reward of selling q from inventory I
// with signal g is
//   -cost(q) - permanent*q*(I - q) + (I - q) * alpha * g - holding_penalty(I - q),
// plus the terminal dump cost on the last step. The next signal is
// rho*g + sqrt(1-rho^2)*sd*Z; the
// expectation over Z uses a 31-point quadrature, and V is linearly
// interpolated on a signal grid spanning +-4 standard deviations.
//
// Speed: on the grid, E[V(t+1, rem, g') | g_j] is the same linear map of the
// row V(t+1, rem, .) for every time step, inventory and action, so it's
// precomputed once as a banded matrix (quadrature weights x interpolation
// weights; ~45 nonzeros per row at the default parameters). The solve then
// costs one banded dot product per (t, rem, j) plus O(1) per action, instead
// of 31 interpolations per (t, inventory, j, action): 74 -> 3.5 ms at the
// 61-point grid. Off-grid queries (act, q_value) still use the quadrature
// directly.
#pragma once

#include <algorithm>
#include <array>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdint>
#include <limits>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

#include "rag/agent/env.hpp"

namespace rag::agent {

class ExecutionDP {
 public:
  static constexpr int kQuad = 31;

  explicit ExecutionDP(const ExecutionParams& p, std::uint32_t grid = 121, double grid_sds = 4.0)
      : ExecutionDP(p, cost_table(p, false), cost_table(p, true), grid, grid_sds) {}

  // Plan with arbitrary cost tables: trade_costs[q] for selling q lots in a
  // step, dump_costs[rem] for dumping rem lots at the end (both indexed
  // 0..lots). A model-based agent passes the costs it has learned.
  ExecutionDP(const ExecutionParams& p, std::vector<double> trade_costs, std::vector<double> dump_costs,
              std::uint32_t grid = 121, double grid_sds = 4.0)
      // The grid needs a positive width even without a signal (signal_sd 0):
      // a zero step made every lookup 0/0 and the whole table NaN.
      : env_(p), p_(p), m_(grid), lo_(-grid_sds * std::max(p.signal_sd, 1e-12)),
        step_(2.0 * grid_sds * std::max(p.signal_sd, 1e-12) / (grid - 1)),
        trade_cost_(std::move(trade_costs)), dump_cost_(std::move(dump_costs)) {
    if (trade_cost_.size() != p.lots + 1u || dump_cost_.size() != p.lots + 1u)
      throw std::invalid_argument("ExecutionDP: cost tables need lots + 1 entries");
    if (grid < 2) throw std::invalid_argument("ExecutionDP: the signal grid needs at least 2 points");
    // Quadrature for E[f(Z)], Z ~ N(0,1): evenly spaced nodes on [-4, 4],
    // weights proportional to the density, normalised to sum to 1.
    double total = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < kQuad; ++i) {
      nodes_[i] = -4.0 + 8.0 * i / (kQuad - 1);
      weights_[i] = std::exp(-0.5 * nodes_[i] * nodes_[i]);
      total += weights_[i];
    }
    for (auto& w : weights_) w /= total;
    innov_ = std::sqrt(1.0 - p.signal_rho * p.signal_rho) * p.signal_sd;
    build_expectation_band();

    v_.assign(std::size_t{p.horizon + 1} * (p.lots + 1) * m_, 0.0);
    std::vector<double> cont(std::size_t{p.lots + 1} * m_, 0.0);
    for (std::uint32_t t = p.horizon; t-- > 0;) {
      const bool last = t + 1 >= p.horizon;
      if (!last) continuation(v_, t + 1, cont);
      for (std::uint32_t inv = 0; inv <= p.lots; ++inv)
        for (std::uint32_t j = 0; j < m_; ++j) {
          double best = -std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity();
          for (Action a = 0; a < ExecutionEnv::kNumActions; ++a) best = std::max(best, q_grid(cont, last, inv, j, a));
          at(t, inv, j) = best;
        }
    }
  }

  // Expected reward-to-go of action a, then acting optimally.
  [[nodiscard]] double q_value(std::uint32_t t, std::uint32_t inv, double g, Action a) const noexcept {
    return q_from(v_, t, inv, g, a);
  }

  // Optimal expected reward-to-go from (t, inventory, signal).
  [[nodiscard]] double value(std::uint32_t t, std::uint32_t inv, double g) const noexcept { return value_from(v_, t, inv, g); }

  [[nodiscard]] const ExecutionParams& params() const noexcept { return p_; }

  // The optimal action (greedy on the exact Q-values, signal not rounded).
  [[nodiscard]] Action act(const ExecutionObs& o) const noexcept {
    Action best = 0;
    double bv = -std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity();
    for (Action a = 0; a < ExecutionEnv::kNumActions; ++a) {
      const double q = q_value(o.t, o.inventory, o.signal, a);
      if (q > bv) { bv = q; best = a; }
    }
    return best;
  }

  // Expected total reward of the optimal policy from the start state,
  // averaged over the stationary distribution of the first signal.
  [[nodiscard]] double expected_start_value() const noexcept { return start_value_from(v_); }

  // Expected total reward of an arbitrary policy (a function of the
  // observation) under this model, from the start state: backward induction
  // with the policy's action in place of the max. The policy is queried on
  // the signal grid. A model's predicted gain of A over B is
  // policy_value(A) - policy_value(B); comparing that with the gain measured
  // in the real world, paired, checks the model (E7).
  template <class Policy>
  [[nodiscard]] double policy_value(Policy&& policy) const {
    return evaluate_policy(std::forward<Policy>(policy)).start_value();
  }

  // The full value table of a fixed policy under this model: V^pi(t, inv, g)
  // and Q^pi(t, inv, g, a) = take a now, follow the policy afterwards. Used
  // by doubly robust off-policy evaluation (E10). Holds a pointer to this
  // DP, which must outlive it.
  class PolicyValues {
   public:
    [[nodiscard]] double value(std::uint32_t t, std::uint32_t inv, double g) const noexcept { return dp_->value_from(v_, t, inv, g); }
    [[nodiscard]] double q(std::uint32_t t, std::uint32_t inv, double g, Action a) const noexcept {
      return dp_->q_from(v_, t, inv, g, a);
    }
    [[nodiscard]] double start_value() const noexcept { return dp_->start_value_from(v_); }

   private:
    friend class ExecutionDP;
    PolicyValues(const ExecutionDP* dp, std::vector<double> v) : dp_(dp), v_(std::move(v)) {}
    const ExecutionDP* dp_;
    std::vector<double> v_;
  };

  template <class Policy>
  [[nodiscard]] PolicyValues evaluate_policy(Policy&& policy) const {
    std::vector<double> w(v_.size(), 0.0);
    std::vector<double> cont(std::size_t{p_.lots + 1} * m_, 0.0);
    for (std::uint32_t t = p_.horizon; t-- > 0;) {
      const bool last = t + 1 >= p_.horizon;
      if (!last) continuation(w, t + 1, cont);
      for (std::uint32_t inv = 1; inv <= p_.lots; ++inv)
        for (std::uint32_t j = 0; j < m_; ++j)
          w[index(t, inv, j)] = q_grid(cont, last, inv, j, policy(ExecutionObs{t, inv, lo_ + j * step_}));
    }
    return PolicyValues(this, std::move(w));
  }

 private:
  [[nodiscard]] std::size_t index(std::uint32_t t, std::uint32_t inv, std::uint32_t j) const noexcept {
    return (std::size_t{t} * (p_.lots + 1) + inv) * m_ + j;
  }

  // Precompute, for every grid point j, the weights that map a value row
  // V(.) on the grid to E[V(rho*g_j + innov*Z)] (quadrature x interpolation).
  void build_expectation_band() {
    band_start_.assign(m_, 0);
    band_len_.assign(m_, 0);
    band_offset_.assign(m_ + 1, 0);
    band_w_.clear();
    std::vector<double> row(m_);
    for (std::uint32_t j = 0; j < m_; ++j) {
      std::fill(row.begin(), row.end(), 0.0);
      const double g = lo_ + j * step_;
      for (int i = 0; i < kQuad; ++i) {
        const double x = std::clamp((p_.signal_rho * g + innov_ * nodes_[i] - lo_) / step_, 0.0, static_cast<double>(m_ - 1));
        const auto k = std::min(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(x), m_ - 2);
        const double f = x - k;
        row[k] += weights_[i] * (1 - f);
        row[k + 1] += weights_[i] * f;
      }
      std::uint32_t lo = 0, hi = m_;
      while (lo < hi && row[lo] == 0.0) ++lo;
      while (hi > lo && row[hi - 1] == 0.0) --hi;
      band_start_[j] = lo;
      band_len_[j] = hi - lo;
      band_offset_[j] = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(band_w_.size());
      band_w_.insert(band_w_.end(), row.begin() + lo, row.begin() + hi);
    }
    band_offset_[m_] = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(band_w_.size());
  }

  // cont[rem * m + j] = E[V(t1, rem, g') | g = g_j] for the table v.
  void continuation(const std::vector<double>& v, std::uint32_t t1, std::vector<double>& cont) const noexcept {
    for (std::uint32_t rem = 1; rem <= p_.lots; ++rem) {
      const double* row = &v[index(t1, rem, 0)];
      double* out = &cont[std::size_t{rem} * m_];
      for (std::uint32_t j = 0; j < m_; ++j) {
        const double* w = &band_w_[band_offset_[j]];
        const double* r = row + band_start_[j];
        double s = 0;
        for (std::uint32_t k = 0; k < band_len_[j]; ++k) s += w[k] * r[k];
        out[j] = s;
      }
    }
  }

  // Q-value at grid point j, given the precomputed continuation.
  [[nodiscard]] double q_grid(const std::vector<double>& cont, bool last, std::uint32_t inv, std::uint32_t j, Action a) const noexcept {
    const std::uint32_t q = env_.lots_for(a, inv);
    const std::uint32_t rem = inv - q;
    const double dr = rem;
    double r = -trade_cost_[q] - p_.permanent_impact * static_cast<double>(q) * dr;
    if (last) return r - dump_cost_[rem];
    if (rem == 0) return r;
    return r + dr * p_.alpha * (lo_ + j * step_) - env_.holding_penalty(rem) + cont[std::size_t{rem} * m_ + j];
  }

  // Q-value of action a, then following the values in table `v`.
  [[nodiscard]] double q_from(const std::vector<double>& v, std::uint32_t t, std::uint32_t inv, double g, Action a) const noexcept {
    const std::uint32_t q = env_.lots_for(a, inv);
    const std::uint32_t rem = inv - q;
    const double dr = rem;
    double r = -trade_cost_[q] - p_.permanent_impact * static_cast<double>(q) * dr;
    if (t + 1 >= p_.horizon) return r - dump_cost_[rem];
    if (rem == 0) return r;  // flat: the episode ends
    r += dr * p_.alpha * g - env_.holding_penalty(rem);
    double future = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < kQuad; ++i) future += weights_[i] * value_from(v, t + 1, rem, p_.signal_rho * g + innov_ * nodes_[i]);
    return r + future;
  }

  [[nodiscard]] double value_from(const std::vector<double>& v, std::uint32_t t, std::uint32_t inv, double g) const noexcept {
    if (t >= p_.horizon || inv == 0) return 0.0;
    const double x = std::clamp((g - lo_) / step_, 0.0, static_cast<double>(m_ - 1));
    const auto j = std::min(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(x), m_ - 2);
    const double f = x - j;
    return (1 - f) * v[index(t, inv, j)] + f * v[index(t, inv, j + 1)];
  }

  [[nodiscard]] double start_value_from(const std::vector<double>& v) const noexcept {
    double s = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < kQuad; ++i) s += weights_[i] * value_from(v, 0, p_.lots, p_.signal_sd * nodes_[i]);
    return s;
  }

  double& at(std::uint32_t t, std::uint32_t inv, std::uint32_t j) noexcept { return v_[index(t, inv, j)]; }

  static std::vector<double> cost_table(const ExecutionParams& p, bool dump) {
    const ExecutionEnv env(p);
    std::vector<double> t(p.lots + 1);
    for (std::uint32_t q = 0; q <= p.lots; ++q) t[q] = dump ? env.dump_cost(q) : env.trade_cost(q);
    return t;
  }

  ExecutionEnv env_;  // only for lots_for()
  ExecutionParams p_;
  std::uint32_t m_;
  double lo_, step_, innov_ = 0;
  std::array<double, kQuad> nodes_{}, weights_{};
  std::vector<double> trade_cost_, dump_cost_;  // [lots]
  std::vector<double> v_;  // V[t][inventory][signal grid]
  // Banded expectation operator on the grid (see build_expectation_band).
  std::vector<std::uint32_t> band_start_, band_len_, band_offset_;
  std::vector<double> band_w_;
};

}  // namespace rag::agent
```

```cpp
// rag/agent/features.hpp — perception: turning an observation into features
// a learner can generalize over.
//
// Two encoders, matching the two learners:
//
//   TileCoder            sparse, for the parametric learner (TileQ). Several
//                        overlapping grids ("tilings"), each offset by a
//                        fraction of a cell; a point activates exactly one
//                        cell per tiling. Nearby states share most active
//                        cells, so what is learned in one state spreads to its
//                        neighbours, by an amount that shrinks with distance.
//
//   RandomFourierEncoder dense, for the episodic memory. Maps a state into a
//                        D-dimensional unit vector whose dot products
//                        approximate a Gaussian similarity between states
//                        (Rahimi & Recht, 2007). Then "recall similar past
//                        situations" is exactly the nearest-neighbour search
//                        the RAG engine runs over text embeddings, and it
//                        reuses the same SIMD kernels and top-K selection.
#pragma once

#include <algorithm>
#include <array>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <numbers>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <vector>

#include "rag/agent/rng.hpp"
#include "rag/common.hpp"
#include "rag/simd.hpp"

namespace rag::agent {

inline constexpr std::uint32_t kMaxTilings = 32;

template <std::size_t Dims>
class TileCoder {
 public:
  TileCoder(const std::array<double, Dims>& lo, const std::array<double, Dims>& hi,
            const std::array<std::uint32_t, Dims>& bins, std::uint32_t tilings)
      : lo_(lo), bins_(bins), tilings_(tilings) {
    if (tilings == 0 || tilings > kMaxTilings) throw std::invalid_argument("TileCoder: tilings must be in [1, 32]");
    cells_ = 1;
    for (std::size_t d = 0; d < Dims; ++d) {
      if (bins[d] == 0 || !(hi[d] > lo[d])) throw std::invalid_argument("TileCoder: need bins > 0 and hi > lo");
      scale_[d] = bins[d] / (hi[d] - lo[d]);
      stride_[d] = cells_;
      cells_ *= bins[d] + 1;  // +1: the offset tilings overhang the range by one cell
    }
    // Asymmetric offsets (Sutton & Barto, 9.5.4): tiling k is shifted by
    // k * (1, 3, 5, ...) / tilings of a cell, which avoids the diagonal
    // artefacts of shifting every dimension by the same amount.
    for (std::uint32_t k = 0; k < tilings; ++k)
      for (std::size_t d = 0; d < Dims; ++d)
        offset_[k][d] = std::fmod(static_cast<double>(k) * static_cast<double>(2 * d + 1) / tilings, 1.0);
  }

  [[nodiscard]] std::uint32_t tilings() const noexcept { return tilings_; }
  [[nodiscard]] std::size_t size() const noexcept { return std::size_t{cells_} * tilings_; }

  // Writes one active feature index per tiling into idx[0..tilings).
  // Inputs outside [lo, hi] are clamped onto the boundary cells.
  void encode(const std::array<double, Dims>& x, std::uint32_t* idx) const noexcept {
    std::array<double, Dims> u;
    for (std::size_t d = 0; d < Dims; ++d)
      u[d] = std::clamp((x[d] - lo_[d]) * scale_[d], 0.0, static_cast<double>(bins_[d]));
    for (std::uint32_t k = 0; k < tilings_; ++k) {
      std::uint32_t flat = 0;
      for (std::size_t d = 0; d < Dims; ++d) {
        const auto c = std::min(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(u[d] + offset_[k][d]), bins_[d]);
        flat += c * stride_[d];
      }
      idx[k] = k * cells_ + flat;
    }
  }

 private:
  std::array<double, Dims> lo_, scale_{};
  std::array<std::uint32_t, Dims> bins_, stride_{};
  std::uint32_t tilings_, cells_ = 1;
  std::array<std::array<double, Dims>, kMaxTilings> offset_{};
};

template <std::size_t Dims, std::size_t D>
  requires ValidDim<D>
class RandomFourierEncoder {
 public:
  static constexpr std::size_t kDim = D;

  // `width[d]`: the distance along dimension d at which similarity has fallen
  // to exp(-1/2) ~ 0.61 (the kernel's length scale).
  RandomFourierEncoder(const std::array<double, Dims>& width, std::uint64_t seed) {
    Rng rng(seed);
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < D; ++i) {
      for (std::size_t d = 0; d < Dims; ++d) {
        if (!(width[d] > 0)) throw std::invalid_argument("RandomFourierEncoder: widths must be > 0");
        w_[i][d] = rng.normal() / width[d];
      }
      b_[i] = 2.0 * std::numbers::pi * rng.uniform();
    }
  }

  // Writes a unit-length embedding of x into out[0..D).
  void encode(const std::array<double, Dims>& x, float* out) const noexcept {
    double norm = 0;
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < D; ++i) {
      double p = b_[i];
      for (std::size_t d = 0; d < Dims; ++d) p += w_[i][d] * x[d];
      const double z = std::cos(p);
      out[i] = static_cast<float>(z);
      norm += z * z;
    }
    const auto inv = static_cast<float>(norm > 0 ? 1.0 / std::sqrt(norm) : 0.0);
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < D; ++i) out[i] *= inv;
  }

 private:
  std::array<std::array<double, Dims>, D> w_{};
  std::array<double, D> b_{};
};

}  // namespace rag::agent
```

```cpp
// rag/agent/learners.hpp — memory and learning.
//
//   TileQ          parametric value learner: Q(s, a) is a sum of one weight
//                  per active tile. Updated by temporal-difference (TD)
//                  learning, i.e. each experience nudges the weights toward
//                  "reward + value of where I ended up". Slow to learn,
//                  generalizes smoothly, constant memory.
//   ReplayBuffer   fixed-capacity ring of past transitions. Each is re-learned
//                  from many times, which squeezes far more out of every
//                  (expensive) interaction with the world.
//   EpisodicMemory instance-based learner: stores embeddings of situations it
//                  has been in, with the returns that followed each action, and
//                  estimates Q(s, a) by averaging its k most similar memories
//                  (model-free episodic control, Blundell et al. 2016). Learns
//                  from a single good episode, but generalizes only as far as
//                  its similarity measure reaches.
//
// Latency notes: weights are stored action-minor ([feature][action]), so
// reading all of a state's Q-values touches one cache line per tiling. The
// episodic memory runs ONE nearest-neighbour search per decision (each slot
// carries values for every action) with the SIMD kernels of rag/simd.hpp.
#pragma once

#include <algorithm>
#include <array>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <limits>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <vector>

#include "rag/agent/env.hpp"
#include "rag/agent/features.hpp"
#include "rag/agent/rng.hpp"
#include "rag/common.hpp"
#include "rag/simd.hpp"
#include "rag/topk.hpp"

namespace rag::agent {

// -------------------------------- TileQ --------------------------------------
class TileQ {
 public:
  TileQ() = default;
  TileQ(std::size_t features, std::uint32_t tilings, std::uint32_t actions, double alpha, double init_q = 0.0)
      : tilings_(tilings), actions_(actions), step_(alpha / tilings),
        w_(features * actions, init_q / tilings) {}

  // out[a] = Q(s, a) for the state whose active tiles are idx[0..tilings).
  void q_values(const std::uint32_t* idx, double* out) const noexcept {
    for (std::uint32_t a = 0; a < actions_; ++a) out[a] = 0.0;
    for (std::uint32_t k = 0; k < tilings_; ++k) {
      const double* w = w_.data() + std::size_t{idx[k]} * actions_;
      for (std::uint32_t a = 0; a < actions_; ++a) out[a] += w[a];
    }
  }

  [[nodiscard]] double q(const std::uint32_t* idx, Action a) const noexcept {
    double s = 0;
    for (std::uint32_t k = 0; k < tilings_; ++k) s += w_[std::size_t{idx[k]} * actions_ + a];
    return s;
  }

  // Move Q(s, a) toward `target` by the step size; returns the TD error.
  double update(const std::uint32_t* idx, Action a, double target) noexcept {
    const double err = target - q(idx, a);
    const double d = step_ * err;
    for (std::uint32_t k = 0; k < tilings_; ++k) w_[std::size_t{idx[k]} * actions_ + a] += d;
    return err;
  }

  // this = (1 - weight) * this + weight * other, for iterate (Polyak) averaging.
  void blend(const TileQ& other, double weight) noexcept {
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < w_.size() && i < other.w_.size(); ++i) w_[i] += weight * (other.w_[i] - w_[i]);
  }

  // Change the step size (the agent anneals it as experience accumulates).
  void set_alpha(double alpha) noexcept { step_ = alpha / tilings_; }
  [[nodiscard]] double alpha() const noexcept { return step_ * tilings_; }

  [[nodiscard]] std::uint32_t actions() const noexcept { return actions_; }
  [[nodiscard]] const std::vector<double>& weights() const noexcept { return w_; }

 private:
  std::uint32_t tilings_ = 0, actions_ = 0;
  double step_ = 0;
  std::vector<double> w_;  // [feature][action]
};

// ------------------------------ ReplayBuffer ---------------------------------
struct Transition {
  std::array<std::uint32_t, kMaxTilings> s;     // active tiles of the state
  std::array<std::uint32_t, kMaxTilings> next;  // ... and of the state `steps` steps later
  float reward;                                 // discounted sum of the `steps` rewards in between
  std::uint16_t action;
  std::uint8_t steps = 1;                       // n of the n-step return (bootstrap discount gamma^steps)
  bool done;                                    // the episode ended within those steps: no bootstrap
};

class ReplayBuffer {
 public:
  explicit ReplayBuffer(std::size_t capacity = 0) : buf_(capacity) {}

  // Overwrites the oldest transition once full.
  void push(const Transition& t) noexcept {
    if (buf_.empty()) return;
    buf_[head_] = t;
    head_ = (head_ + 1) % buf_.size();
    size_ = std::min(size_ + 1, buf_.size());
  }

  [[nodiscard]] const Transition& sample(Rng& rng) const noexcept {
    return buf_[rng.below(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(size_))];
  }

  void clear() noexcept { head_ = size_ = 0; }

  [[nodiscard]] std::size_t size() const noexcept { return size_; }
  [[nodiscard]] std::size_t capacity() const noexcept { return buf_.size(); }
  [[nodiscard]] const Transition& newest() const noexcept { return buf_[(head_ + buf_.size() - 1) % buf_.size()]; }

 private:
  std::vector<Transition> buf_;
  std::size_t head_ = 0, size_ = 0;
};

// ----------------------------- EpisodicMemory --------------------------------
struct EpisodicParams {
  std::uint32_t capacity = 4096;  // slots; least recently used is evicted when full
  std::uint32_t neighbors = 8;    // k for the k-NN estimate
  float same_situation = 0.97f;   // cosine above which a new memory updates an old slot
  double learning_rate = 0.2;     // EMA step for updating a slot's value
};

template <std::size_t D, std::size_t A>
  requires ValidDim<D>
class EpisodicMemory {
 public:
  static constexpr std::uint32_t kMaxNeighbors = 32;

  explicit EpisodicMemory(const EpisodicParams& p = {})
      : p_(p), keys_(make_aligned_array<float>(std::size_t{std::max(p.capacity, 1u)} * D, Init::Lazy)),
        slots_(std::max(p.capacity, 1u)) {
    if (p.neighbors == 0 || p.neighbors > kMaxNeighbors) throw std::invalid_argument("EpisodicParams: neighbors in [1, 32]");
  }

  EpisodicMemory(const EpisodicMemory& o) : p_(o.p_), keys_(make_aligned_array<float>(std::size_t{std::max(o.p_.capacity, 1u)} * D, Init::Lazy)),
                                            slots_(o.slots_), size_(o.size_), tick_(o.tick_) {
    std::copy_n(o.keys_.get(), std::size_t{size_} * D, keys_.get());
  }
  EpisodicMemory& operator=(const EpisodicMemory& o) {
    if (this != &o) {
      EpisodicMemory tmp(o);
      std::swap(p_, tmp.p_);
      std::swap(keys_, tmp.keys_);
      std::swap(slots_, tmp.slots_);
      size_ = tmp.size_;
      tick_ = tmp.tick_;
    }
    return *this;
  }
  EpisodicMemory(EpisodicMemory&&) noexcept = default;
  EpisodicMemory& operator=(EpisodicMemory&&) noexcept = default;

  // Q-value estimates for every action: the similarity-weighted mean of the
  // values the k most similar memories hold for that action. known[a] is
  // false when none of them has ever tried a (the caller decides what an
  // unknown action is worth; optimism drives exploration).
  void estimate(const float* key, double* out, bool* known) const noexcept {
    TopK<kMaxNeighbors> nn(p_.neighbors);
    search(key, nn);
    std::array<double, A> sum{}, wsum{};
    for (const Hit& h : nn.sorted()) {
      const Slot& s = slots_[h.id];
      const double w = std::max(1e-3, static_cast<double>(h.score));  // similarity weight
      for (std::size_t a = 0; a < A; ++a)
        if (s.visits[a]) { sum[a] += w * s.value[a]; wsum[a] += w; }
    }
    for (std::size_t a = 0; a < A; ++a) {
      known[a] = wsum[a] > 0;
      out[a] = known[a] ? sum[a] / wsum[a] : 0.0;
    }
  }

  // Remember that taking `a` in situation `key` led to return `g`. Updates
  // the nearest slot if it is the same situation, else stores a new one.
  void write(const float* key, Action a, double g) {
    ++tick_;
    TopK<1> nn(1);
    search(key, nn);
    const auto best = nn.sorted();
    if (!best.empty() && best[0].score >= p_.same_situation) {
      Slot& s = slots_[best[0].id];
      s.value[a] = s.visits[a] ? s.value[a] + p_.learning_rate * (g - s.value[a]) : g;
      ++s.visits[a];
      s.last_used = tick_;
      return;
    }
    std::uint32_t slot;
    if (size_ < slots_.size()) {
      slot = size_++;
    } else {  // full: evict the least recently used slot
      slot = 0;
      for (std::uint32_t i = 1; i < size_; ++i)
        if (slots_[i].last_used < slots_[slot].last_used) slot = i;
    }
    std::copy_n(key, D, keys_.get() + std::size_t{slot} * D);
    slots_[slot] = Slot{};
    slots_[slot].value[a] = g;
    slots_[slot].visits[a] = 1;
    slots_[slot].last_used = tick_;
  }

  [[nodiscard]] std::uint32_t size() const noexcept { return size_; }
  [[nodiscard]] std::uint32_t capacity() const noexcept { return static_cast<std::uint32_t>(slots_.size()); }

 private:
  struct Slot {
    std::array<double, A> value{};
    std::array<std::uint32_t, A> visits{};
    std::uint64_t last_used = 0;
  };

  template <class TK>
  void search(const float* key, TK& out) const noexcept {
    std::uint32_t i = 0;
    float s[4];
    for (; i + 4 <= size_; i += 4) {
      simd::dot4(key, keys_.get() + std::size_t{i} * D, D, D, s);
      out.push(s[0], i); out.push(s[1], i + 1); out.push(s[2], i + 2); out.push(s[3], i + 3);
    }
    for (; i < size_; ++i) out.push(simd::dot1(key, keys_.get() + std::size_t{i} * D, D), i);
  }

  EpisodicParams p_;
  AlignedArray<float> keys_;  // [slot][D], unit vectors
  std::vector<Slot> slots_;
  std::uint32_t size_ = 0;
  std::uint64_t tick_ = 0;
};

}  // namespace rag::agent
```
