```cpp
// rag/agent/market_making.hpp — a second task for the same agent: market
// making, with its exact optimum.
//
// Each step the agent quotes a bid at mid - d_b and an ask at mid + d_a, with
// d_b and d_a chosen from three distances (9 actions). Each side fills with
// probability fill_rate * exp(-decay * d): a wider quote earns more per fill
// but fills less often. A bid fill buys one unit (+1 inventory, earning d_b
// against the mid), an ask fill sells one (-1, earning d_a). Then the mid
// moves by volatility * N(0,1). Inventory is capped at +-max_inventory (the
// side that would breach the cap doesn't fill).
//
// Reward is the change in mark-to-market wealth, minus a risk penalty
// risk_aversion * volatility^2 * q^2 on the inventory carried through each
// price move; on the last step the inventory is liquidated at
// terminal_penalty * q^2. With risk_aversion = 0, an episode's total reward
// is exactly the final cash (the accounting identity the tests check).
//
// What makes it interesting: the risk-neutral spread-maximizing quote is the
// same on both sides, but holding inventory is penalized, so the optimal
// policy *skews*: when long it quotes a tighter ask (to sell) and a wider bid
// (to stop buying), and the other way round when short (the discrete-time
// version of Avellaneda & Stoikov, 2008). The agent sees only (t, q) and
// rewards, and has to discover the skew.
//
// MarketMakingDP solves it exactly: the state space is (t, q), and the price
// noise has mean zero, so the expected reward of a quote pair depends only
// on q.
#pragma once

#include <algorithm>
#include <array>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdint>
#include <limits>
#include <memory>
#include <vector>

#include "rag/agent/env.hpp"
#include "rag/agent/rng.hpp"

namespace rag::agent {

struct MarketMakingParams {
  std::uint32_t horizon = 50;
  std::int32_t max_inventory = 10;
  std::array<double, 3> distances = {0.5, 1.0, 2.0};  // quote distance from the mid
  double fill_rate = 0.9;          // fill probability at distance 0
  double decay = 1.0;              // P(fill) = fill_rate * exp(-decay * d)
  double volatility = 1.0;         // mid-price move per step: volatility * N(0,1)
  double risk_aversion = 0.05;     // per-step penalty risk_aversion * volatility^2 * q^2
  double terminal_penalty = 0.5;   // liquidation cost terminal_penalty * q^2 at the end
  // Optional fill curve: fill probability per distance index. Entries < 0
  // fall back to fill_rate * exp(-decay * d). Lets a market have a curve
  // that isn't exponential (E15).
  std::array<double, 3> fill_probs = {-1.0, -1.0, -1.0};
};

struct MarketMakingObs {
  std::uint32_t t;   // steps taken so far
  std::int32_t q;    // inventory (+ long, - short)
};

class MarketMakingEnv {
 public:
  using Observation = MarketMakingObs;
  static constexpr std::size_t kNumActions = 9;  // bid distance index * 3 + ask distance index
  static constexpr std::size_t kStateDims = 2;
  static constexpr std::array<double, 2> kLo{0.0, -1.0}, kHi{1.0, 1.0};
  static constexpr Action kSymmetricAction = 4;  // both sides at distances[1]

  explicit MarketMakingEnv(MarketMakingParams p = {}) : p_(p) {}

  [[nodiscard]] static constexpr Action action(std::uint32_t bid, std::uint32_t ask) noexcept { return bid * 3 + ask; }
  [[nodiscard]] double bid_distance(Action a) const noexcept { return p_.distances[a / 3]; }
  [[nodiscard]] double ask_distance(Action a) const noexcept { return p_.distances[a % 3]; }
  [[nodiscard]] double fill_probability(double d) const noexcept { return p_.fill_rate * std::exp(-p_.decay * d); }
  // Fill probability at distance index k (0-2), honouring fill_probs.
  [[nodiscard]] double fill_probability_at(std::uint32_t k) const noexcept {
    return p_.fill_probs[k] >= 0 ? p_.fill_probs[k] : fill_probability(p_.distances[k]);
  }
  // Probability that the bid (ask) fills from inventory q: 0 at the cap.
  [[nodiscard]] double bid_fill(Action a, std::int32_t q) const noexcept {
    return q >= p_.max_inventory ? 0.0 : fill_probability_at(a / 3);
  }
  [[nodiscard]] double ask_fill(Action a, std::int32_t q) const noexcept {
    return q <= -p_.max_inventory ? 0.0 : fill_probability_at(a % 3);
  }
  [[nodiscard]] double risk_penalty(std::int32_t q) const noexcept {
    return p_.risk_aversion * p_.volatility * p_.volatility * static_cast<double>(q) * q;
  }

  Observation reset(Rng&) noexcept {
    t_ = 0;
    q_ = 0;
    mid_ = 100.0;
    cash_ = 0.0;
    return {t_, q_};
  }

  Step<Observation> step(Action a, Rng& rng) noexcept {
    const bool bought = rng.uniform() < bid_fill(a, q_);
    const bool sold = rng.uniform() < ask_fill(a, q_);
    last_bought_ = bought;
    last_sold_ = sold;
    last_move_ = 0.0;
    double reward = 0;
    if (bought) {
      cash_ -= mid_ - bid_distance(a);
      reward += bid_distance(a);  // bought below the mid: marked at the mid
      ++q_;
    }
    if (sold) {
      cash_ += mid_ + ask_distance(a);
      reward += ask_distance(a);
      --q_;
    }
    ++t_;
    if (t_ >= p_.horizon) {  // liquidate at the mid, paying the terminal penalty
      const double cost = p_.terminal_penalty * static_cast<double>(q_) * q_;
      cash_ += q_ * mid_ - cost;
      reward -= cost;
      q_ = 0;
      return {{t_, q_}, reward, true};
    }
    const double move = p_.volatility * rng.normal();
    last_move_ = move;
    mid_ += move;
    reward += q_ * move - risk_penalty(q_);
    return {{t_, q_}, reward, false};
  }

  std::array<double, 2> features(const Observation& o) const noexcept {
    return {static_cast<double>(o.t) / static_cast<double>(p_.horizon), static_cast<double>(o.q) / p_.max_inventory};
  }

  [[nodiscard]] double cash() const noexcept { return cash_; }
  // What a market maker observes after a step besides its reward: its own
  // fills (execution reports) and the mid-price move (market data).
  [[nodiscard]] bool last_bought() const noexcept { return last_bought_; }
  [[nodiscard]] bool last_sold() const noexcept { return last_sold_; }
  [[nodiscard]] double last_mid_move() const noexcept { return last_move_; }
  [[nodiscard]] std::int32_t inventory() const noexcept { return q_; }
  [[nodiscard]] const MarketMakingParams& params() const noexcept { return p_; }

  // Change the market mid-life (a volatility regime switch), to test whether
  // a learning agent notices and adapts (E13).
  void set_volatility(double v) noexcept { p_.volatility = v; }
  void set_decay(double d) noexcept { p_.decay = d; }  // book depth: how fast fills fall off with distance

 private:
  MarketMakingParams p_;
  std::uint32_t t_ = 0;
  std::int32_t q_ = 0;
  double mid_ = 100.0, cash_ = 0.0;
  bool last_bought_ = false, last_sold_ = false;
  double last_move_ = 0.0;
};

static_assert(Environment<MarketMakingEnv>);

// Exact optimum by backward induction over (t, q): four fill outcomes per
// quote pair, each with its spread earned, risk penalty and continuation.
class MarketMakingDP {
 public:
  explicit MarketMakingDP(const MarketMakingParams& p) : env_(p), p_(p), width_(2 * p.max_inventory + 1) {
    v_.assign(std::size_t{p.horizon + 1} * width_, 0.0);
    for (std::uint32_t t = p.horizon; t-- > 0;)
      for (std::int32_t q = -p.max_inventory; q <= p.max_inventory; ++q) {
        double best = -std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity();
        for (Action a = 0; a < MarketMakingEnv::kNumActions; ++a) best = std::max(best, q_value(t, q, a));
        v_[idx(t, q)] = best;
      }
  }

  // Expected reward-to-go of quoting `a` at (t, q), then acting optimally.
  [[nodiscard]] double q_value(std::uint32_t t, std::int32_t q, Action a) const noexcept {
    const double pb = env_.bid_fill(a, q), pa = env_.ask_fill(a, q);
    const double db = env_.bid_distance(a), da = env_.ask_distance(a);
    const bool last = t + 1 >= p_.horizon;
    auto after = [&](std::int32_t q2) {
      return last ? -p_.terminal_penalty * static_cast<double>(q2) * q2 : -env_.risk_penalty(q2) + v_[idx(t + 1, q2)];
    };
    return (1 - pb) * (1 - pa) * after(q) + pb * (1 - pa) * (db + after(q + 1)) + (1 - pb) * pa * (da + after(q - 1)) +
           pb * pa * (db + da + after(q));
  }

  [[nodiscard]] double value(std::uint32_t t, std::int32_t q) const noexcept { return t >= p_.horizon ? 0.0 : v_[idx(t, q)]; }

  [[nodiscard]] Action act(const MarketMakingObs& o) const noexcept {
    Action best = 0;
    for (Action a = 1; a < MarketMakingEnv::kNumActions; ++a)
      if (q_value(o.t, o.q, a) > q_value(o.t, o.q, best)) best = a;
    return best;
  }

  [[nodiscard]] double expected_start_value() const noexcept { return value(0, 0); }

  // Exact value of any policy of (t, q), from the start.
  template <class Policy>
  [[nodiscard]] double policy_value(Policy&& policy) const {
    MarketMakingDP copy = *this;
    for (std::uint32_t t = p_.horizon; t-- > 0;)
      for (std::int32_t q = -p_.max_inventory; q <= p_.max_inventory; ++q)
        copy.v_[idx(t, q)] = copy.q_value(t, q, policy(MarketMakingObs{t, q}));
    return copy.value(0, 0);
  }

 private:
  [[nodiscard]] std::size_t idx(std::uint32_t t, std::int32_t q) const noexcept {
    return std::size_t{t} * width_ + static_cast<std::size_t>(q + p_.max_inventory);
  }

  MarketMakingEnv env_;
  MarketMakingParams p_;
  std::uint32_t width_;
  std::vector<double> v_;  // V[t][q + max_inventory]
};

// A model-based market maker: it knows its own objective (risk penalty,
// liquidation penalty, inventory cap, quote distances) but not the market.
// It estimates each distance's fill probability by counting fills (a
// Beta(1, 1) prior, pooled over bid and ask) and the volatility from the
// observed mid moves, then plans with MarketMakingDP on the estimates. The
// fill model is non-parametric over the three distances, so any fill curve
// is inside its model class. E15.
class ModelBasedMarketMaker {
 public:
  struct Config {
    std::uint32_t explore_episodes = 3;  // random quotes first: every distance gets tried
    double eps = 0.01;                   // exploration after that
    std::uint32_t replan_every = 5;      // episodes between re-plans, doubling up to replan_max_gap
    std::uint32_t replan_max_gap = 200;
    std::uint64_t seed = 1;
  };

  ModelBasedMarketMaker(const MarketMakingParams& objective, Config cfg)
      : objective_(objective), cfg_(cfg), rng_(cfg.seed), gap_(cfg.replan_every) {}

  Action act(const MarketMakingObs& o, bool explore) {
    // Greedy without a plan yet: symmetric quotes, without touching the RNG
    // (greedy evaluation must not change what training explores next).
    if (!plan_ && !explore) return MarketMakingEnv::kSymmetricAction;
    if (!plan_ || (explore && (episodes_ < cfg_.explore_episodes || rng_.uniform() < cfg_.eps)))
      return rng_.below(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(MarketMakingEnv::kNumActions));
    return plan_->act(o);
  }

  // One step's evidence: which quotes could fill (not at the cap), which did,
  // and the mid move (none on the last step).
  void observe(const MarketMakingObs& before, Action a, bool bought, bool sold, double mid_move, bool last) {
    const std::int32_t cap = objective_.max_inventory;
    if (before.q < cap) {
      attempts_[a / 3] += 1;
      fills_[a / 3] += bought ? 1 : 0;
    }
    if (before.q > -cap) {
      attempts_[a % 3] += 1;
      fills_[a % 3] += sold ? 1 : 0;
    }
    if (!last) {
      move2_ += mid_move * mid_move;
      moves_ += 1;
    }
  }

  void end_episode() {
    ++episodes_;
    // The gap doubles after each *re*-plan, so the first re-plan comes
    // replan_every episodes after the first plan (bug: it came 2x later).
    if (episodes_ >= cfg_.explore_episodes && (!plan_ || episodes_ - last_plan_ >= gap_)) {
      const bool first = !plan_;
      replan();
      if (!first) gap_ = std::min(gap_ * 2, cfg_.replan_max_gap);
    }
  }

  void replan() {
    MarketMakingParams p = objective_;
    for (std::uint32_t k = 0; k < 3; ++k) p.fill_probs[k] = estimated_fill(k);
    p.volatility = estimated_volatility();
    plan_ = std::make_unique<MarketMakingDP>(p);
    last_plan_ = episodes_;
  }

  [[nodiscard]] double estimated_fill(std::uint32_t k) const noexcept { return (fills_[k] + 1.0) / (attempts_[k] + 2.0); }
  [[nodiscard]] double estimated_volatility() const noexcept { return moves_ > 0 ? std::sqrt(move2_ / moves_) : 1.0; }
  [[nodiscard]] bool has_plan() const noexcept { return plan_ != nullptr; }
  [[nodiscard]] std::uint64_t episodes() const noexcept { return episodes_; }

 private:
  MarketMakingParams objective_;
  Config cfg_;
  Rng rng_;
  std::unique_ptr<MarketMakingDP> plan_;
  std::array<double, 3> fills_{}, attempts_{};
  double move2_ = 0, moves_ = 0;
  std::uint64_t episodes_ = 0, last_plan_ = 0;
  std::uint32_t gap_;
};

// Run `episodes` online episodes of the model-based market maker; returns
// the total reward per episode.
inline std::vector<double> train_model_based(ModelBasedMarketMaker& agent, MarketMakingEnv& env, std::uint32_t episodes, Rng& rng) {
  std::vector<double> returns;
  returns.reserve(episodes);
  for (std::uint32_t e = 0; e < episodes; ++e) {
    auto o = env.reset(rng);
    double total = 0;
    for (;;) {
      const Action a = agent.act(o, true);
      const auto st = env.step(a, rng);
      agent.observe(o, a, env.last_bought(), env.last_sold(), env.last_mid_move(), st.done);
      total += st.reward;
      o = st.obs;
      if (st.done) break;
    }
    agent.end_episode();
    returns.push_back(total);
  }
  return returns;
}

}  // namespace rag::agent
```

```cpp
// rag/agent/mlp.hpp — a small multilayer perceptron with backpropagation and
// Adam, written from scratch (no ML library): the neural alternative to tile
// coding for value functions (E16).
//
//   sizes = {in, h1, ..., out}; ReLU on hidden layers, linear output.
//   He-uniform initialization from the project's seeded Rng, so training is
//   reproducible bit for bit.
//
// Training is per sample: accumulate() adds the gradient of
// 0.5 * (out[k] - target)^2 for one output k (the action taken, as in
// Q-learning), and step() applies the averaged gradient with Adam and clears
// it. forward() is const and uses caller-provided scratch, so a target
// network can be a plain copy evaluated alongside.
#pragma once

#include <algorithm>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstring>
#include <filesystem>
#include <vector>

#include "rag/io.hpp"

#include "rag/agent/rng.hpp"

namespace rag::agent {

class Mlp {
 public:
  Mlp() = default;
  Mlp(std::vector<std::uint32_t> sizes, Rng& rng) : sizes_(std::move(sizes)) {
    std::size_t n = 0, units = 0;
    for (std::size_t l = 0; l + 1 < sizes_.size(); ++l) n += std::size_t{sizes_[l] + 1} * sizes_[l + 1];
    for (auto s : sizes_) units += s;
    w_.resize(n);
    g_.assign(n, 0.0);
    m_.assign(n, 0.0);
    v_.assign(n, 0.0);
    act_.resize(units);
    delta_.resize(units);
    std::size_t off = 0;
    for (std::size_t l = 0; l + 1 < sizes_.size(); ++l) {
      const double bound = std::sqrt(6.0 / sizes_[l]);  // He-uniform for ReLU
      for (std::uint32_t o = 0; o < sizes_[l + 1]; ++o) {
        for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < sizes_[l]; ++i) w_[off++] = bound * (2 * rng.uniform() - 1);
        w_[off++] = 0.0;  // bias
      }
    }
  }

  // The network's shape and weights (not the optimizer state) in the
  // rag::io format: checksummed, crash-safe, validated on load. Enough to
  // deploy a trained policy elsewhere; training resumes with fresh Adam state.
  void save(const std::filesystem::path& path) const {
    io::Writer w(path);
    w.bytes(kMagic, sizeof kMagic);
    w.vec(sizes_);
    w.vec(w_);
    w.commit();
  }
  [[nodiscard]] static Mlp load(const std::filesystem::path& path) {
    io::Reader r(path);
    char magic[sizeof kMagic];
    r.bytes(magic, sizeof magic);
    if (std::memcmp(magic, kMagic, sizeof magic) != 0) throw io::FormatError("Mlp: not a network file");
    Mlp m;
    m.sizes_ = r.vec<std::uint32_t>();
    auto weights = r.vec<double>();
    r.finish();
    if (m.sizes_.size() < 2) throw io::FormatError("Mlp: needs at least two layers");
    std::size_t n = 0, units = 0;
    for (std::size_t l = 0; l + 1 < m.sizes_.size(); ++l) {
      if (m.sizes_[l] == 0 || m.sizes_[l + 1] == 0 || m.sizes_[l] > 1'000'000 || m.sizes_[l + 1] > 1'000'000) throw io::FormatError("Mlp: bad layer size");
      n += std::size_t{m.sizes_[l] + 1} * m.sizes_[l + 1];
    }
    for (auto s : m.sizes_) units += s;
    if (weights.size() != n) throw io::FormatError("Mlp: weight count does not match the shape");
    for (double x : weights)
      if (!std::isfinite(x)) throw io::FormatError("Mlp: non-finite weight");
    m.w_ = std::move(weights);
    m.g_.assign(n, 0.0);
    m.m_.assign(n, 0.0);
    m.v_.assign(n, 0.0);
    m.act_.resize(units);
    m.delta_.resize(units);
    return m;
  }

  [[nodiscard]] std::uint32_t inputs() const noexcept { return sizes_.front(); }
  [[nodiscard]] std::uint32_t outputs() const noexcept { return sizes_.back(); }
  [[nodiscard]] std::size_t parameters() const noexcept { return w_.size(); }

  // out[0..outputs) = network(x). `scratch` must hold scratch_size() doubles.
  [[nodiscard]] std::size_t scratch_size() const noexcept { return act_.size(); }
  void forward(const double* x, double* out, double* scratch) const noexcept {
    for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < sizes_[0]; ++i) scratch[i] = x[i];
    propagate(scratch);
    const double* last = scratch + (act_.size() - sizes_.back());
    for (std::uint32_t k = 0; k < sizes_.back(); ++k) out[k] = last[k];
  }

  // Add the gradient of 0.5 * (out[k] - target)^2; returns out[k] - target.
  double accumulate(const double* x, std::uint32_t k, double target) {
    for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < sizes_[0]; ++i) act_[i] = x[i];
    propagate(act_.data());
    const std::size_t L = sizes_.size() - 1;
    std::size_t out_base = act_.size() - sizes_[L];
    std::fill(delta_.begin(), delta_.end(), 0.0);
    const double err = act_[out_base + k] - target;
    delta_[out_base + k] = err;
    // Backward through the layers.
    std::size_t w_end = w_.size(), a_hi = out_base;
    for (std::size_t l = L; l-- > 0;) {
      const std::uint32_t in = sizes_[l], out = sizes_[l + 1];
      const std::size_t w_base = w_end - std::size_t{in + 1} * out;
      const std::size_t a_lo = a_hi - in;  // activations of layer l
      for (std::uint32_t o = 0; o < out; ++o) {
        const double d = delta_[a_hi + o];
        if (d == 0.0) continue;
        double* gw = &g_[w_base + std::size_t{o} * (in + 1)];
        const double* w = &w_[w_base + std::size_t{o} * (in + 1)];
        for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < in; ++i) {
          gw[i] += d * act_[a_lo + i];
          delta_[a_lo + i] += d * w[i];
        }
        gw[in] += d;
      }
      if (l > 0)  // ReLU derivative on hidden activations
        for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < in; ++i)
          if (act_[a_lo + i] <= 0.0) delta_[a_lo + i] = 0.0;
      w_end = w_base;
      a_hi = a_lo;
    }
    ++pending_;
    return err;
  }

  // Move this network's weights a fraction tau of the way toward other's
  // (Polyak / exponential moving average; E24). Shapes must match.
  void blend_toward(const Mlp& other, double tau) {
    if (tau >= 1) {  // exact copy (w + 1 * (o - w) can differ from o in the last bit)
      w_ = other.w_;
      return;
    }
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < w_.size(); ++i) w_[i] += tau * (other.w_[i] - w_[i]);
  }

  // Apply the averaged accumulated gradient with Adam, then clear it.
  void step(double lr, double beta1 = 0.9, double beta2 = 0.999, double eps = 1e-8) {
    if (pending_ == 0) return;
    ++t_;
    const double inv = 1.0 / static_cast<double>(pending_);
    const double c1 = 1 - std::pow(beta1, static_cast<double>(t_)), c2 = 1 - std::pow(beta2, static_cast<double>(t_));
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < w_.size(); ++i) {
      const double g = g_[i] * inv;
      m_[i] = beta1 * m_[i] + (1 - beta1) * g;
      v_[i] = beta2 * v_[i] + (1 - beta2) * g * g;
      w_[i] -= lr * (m_[i] / c1) / (std::sqrt(v_[i] / c2) + eps);
      g_[i] = 0.0;
    }
    pending_ = 0;
  }

  // Plain stochastic gradient descent on the averaged gradient (the ablation
  // baseline for Adam), then clear it.
  void sgd_step(double lr) {
    if (pending_ == 0) return;
    const double scale = lr / static_cast<double>(pending_);
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < w_.size(); ++i) {
      w_[i] -= scale * g_[i];
      g_[i] = 0.0;
    }
    pending_ = 0;
  }

  // Parameter access (for gradient checks and soft target updates).
  [[nodiscard]] std::vector<double>& weights() noexcept { return w_; }
  [[nodiscard]] const std::vector<double>& weights() const noexcept { return w_; }
  [[nodiscard]] const std::vector<double>& gradient() const noexcept { return g_; }

 private:
  // In place: act[0..in) holds the input; fills every later layer.
  void propagate(double* act) const noexcept {
    std::size_t w_off = 0, a_in = 0;
    for (std::size_t l = 0; l + 1 < sizes_.size(); ++l) {
      const std::uint32_t in = sizes_[l], out = sizes_[l + 1];
      const std::size_t a_out = a_in + in;
      const bool hidden = l + 2 < sizes_.size();
      for (std::uint32_t o = 0; o < out; ++o) {
        const double* w = &w_[w_off + std::size_t{o} * (in + 1)];
        double s = w[in];
        for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < in; ++i) s += w[i] * act[a_in + i];
        act[a_out + o] = hidden ? std::max(0.0, s) : s;
      }
      w_off += std::size_t{in + 1} * out;
      a_in = a_out;
    }
  }

  static constexpr char kMagic[8] = {'R', 'A', 'G', 'M', 'L', 'P', '0', '1'};
  std::vector<std::uint32_t> sizes_;
  std::vector<double> w_, g_, m_, v_;  // weights (row per output unit, bias last), gradient, Adam moments
  std::vector<double> act_, delta_;    // training scratch
  std::uint64_t t_ = 0;
  std::uint32_t pending_ = 0;
};

}  // namespace rag::agent
```

```cpp
// rag/agent/model_based.hpp — a model-based agent for ExecutionEnv:
// learn the market's parameters from experience, then plan with the DP.
//
// Model-free learners (TileQ, EpisodicMemory) learn values directly and
// assume nothing about the world. This agent assumes the *form* of the model
// ("grey box"), and only its numbers are unknown:
//
//   reward  = -cost(q) + alpha * I' * g - holding * I'^2 - permanent * q * I' + I' * noise
//             (I' = inventory held after the trade)
//   last    = -cost(q) - permanent * q * rem - terminal_impact * rem^2
//   g'      = rho * g + innovation
//
// `holding` is a per-step cost of carrying inventory: the risk penalty of a
// risk-averse objective (ExecutionParams::risk_aversion, E4), 0 if
// risk-neutral. `permanent` is permanent price impact (each lot sold lowers
// the price of everything still held), learned only with
// learn_permanent_impact (E7). All coefficients are estimated by weighted least squares over
// every non-terminal step (weights 1/max(1, I')^2: the noise term scales with
// I'), from one normal-equations system solved by Gaussian elimination;
// terminal_impact from last steps; (rho, signal sd) by regressing each signal
// on the previous one. Every `replan_every` episodes it re-solves ExecutionDP
// with the current estimates and acts greedily on that plan, exploring with
// probability eps.
//
// Cost models (CostModel):
//   Quadratic  cost(q) = impact * q^2: one number, the textbook form.
//   PerSize    one learned cost per order size actually traded; unseen sizes
//              are interpolated. No assumption about the shape of the impact
//              curve; the dump at the end is fitted as a * rem^2 + b.
//   Shrunk     per-size costs blended with the quadratic fit by trade count.
//
// What it demonstrates (docs/ai/EXPERIMENTS.md, E1): with the right form, a
// few episodes pin down a handful of numbers and planning does the rest:
// 99-100% of the optimal gain after 20-50 episodes, against ~70% after 40,000
// for the model-free learner. With a badly wrong form (impact ~ q^3, fixed
// costs) the quadratic planner exploits its model's errors (53-83%); per-size
// costs recover (100%) but are catastrophic on some seeds with little data;
// Shrunk is never catastrophic.
//
// Outside its model class (E7: permanent impact with learn_permanent_impact
// off) it falls to 22-55%, and *more data makes it worse*: its plan exploits
// the model's errors, so the data it collects is increasingly one-sided.
// check_model() detects this: the gain over TWAP the model predicts for its
// own plan (exact, by policy evaluation) against the gain realized on real
// scenarios, paired. |z| <= 2.5 when the model is right, 8.5-27 after 100
// episodes when a term is missing (the model is optimistic).
//
// In a market that changes (E9), statistics that never forget average the
// old and new regimes: -166% of the new optimum 20 episodes after a flip.
// Constant forgetting (`forget`) tracks but plans on less data (54-93% in a
// noisy stable market at 0.95). Change detection (`detect_drift`: CUSUM on
// the plan's surprise, reset on an alarm) recovers to 95-100% within 20
// episodes and costs nothing while the market is stable.
#pragma once

#include <algorithm>
#include <array>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdint>
#include <memory>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

#include "rag/agent/drift.hpp"
#include "rag/agent/env.hpp"
#include "rag/agent/evaluate.hpp"
#include "rag/agent/execution_dp.hpp"
#include "rag/agent/rng.hpp"

namespace rag::agent {

enum class CostModel : std::uint8_t {
  Quadratic,  // cost(q) = impact * q^2
  PerSize,    // a free cost per order size: flexible, but wild with little data
  Shrunk,     // per-size costs shrunk toward the quadratic fit by data count (empirical Bayes)
};

// Result of ModelBasedExecutionAgent::check_model().
struct ModelCheck {
  double predicted_gain = 0;  // plan's gain over TWAP under the learned model (exact)
  double realized_gain = 0;   // measured on real scenarios, paired with TWAP
  double std_error = 0;       // of realized_gain
  double z = 0;               // (predicted - realized) / std_error; > 4: the model is wrong
};

struct ModelEstimate {
  double impact = 0, terminal_impact = 0, alpha = 0, rho = 0, signal_sd = 0;
  double holding = 0;  // per-step cost of holding I' lots: holding * I'^2 (risk penalty)
  double permanent = 0;  // permanent impact: price drop per lot sold
  std::uint64_t steps = 0;  // transitions the estimate is based on
};

class ModelBasedExecutionAgent {
 public:
  struct Config {
    std::uint32_t explore_episodes = 10;  // purely random actions first: diverse data for the regressions
    double eps = 0.01;                    // exploration after that (E11: 0.05 cost 6-10% of the online gain)
    // Exploratory actions are drawn uniformly from [explore_lo, explore_hi].
    // The full range (0-4) includes selling nothing and 3x TWAP, which make
    // random episodes expensive; 1-3 explores near TWAP (E11).
    Action explore_lo = 0, explore_hi = ExecutionEnv::kNumActions - 1;
    std::uint32_t replan_every = 20;      // episodes between DP re-solves...
    std::uint32_t replan_max_gap = 500;   // ...growing (doubling) up to this, as estimates settle
    std::uint32_t dp_grid = 61;           // signal grid of the planner (121 = the benchmark's)
    CostModel cost_model = CostModel::Quadratic;
    double shrink_steps = 30;  // Shrunk: pseudo-observations given to the quadratic prior per size
    bool learn_holding_cost = true;  // estimate the -holding * I'^2 term (needed for risk-averse objectives)
    bool learn_permanent_impact = true;  // estimate the -permanent * q * I' term (E7)
    // Per-episode decay of every sufficient statistic: 1 keeps all data
    // (stationary markets); 0.99 gives old data a half-life of ~70 episodes,
    // so the estimates track a market that changes (E9). Pair it with a small
    // replan_max_gap, or the plan won't follow the estimates.
    double forget = 1.0;
    // Change detection: a one-sided CUSUM test on surprise (episode return
    // minus the plan's predicted value from the start state). On an alarm
    // the agent multiplies its statistics by drift_forget (0 = start over)
    // and replans after replan_every new episodes. Unlike constant
    // forgetting, it costs nothing while the market is stable (E9).
    bool detect_drift = false;
    DriftParams drift{.lag = 10, .allowance = 0.3, .threshold = 10.0, .baseline_rate = 0.01, .warmup = 50};
    double drift_forget = 0.0;
    std::uint64_t seed = 1;
  };

  // `structure` supplies only what the agent is assumed to know: lots,
  // horizon and the action sizes (what each action does). Its impact, alpha,
  // rho, signal_sd and terminal_impact are ignored; they are learned.
  ModelBasedExecutionAgent(const ExecutionParams& structure, Config cfg)
      : structure_(structure), cfg_(cfg), rng_(cfg.seed), env_(structure), gap_(cfg.replan_every),
        nparams_(kCost0 + structure.lots), xtx_(std::size_t{nparams_} * nparams_, 0.0), xty_(nparams_, 0.0),
        per_n_(structure.lots + 1, 0.0), detector_(cfg.drift) {}
  explicit ModelBasedExecutionAgent(const ExecutionParams& structure) : ModelBasedExecutionAgent(structure, Config{}) {}

  Action act(const ExecutionObs& o, bool explore) {
    // Greedy without a plan yet: TWAP, without touching the RNG (greedy
    // evaluation must not change what training explores next).
    if (!plan_ && !explore) return ExecutionEnv::kTwapAction;
    if (!plan_ || (explore && (episodes_ < cfg_.explore_episodes || rng_.uniform() < cfg_.eps)))
      return static_cast<Action>(cfg_.explore_lo + rng_.below(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(cfg_.explore_hi - cfg_.explore_lo + 1)));
    return plan_->act(o);
  }

  void observe(const ExecutionObs& o, Action a, double r, const ExecutionObs& next, bool done) {
    const bool last = done && next.t >= structure_.horizon;
    // Lots sold this step, from the inventory change. On the last step the
    // env also dumps the remainder (next.inventory is then 0), so the sale is
    // taken from the action's known size, lots_for(a, inventory).
    const std::uint32_t q = last ? env_.lots_for(a, o.inventory) : o.inventory - next.inventory;
    if (o.t == 0) {  // first step of an episode: what does the plan expect from here?
      has_prediction_ = plan_ != nullptr;
      predicted_ = has_prediction_ ? plan_->value(0, o.inventory, o.signal) : 0.0;
    }
    episode_return_ += r;
    const double dq = q;
    if (last) {
      const double rem = static_cast<double>(o.inventory - q);
      if (rem > 0) {  // r = -impact q^2 - permanent q rem - terminal_impact rem^2
        t_rem4_ += rem * rem * rem * rem;
        t_rem2_r_ += rem * rem * r;
        t_rem2_q2_ += rem * rem * dq * dq;
        t_rem3_q_ += rem * rem * rem * dq;
      }
      last_steps_.push_back({q, o.inventory - q, r, 1.0});
      ++steps_;
      return;
    }
    // r = alpha (I' g) + holding (-I'^2) + permanent (-q I') + impact (-q^2) [or c_q (-1)] + I' noise
    const double held = next.inventory;
    const double w = 1.0 / std::max(1.0, held * held);
    std::array<std::pair<std::uint32_t, double>, 5> x{};
    std::size_t nx = 0;
    x[nx++] = {kAlpha, held * o.signal};
    x[nx++] = {kHolding, -held * held};
    x[nx++] = {kPermanent, -dq * held};
    x[nx++] = {kImpact, -dq * dq};
    if (q > 0) x[nx++] = {kCost0 + q - 1, -1.0};
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < nx; ++i) {
      xty_[x[i].first] += w * x[i].second * r;
      for (std::size_t j = 0; j < nx; ++j) xtx_[std::size_t{x[i].first} * nparams_ + x[j].first] += w * x[i].second * x[j].second;
    }
    per_n_[q] += 1.0;
    if (!done) {  // signal transition g -> g'
      g_gg_ += o.signal * o.signal;
      g_gn_ += o.signal * next.signal;
      g_nn_ += next.signal * next.signal;
      g_n_ += 1.0;
    }
    ++steps_;
  }

  // Kept for existing trainers; no longer needed. observe() separates the
  // last step's sale from the dump itself, from its action argument. (Bug:
  // it used to rely on this call, so trainers that only called observe()
  // fitted terminal_impact as if the whole last-step inventory was dumped.)
  void note_action(const ExecutionObs& /*o*/, Action /*a*/) noexcept {}

  void end_episode() {
    ++episodes_;
    if (cfg_.forget < 1.0) decay(cfg_.forget);
    const double surprise = episode_return_ - predicted_;
    const bool planned = has_prediction_;
    episode_return_ = predicted_ = 0.0;
    has_prediction_ = false;
    if (cfg_.detect_drift && planned && detector_.add(surprise)) {
      detector_.reset();  // the model starts over, so does the detector's baseline
      decay(cfg_.drift_forget);
      drift_alarms_.push_back(episodes_);
      last_plan_ = episodes_;
      gap_ = cfg_.replan_every;
      return;
    }
    // The first plan comes as soon as exploration ends. (Bug fixed in E11:
    // it used to wait for replan_every episodes too, so the agent acted
    // randomly for max(explore_episodes, replan_every) = 20 episodes, not 10.)
    // The gap doubles after each *re*-plan, so the first re-plan comes
    // replan_every episodes after the first plan. (Bug: it doubled after the
    // first plan too, giving plans at 10, 50, 130 instead of 10, 30, 70.)
    if (episodes_ >= cfg_.explore_episodes && (!plan_ || episodes_ - last_plan_ >= gap_)) {
      const bool first = !plan_;
      replan();
      if (!first) gap_ = std::min(gap_ * 2, cfg_.replan_max_gap);
    }
  }

  // Re-estimate parameters and re-solve the plan now.
  void replan() {
    estimate_ = current_estimate();
    ExecutionParams p = structure_;
    p.impact = std::max(estimate_.impact, 1e-6);
    p.terminal_impact = std::max(estimate_.terminal_impact, p.impact);
    p.alpha = estimate_.alpha;
    p.signal_rho = std::clamp(estimate_.rho, -0.99, 0.99);
    p.signal_sd = std::max(estimate_.signal_sd, 1e-6);
    p.impact_exponent = 2.0;
    p.fixed_cost = 0.0;
    // holding_penalty(h) = risk_aversion * noise_sd^2 * h^2 = holding * h^2.
    p.risk_aversion = std::max(0.0, estimate_.holding);
    p.noise_sd = 1.0;
    p.permanent_impact = std::max(0.0, estimate_.permanent);
    if (cfg_.cost_model != CostModel::Quadratic) {
      auto [trade, dump] = per_size_costs();
      if (cfg_.cost_model == CostModel::Shrunk) {
        // Blend each size's own estimate with the quadratic prediction,
        // weighted by how often that size was traded: unseen sizes fall back
        // to the quadratic fit instead of being extrapolated.
        const double k = cfg_.shrink_steps;
        for (std::uint32_t q = 1; q <= structure_.lots; ++q) {
          const double prior = p.impact * q * q, n = per_n_[q];
          trade[q] = (n * (seen(q) ? trade[q] : prior) + k * prior) / (n + k);
        }
        double n_last = 0;
        for (const auto& ls : last_steps_) n_last += ls.w;
        for (std::uint32_t rem = 1; rem <= structure_.lots; ++rem) {
          const double prior = p.terminal_impact * rem * rem;
          dump[rem] = (n_last * dump[rem] + k * prior) / (n_last + k);
        }
      }
      plan_ = std::make_unique<ExecutionDP>(p, std::move(trade), std::move(dump), cfg_.dp_grid);
    } else {
      plan_ = std::make_unique<ExecutionDP>(p, cfg_.dp_grid);
    }
    last_plan_ = episodes_;
    ++replans_;
  }

  // Learned cost tables (PerSize): c[q] by closed-form least squares with
  // alpha profiled out; unseen sizes linearly interpolated (or extrapolated
  // along the last segment); dump cost fitted as a*rem^2 + b on last steps.
  [[nodiscard]] std::pair<std::vector<double>, std::vector<double>> per_size_costs() const {
    const std::uint32_t L = structure_.lots;
    std::vector<double> c(L + 1, 0.0);
    std::vector<std::uint32_t> seen_sizes;
    const auto theta = solve_costs(/*per_size=*/true);
    for (std::uint32_t q = 1; q <= L; ++q)
      if (seen(q)) {
        c[q] = theta[kCost0 + q - 1];
        seen_sizes.push_back(q);
      }
    // c[0] = 0 by definition (no trade, no cost); fill the gaps.
    std::vector<std::uint32_t> knots{0};
    knots.insert(knots.end(), seen_sizes.begin(), seen_sizes.end());
    for (std::uint32_t q = 1; q <= L; ++q) {
      if (seen(q)) continue;
      auto hi = std::upper_bound(knots.begin(), knots.end(), q);
      if (hi == knots.end()) {  // beyond the largest seen size: extend the last segment
        const std::uint32_t b = knots.back(), a = knots.size() > 1 ? knots[knots.size() - 2] : 0;
        c[q] = b == a ? c[b] : c[b] + (c[b] - c[a]) * (q - b) / static_cast<double>(b - a);
      } else {
        const std::uint32_t b = *hi, a = *(hi - 1);
        c[q] = c[a] + (c[b] - c[a]) * (q - a) / static_cast<double>(b - a);
      }
    }
    // Dump: -r - c[q] = a * rem^2 + b, least squares over last steps with rem > 0.
    double s44 = 0, s42 = 0, s22 = 0, s4y = 0, s2y = 0;
    for (const auto& ls : last_steps_) {
      if (ls.rem == 0) continue;
      const double x = static_cast<double>(ls.rem) * ls.rem;
      const double y = -ls.r - c[ls.q] - estimate_.permanent * ls.q * static_cast<double>(ls.rem);
      s44 += ls.w * x * x; s42 += ls.w * x; s22 += ls.w; s4y += ls.w * x * y; s2y += ls.w * y;
    }
    double a = std::max(estimate_.terminal_impact, 1e-6), b = 0;
    const double det = s44 * s22 - s42 * s42;
    if (s22 >= 2 && det > 1e-9) {
      a = (s22 * s4y - s42 * s2y) / det;
      b = (s44 * s2y - s42 * s4y) / det;
    }
    std::vector<double> dump(L + 1, 0.0);
    for (std::uint32_t rem = 1; rem <= L; ++rem) dump[rem] = std::max(0.0, a * rem * rem + b);
    return {std::move(c), std::move(dump)};
  }

  [[nodiscard]] ModelEstimate current_estimate() const {
    ModelEstimate m;
    m.steps = steps_;
    const auto quad = solve_costs(/*per_size=*/false);
    m.impact = quad[kImpact];
    m.alpha = quad[kAlpha];
    m.holding = quad[kHolding];
    m.permanent = quad[kPermanent];
    if (cfg_.cost_model != CostModel::Quadratic) {  // alpha, holding, permanent with one free cost per size
      const auto per = solve_costs(/*per_size=*/true);
      m.alpha = per[kAlpha];
      m.holding = per[kHolding];
      m.permanent = per[kPermanent];
    }
    if (t_rem4_ > 0) m.terminal_impact = -(t_rem2_r_ + m.impact * t_rem2_q2_ + m.permanent * t_rem3_q_) / t_rem4_;
    if (g_gg_ > 0 && g_n_ > 1) {
      m.rho = g_gn_ / g_gg_;
      const double innov_var = std::max(0.0, (g_nn_ - m.rho * g_gn_) / g_n_);
      const double r2 = std::min(m.rho * m.rho, 0.9999);
      m.signal_sd = std::sqrt(innov_var / (1.0 - r2));
    }
    return m;
  }

  [[nodiscard]] const ModelEstimate& model() const noexcept { return estimate_; }
  [[nodiscard]] bool seen(std::uint32_t q) const noexcept { return q > 0 && q < per_n_.size() && per_n_[q] > 1e-6; }
  [[nodiscard]] bool has_plan() const noexcept { return plan_ != nullptr; }
  [[nodiscard]] const ExecutionDP* plan() const noexcept { return plan_.get(); }

  // Check the learned model against reality: the gain over TWAP it predicts
  // for its own greedy plan vs the gain measured on `episodes` scenarios of
  // `market`, paired. A model that exploits its own errors is optimistic, so
  // the test is one-sided: z > 4 means the model is wrong (E7: never above
  // 2.2 for a correct model, 8.5-27 with a missing term at 100 episodes).
  // Needs a plan (replan() first); costs 2 x `episodes` real episodes.
  [[nodiscard]] ModelCheck check_model(const ExecutionEnv& market, std::uint32_t episodes, std::uint64_t seed) const {
    ModelCheck c;
    if (!plan_) return c;
    const ExecutionDP& m = *plan_;
    auto plan = [&](const ExecutionObs& o) { return m.act(o); };
    auto twap = [](const ExecutionObs&) { return ExecutionEnv::kTwapAction; };
    // The plan is greedy on the model's own values, so its value under the
    // model is the DP's optimum (AgentExecutionDP.PolicyValueTablesAreSelfConsistent).
    c.predicted_gain = m.expected_start_value() - m.policy_value(twap);
    const EvalStats real = compare(market, plan, twap, episodes, seed);
    c.realized_gain = real.mean;
    c.std_error = real.std_error;
    c.z = real.std_error > 0 ? (c.predicted_gain - real.mean) / real.std_error : 0.0;
    return c;
  }
  [[nodiscard]] std::uint64_t episodes() const noexcept { return episodes_; }
  [[nodiscard]] std::uint32_t replans() const noexcept { return replans_; }
  // Episodes at which change detection fired (detect_drift).
  [[nodiscard]] const std::vector<std::uint64_t>& drift_alarms() const noexcept { return drift_alarms_; }

 private:
  // Parameter layout of the normal equations.
  static constexpr std::uint32_t kAlpha = 0, kHolding = 1, kImpact = 2, kPermanent = 3;
  static constexpr std::uint32_t kCost0 = 4;  // kCost0 + q - 1: cost of q lots

  // Weighted least squares over the chosen parameters: alpha, holding (if
  // learned) and either impact (quadratic) or one cost per seen size.
  // Returns a full-length parameter vector; unused entries are 0.
  [[nodiscard]] std::vector<double> solve_costs(bool per_size) const {
    std::vector<std::uint32_t> idx{kAlpha};
    if (cfg_.learn_holding_cost) idx.push_back(kHolding);
    if (cfg_.learn_permanent_impact) idx.push_back(kPermanent);
    if (per_size) {
      for (std::uint32_t q = 1; q <= structure_.lots; ++q)
        if (seen(q)) idx.push_back(kCost0 + q - 1);
    } else {
      idx.push_back(kImpact);
    }
    const std::size_t n = idx.size();
    std::vector<double> a(n * (n + 1));  // augmented [X'WX | X'Wy]
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
      for (std::size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) a[i * (n + 1) + j] = xtx_[std::size_t{idx[i]} * nparams_ + idx[j]];
      a[i * (n + 1) + n] = xty_[idx[i]];
      a[i * (n + 1) + i] += 1e-9 * (1.0 + a[i * (n + 1) + i]);  // tiny ridge: well-defined before data arrives
    }
    // Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting.
    for (std::size_t c = 0; c < n; ++c) {
      std::size_t piv = c;
      for (std::size_t r = c + 1; r < n; ++r)
        if (std::abs(a[r * (n + 1) + c]) > std::abs(a[piv * (n + 1) + c])) piv = r;
      if (std::abs(a[piv * (n + 1) + c]) < 1e-15) continue;
      if (piv != c)
        for (std::size_t k = 0; k <= n; ++k) std::swap(a[c * (n + 1) + k], a[piv * (n + 1) + k]);
      for (std::size_t r = 0; r < n; ++r) {
        if (r == c) continue;
        const double f = a[r * (n + 1) + c] / a[c * (n + 1) + c];
        if (f != 0)
          for (std::size_t k = c; k <= n; ++k) a[r * (n + 1) + k] -= f * a[c * (n + 1) + k];
      }
    }
    std::vector<double> theta(nparams_, 0.0);
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
      const double d = a[i * (n + 1) + i];
      theta[idx[i]] = std::abs(d) < 1e-15 ? 0.0 : a[i * (n + 1) + n] / d;
    }
    return theta;
  }

  ExecutionParams structure_;
  Config cfg_;
  Rng rng_;
  ExecutionEnv env_;  // for lots_for() only
  std::unique_ptr<ExecutionDP> plan_;
  ModelEstimate estimate_{};
  std::uint64_t episodes_ = 0, last_plan_ = 0, steps_ = 0;
  std::uint32_t gap_, replans_ = 0;
  // Weighted least squares sufficient statistics: X'WX (nparams x nparams) and X'Wy.
  std::uint32_t nparams_;
  std::vector<double> xtx_, xty_;
  // Terminal dump: sum rem^4, rem^2 r, rem^2 q^2, rem^3 q.
  double t_rem4_ = 0, t_rem2_r_ = 0, t_rem2_q2_ = 0, t_rem3_q_ = 0;
  std::vector<double> per_n_;  // non-terminal steps observed per size (decayed by `forget`)
  struct LastStep {
    std::uint32_t q, rem;
    double r;
    double w;  // weight (decayed by `forget`)
  };
  std::vector<LastStep> last_steps_;
  // Signal AR(1): sum g^2, g g', g'^2, count.
  double g_gg_ = 0, g_gn_ = 0, g_nn_ = 0;
  double g_n_ = 0;
  // Change detection.
  DriftDetector detector_;
  double predicted_ = 0, episode_return_ = 0;
  bool has_prediction_ = false;
  std::vector<std::uint64_t> drift_alarms_;

  // Multiply every sufficient statistic by f (exponential forgetting).
  void decay(double f) {
    for (double& x : xtx_) x *= f;
    for (double& x : xty_) x *= f;
    t_rem4_ *= f; t_rem2_r_ *= f; t_rem2_q2_ *= f; t_rem3_q_ *= f;
    g_gg_ *= f; g_gn_ *= f; g_nn_ *= f; g_n_ *= f;
    for (double& n : per_n_) n *= f;
    for (auto& ls : last_steps_) ls.w *= f;
    std::erase_if(last_steps_, [](const LastStep& ls) { return ls.w < 1e-4; });
  }
};

// Train a model-based agent for `episodes` episodes on `env` (own RNG stream).
inline void train_model_based(ModelBasedExecutionAgent& agent, ExecutionEnv& env, std::uint32_t episodes, Rng& rng) {
  for (std::uint32_t e = 0; e < episodes; ++e) {
    auto o = env.reset(rng);
    for (;;) {
      const Action a = agent.act(o, true);
      const auto st = env.step(a, rng);
      agent.observe(o, a, st.reward, st.obs, st.done);
      o = st.obs;
      if (st.done) break;
    }
    agent.end_episode();
  }
}

}  // namespace rag::agent
```

```cpp
// rag/agent/ope.hpp — off-policy evaluation: estimate a target policy's value
// from episodes logged under a different (behaviour) policy, without running
// the target.
//
// Estimators (per-decision forms; Precup et al. 2000, Jiang & Li 2016):
//   PDIS   sum_t mean_i( w_it r_it ),            w_it = prod_{k<=t} pi(a_ik|s_ik) / b(a_ik|s_ik)
//   WPDIS  sum_t sum_i( w_it r_it ) / sum_i w_it  (self-normalized: biased, much lower variance)
//   DR     mean_i sum_t [ w_it (r_it - Q(s_it, a_it)) + w_i,t-1 V(s_it) ]
//          (doubly robust: a model's Q/V plus importance-weighted corrections)
// The direct method (DM) is just the model's own value of the target, e.g.
// ExecutionDP::policy_value() on a fitted model.
//
// Diagnostic: the effective sample size of the step-t weights,
//   ESS_t = (sum_i w_it)^2 / sum_i w_it^2,
// is how many logged episodes the estimate at step t effectively rests on.
// When it collapses toward 0, importance sampling can't be trusted.
//
// Measured on ExecutionEnv (E10): with horizon 20 and a deterministic target
// that differs from the behaviour in many states, no logged episode follows
// the target beyond a few steps (ESS ~ 0), and the IS family's errors stay
// at 45-2,968% of the optimal gain even with 10,000 logged episodes. The
// direct method is accurate when the model class is right (<= 2% at 1,000
// episodes) and biased when it isn't, by an amount more data doesn't
// shrink; DR repairs that bias only for targets close to the behaviour.
#pragma once

#include <algorithm>
#include <cstdint>
#include <limits>
#include <vector>

#include "rag/agent/env.hpp"

namespace rag::agent {

template <class Obs>
struct LoggedStep {
  Obs obs;
  Action action;
  double reward;
  double propensity;  // b(action | obs) under the behaviour policy, > 0
};
template <class Obs>
using LoggedEpisode = std::vector<LoggedStep<Obs>>;

struct OpeEstimates {
  double pdis = 0, wpdis = 0, dr = 0;
  double min_ess = 0;               // smallest effective sample size over steps (in episodes)
  std::uint32_t uncovered_steps = 0;  // steps at which no logged episode followed the target
};

// Estimates for a deterministic target policy pi(obs) -> Action. q(obs, a)
// and v(obs) are a model's action values and state values *for the target*
// (used by DR only; pass functions returning 0 to get plain IS). Episodes
// shorter than `horizon` ended early with reward 0 afterwards.
template <class Obs, class Target, class QModel, class VModel>
OpeEstimates off_policy_estimates(const std::vector<LoggedEpisode<Obs>>& logs, Target&& pi, QModel&& q, VModel&& v,
                                  std::uint32_t horizon) {
  OpeEstimates out;
  if (logs.empty()) {
    out.uncovered_steps = horizon;  // nothing was logged, so nothing followed the target
    return out;
  }
  const double n = static_cast<double>(logs.size());
  std::vector<double> wsum(horizon, 0.0), w2sum(horizon, 0.0), wr(horizon, 0.0);
  double pdis = 0, dr = 0;
  for (const auto& ep : logs) {
    double w = 1.0, w_prev = 1.0;
    for (std::uint32_t t = 0; t < horizon; ++t) {
      if (t < ep.size()) {
        const auto& s = ep[t];
        w *= (pi(s.obs) == s.action ? 1.0 : 0.0) / s.propensity;
        pdis += w * s.reward;
        wr[t] += w * s.reward;
        dr += w * (s.reward - q(s.obs, s.action)) + w_prev * v(s.obs);
        w_prev = w;
      }
      wsum[t] += w;  // after the episode ended: weight carries over, reward 0
      w2sum[t] += w * w;
    }
  }
  out.pdis = pdis / n;
  out.dr = dr / n;
  out.min_ess = std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity();
  for (std::uint32_t t = 0; t < horizon; ++t) {
    if (wsum[t] > 0) {
      out.wpdis += wr[t] / wsum[t];
      out.min_ess = std::min(out.min_ess, wsum[t] * wsum[t] / w2sum[t]);
    } else {
      ++out.uncovered_steps;
      out.min_ess = 0;
    }
  }
  return out;
}

}  // namespace rag::agent
```

```cpp
// rag/agent/policy_table.hpp — compile an execution policy into a lookup
// table (E22).
//
// The execution state is small: time (horizon values), inventory (lots + 1
// values) and one continuous signal. Sampling any policy (a trained neural
// network, a planner, an expensive ensemble) at the centre of every
// (t, inventory, signal bin) cell gives a table of one-byte actions whose
// lookup costs a few nanoseconds, whatever the original policy cost.
//
//   ExecutionPolicyTable table(params, [&](const ExecutionObs& o) { return trainer.deployed_act(o); });
//   Action a = table.act(obs);            // no allocation, no floating-point model
//
// Signals outside +-signal_range_sd standard deviations use the edge bins; a
// NaN signal uses bin 0. Times and inventories past the grid are clamped.
//
//   table.save(path); auto t = ExecutionPolicyTable::load(path);   // rag::io format, checksummed
//   auto ens = ExecutionPolicyTable::median({t1, t2, t3});         // ensemble at table cost
//
// median() combines tables of the same shape cell by cell with the (lower)
// median action. Actions are ordered by trade size (ExecutionParams::sizes is
// increasing by default), so the median is the natural vote for an ordinal
// choice.
#pragma once

#include <algorithm>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstring>
#include <filesystem>
#include <limits>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <vector>

#include "rag/agent/env.hpp"
#include "rag/io.hpp"

namespace rag::agent {

struct PolicyTableParams {
  std::uint32_t signal_bins = 64;  // bins over [-range, +range] signal standard deviations
  double signal_range_sd = 4.0;    // the signal's stationary sd is ExecutionParams::signal_sd
};

class ExecutionPolicyTable {
 public:
  template <class Policy>
  ExecutionPolicyTable(const ExecutionParams& p, Policy&& policy, PolicyTableParams tp = {})
      : horizon_(p.horizon), lots_(p.lots), bins_(tp.signal_bins) {
    if (p.horizon == 0 || tp.signal_bins == 0 || !(tp.signal_range_sd > 0) || !(p.signal_sd > 0) ||
        !std::isfinite(tp.signal_range_sd * p.signal_sd))
      throw std::invalid_argument("ExecutionPolicyTable: horizon, bins, range and signal_sd must be positive");
    lo_ = -tp.signal_range_sd * p.signal_sd;
    width_ = 2 * tp.signal_range_sd * p.signal_sd / static_cast<double>(bins_);
    if (!valid_grid(lo_, width_))
      throw std::invalid_argument("ExecutionPolicyTable: signal_range_sd * signal_sd gives a zero, infinite or subnormal bin width");
    inv_width_ = 1.0 / width_;
    const std::size_t cells = cell_count(horizon_, lots_, bins_);
    if (cells == 0 || cells > table_.max_size())
      throw std::invalid_argument("ExecutionPolicyTable: horizon x (lots + 1) x signal_bins is too large");
    table_.resize(cells);
    std::size_t k = 0;
    for (std::uint32_t t = 0; t < horizon_; ++t)
      for (std::uint64_t inv = 0; inv <= lots_; ++inv)  // 64-bit: lots_ may be UINT32_MAX
        for (std::uint32_t b = 0; b < bins_; ++b) {
          const Action a = policy(ExecutionObs{t, static_cast<std::uint32_t>(inv), bin_centre(b)});
          if (a >= ExecutionEnv::kNumActions) throw std::out_of_range("ExecutionPolicyTable: policy returned an invalid action");
          table_[k++] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(a);
        }
  }

  [[nodiscard]] Action act(const ExecutionObs& o) const noexcept {
    const double x = (o.signal - lo_) * inv_width_;
    const std::uint32_t b = !(x > 0) ? 0u : x >= static_cast<double>(bins_) ? bins_ - 1 : static_cast<std::uint32_t>(x);
    const std::uint32_t t = std::min(o.t, horizon_ - 1), inv = std::min(o.inventory, lots_);
    return table_[(static_cast<std::size_t>(t) * (static_cast<std::size_t>(lots_) + 1) + inv) * bins_ + b];
  }

  // Cell-by-cell lower median of tables with the same grid.
  [[nodiscard]] static ExecutionPolicyTable median(const std::vector<ExecutionPolicyTable>& tables) {
    if (tables.empty()) throw std::invalid_argument("ExecutionPolicyTable::median: no tables");
    const auto& f = tables.front();
    for (const auto& t : tables)
      if (t.horizon_ != f.horizon_ || t.lots_ != f.lots_ || t.bins_ != f.bins_ || t.lo_ != f.lo_ || t.width_ != f.width_)
        throw std::invalid_argument("ExecutionPolicyTable::median: tables have different grids");
    ExecutionPolicyTable out = f;
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> votes(tables.size());
    for (std::size_t k = 0; k < out.table_.size(); ++k) {
      for (std::size_t i = 0; i < tables.size(); ++i) votes[i] = tables[i].table_[k];
      std::nth_element(votes.begin(), votes.begin() + static_cast<std::ptrdiff_t>((votes.size() - 1) / 2), votes.end());
      out.table_[k] = votes[(votes.size() - 1) / 2];
    }
    return out;
  }

  void save(const std::filesystem::path& path) const {
    io::Writer w(path);
    w.bytes(kMagic, sizeof kMagic);
    w.pod(horizon_);
    w.pod(lots_);
    w.pod(bins_);
    w.pod(lo_);
    w.pod(width_);
    w.vec(table_);
    w.commit();
  }

  // Rejects anything save() could not have written (io::FormatError).
  [[nodiscard]] static ExecutionPolicyTable load(const std::filesystem::path& path) {
    io::Reader r(path);
    char magic[sizeof kMagic];
    r.bytes(magic, sizeof magic);
    if (std::memcmp(magic, kMagic, sizeof magic) != 0) throw io::FormatError("ExecutionPolicyTable: not a policy table");
    ExecutionPolicyTable t;
    t.horizon_ = r.pod<std::uint32_t>();
    t.lots_ = r.pod<std::uint32_t>();
    t.bins_ = r.pod<std::uint32_t>();
    t.lo_ = r.pod<double>();
    t.width_ = r.pod<double>();
    t.table_ = r.vec<std::uint8_t>();
    r.finish();
    const double cells = static_cast<double>(t.horizon_) * (static_cast<double>(t.lots_) + 1) * static_cast<double>(t.bins_);
    if (t.horizon_ == 0 || t.bins_ == 0 || !valid_grid(t.lo_, t.width_) || cells != static_cast<double>(t.table_.size()))
      throw io::FormatError("ExecutionPolicyTable: inconsistent grid");
    for (auto a : t.table_)
      if (a >= ExecutionEnv::kNumActions) throw io::FormatError("ExecutionPolicyTable: invalid action");
    t.inv_width_ = 1.0 / t.width_;
    return t;
  }

  [[nodiscard]] double bin_centre(std::uint32_t b) const noexcept { return lo_ + (static_cast<double>(b) + 0.5) * width_; }
  [[nodiscard]] std::size_t bytes() const noexcept { return table_.size(); }
  [[nodiscard]] std::uint32_t signal_bins() const noexcept { return bins_; }

 private:
  static constexpr char kMagic[8] = {'R', 'A', 'G', 'P', 'T', 'B', 'L', '1'};
  ExecutionPolicyTable() = default;

  // A finite origin and a normal (finite, non-zero, non-subnormal) bin width:
  // then 1 / width is finite too and act()'s multiply bins what bin_centre()
  // describes.
  [[nodiscard]] static bool valid_grid(double lo, double width) noexcept {
    return std::isfinite(lo) && width > 0 && std::isnormal(width);
  }
  // horizon x (lots + 1) x bins, or 0 if that does not fit in a size_t.
  [[nodiscard]] static std::size_t cell_count(std::uint32_t horizon, std::uint32_t lots, std::uint32_t bins) noexcept {
    const std::uint64_t rows = std::uint64_t{horizon} * (std::uint64_t{lots} + 1);  // < 2^64
    if (bins == 0 || rows > std::numeric_limits<std::size_t>::max() / bins) return 0;
    return static_cast<std::size_t>(rows * bins);
  }

  std::uint32_t horizon_ = 1, lots_ = 0, bins_ = 1;
  double lo_ = 0, width_ = 1, inv_width_ = 1;
  std::vector<std::uint8_t> table_;
};

}  // namespace rag::agent
```

```cpp
// rag/agent/rng.hpp — fast, deterministic random numbers for simulation and
// exploration.
//
// xoshiro256** (Blackman & Vigna): 4 x 64-bit state, ~1 ns per draw, passes
// BigCrush. Seeded through splitmix64 so that nearby seeds (1, 2, 3, ...)
// give unrelated streams — evaluation runs use seed + episode as a cheap way
// to replay the *same* market for every policy (common random numbers).
// std::mt19937 is avoided on purpose: 2.5 KB of state per generator and
// implementation-defined distributions would make results differ between
// standard libraries.
#pragma once

#include <cmath>
#include <cstdint>
#include <numbers>

namespace rag::agent {

class Rng {
 public:
  explicit constexpr Rng(std::uint64_t seed = 1) noexcept { reseed(seed); }

  constexpr void reseed(std::uint64_t seed) noexcept {
    for (auto& s : s_) {
      seed += 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15ull;
      std::uint64_t z = seed;
      z = (z ^ (z >> 30)) * 0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9ull;
      z = (z ^ (z >> 27)) * 0x94D049BB133111EBull;
      s = z ^ (z >> 31);
    }
    has_spare_ = false;
  }

  constexpr std::uint64_t next() noexcept {
    const std::uint64_t result = rotl(s_[1] * 5, 7) * 9;
    const std::uint64_t t = s_[1] << 17;
    s_[2] ^= s_[0];
    s_[3] ^= s_[1];
    s_[1] ^= s_[2];
    s_[0] ^= s_[3];
    s_[2] ^= t;
    s_[3] = rotl(s_[3], 45);
    return result;
  }

  // Uniform in [0, 1) with 53 random bits.
  constexpr double uniform() noexcept { return static_cast<double>(next() >> 11) * 0x1.0p-53; }

  // Uniform integer in [0, n) (Lemire's multiply-shift; bias < 2^-32).
  constexpr std::uint32_t below(std::uint32_t n) noexcept {
    return static_cast<std::uint32_t>((static_cast<std::uint64_t>(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(next() >> 32)) * n) >> 32);
  }

  // Standard normal (Marsaglia polar method; caches the second variate).
  double normal() noexcept {
    if (has_spare_) {
      has_spare_ = false;
      return spare_;
    }
    double u, v, s;
    do {
      u = 2.0 * uniform() - 1.0;
      v = 2.0 * uniform() - 1.0;
      s = u * u + v * v;
    } while (s >= 1.0 || s == 0.0);
    const double m = std::sqrt(-2.0 * std::log(s) / s);
    spare_ = v * m;
    has_spare_ = true;
    return u * m;
  }

 private:
  static constexpr std::uint64_t rotl(std::uint64_t x, int k) noexcept { return (x << k) | (x >> (64 - k)); }
  std::uint64_t s_[4]{};
  double spare_ = 0.0;
  bool has_spare_ = false;
};

}  // namespace rag::agent
```

```cpp
// rag/agent/trainer.hpp — the supervisor around a learning agent: training
// loop, held-out evaluation, champion/challenger promotion, and drift
// detection.
//
// A self-learning system needs more than a learner. It also needs:
//
//   * Held-out evaluation. Training returns are measured while exploring,
//     and on scenarios the agent has adapted to. Evaluation replays a fixed
//     set of *unseen* scenarios (seeds the trainer never uses) greedily, so
//     every score is comparable with every other.
//   * A champion. Learning is noisy, and a later policy can be worse than an
//     earlier one. The trainer keeps the best policy seen so far and only
//     promotes a challenger that scores at least as well on the same
//     scenarios. The champion is re-scored each time, so after the world
//     changes it is judged on the new world, not its old record. The
//     champion is what gets *deployed* (deployed_act()); the learner keeps
//     its own weights and keeps improving. Overwriting the learner with the
//     champion would throw away whatever it was in the middle of learning.
//   * Drift detection, in two stages.
//       1. Suspect (fast, noisy): a CUSUM test on surprise = (return obtained)
//          - (return the agent predicted at the start of the episode). A
//          sustained negative shift means things go worse than the agent
//          expects. But that has two causes: the world changed, or the
//          agent's own learning wobbled (values are biased and still moving
//          while it learns).
//       2. Confirm (slow, exact): re-score the frozen champion on the fixed
//          held-out scenarios. In an unchanged world that score is
//          reproduced bit for bit; only a changed world moves it. A
//          confirmed drift makes the agent explore again, with a fresh step
//          size and an empty replay buffer, instead of exploiting stale
//          knowledge. Without a champion yet, suspicions are acted on.
#pragma once

#include <algorithm>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdint>
#include <deque>
#include <functional>
#include <optional>
#include <vector>

#include "rag/agent/agent.hpp"
#include "rag/agent/drift.hpp"
#include "rag/agent/env.hpp"
#include "rag/agent/evaluate.hpp"
#include "rag/agent/rng.hpp"

namespace rag::agent {

struct TrainConfig {
  std::uint32_t eval_every = 250;      // episodes between champion/challenger evaluations
  std::uint32_t eval_episodes = 300;   // held-out scenarios per evaluation
  std::uint64_t eval_seed = 9'000'000; // held-out scenario seeds: eval_seed + i
  std::uint64_t train_seed = 1;        // training scenarios come from one stream seeded here
  bool keep_champion = true;           // deploy the best policy seen, not just the latest
  bool detect_drift = true;
  DriftParams drift{};
  // Drift is only meaningful once the agent has stopped exploring heavily.
  // 0 = once the agent's ε schedule has finished (AgentConfig::eps_decay_episodes).
  std::uint32_t drift_after_episodes = 0;
  double reexplore_epsilon = 0.5;
  std::uint32_t reexplore_episodes = 5000;
  bool forget_on_drift = true;  // clear the replay buffer when drift is detected
  // Policy bank: on a confirmed drift the outgoing champion is banked, and
  // every banked policy is scored on the new world. If one clearly beats the
  // current champion (by 2 standard errors), the world has returned to a
  // regime seen before: that policy is redeployed, the learner warm-starts
  // from it, and exploration stays light (recall_epsilon).
  bool policy_bank = true;
  std::uint32_t bank_capacity = 8;  // oldest entries are dropped beyond this
  double recall_epsilon = 0.05;
  std::uint32_t recall_episodes = 500;
};

struct EvalPoint {
  std::uint64_t episode;
  double challenger;  // current policy on the held-out scenarios
  double champion;    // best policy so far, re-scored on the same scenarios
  bool promoted;
  double epsilon;
  bool learned_deployed = true;  // false while a baseline (set_baseline) beats the champion
  // The champion's re-score moved by more than 2 standard errors. In an
  // unchanged world it reproduces exactly (frozen policy, fixed scenarios),
  // so this is a confirmed change, in either direction (E13).
  bool world_changed = false;
};

struct TrainReport {
  std::vector<EvalPoint> evals;
  std::vector<std::uint64_t> drift_alarms;    // confirmed drifts (episode numbers)
  std::vector<std::uint64_t> drift_rejected;  // suspicions the champion check rejected
  std::vector<std::uint64_t> bank_recalls;    // confirmed drifts answered by redeploying a banked policy
  std::vector<double> returns;              // every training episode's return
  double champion_score = 0;                // held-out score of the deployed policy
};

template <Environment Env>
class Trainer {
 public:
  Trainer(Agent<Env>& agent, Env& env, TrainConfig cfg = {})
      : agent_(agent), env_(env), cfg_(cfg), rng_(cfg.train_seed), drift_(cfg.drift) {}

  // One training episode: act with exploration, learn from every step.
  double run_episode() {
    auto o = env_.reset(rng_);
    const double predicted = agent_.value(o);
    double total = 0;
    for (;;) {
      const Action a = agent_.act(o, /*explore=*/true);
      const auto st = env_.step(a, rng_);
      agent_.observe(o, a, st.reward, st.obs, st.done);
      total += st.reward;
      o = st.obs;
      if (st.done) break;
    }
    agent_.end_episode();
    last_surprise_ = total - predicted;
    return total;
  }

  // Train for `episodes` more episodes. Can be called repeatedly; the
  // champion, drift detector and scenario stream carry over between calls.
  TrainReport run(std::uint32_t episodes, const std::function<void(const EvalPoint&)>& on_eval = {}) {
    TrainReport rep;
    rep.returns.reserve(episodes);
    for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < episodes; ++i) {
      rep.returns.push_back(run_episode());
      const std::uint64_t drift_after =
          cfg_.drift_after_episodes ? cfg_.drift_after_episodes : agent_.config().eps_decay_episodes;
      if (cfg_.detect_drift && agent_.episodes() > drift_after && drift_.add(last_surprise_)) {
        if (confirm_drift()) {
          handle_drift(rep);
        } else {
          drift_.rebase();  // a false alarm: stay armed
          rep.drift_rejected.push_back(agent_.episodes());
        }
      }
      if (cfg_.eval_every && agent_.episodes() % cfg_.eval_every == 0) {
        rep.evals.push_back(check_champion());
        if (rep.evals.back().world_changed) handle_drift(rep);
        if (on_eval) on_eval(rep.evals.back());
      }
    }
    rep.champion_score = deployed_score();
    return rep;
  }

  // The policy to use in production: the champion, or the learner itself
  // when no evaluation has happened yet (or keep_champion is off). With a
  // baseline set, the baseline until a learned policy has beaten it.
  [[nodiscard]] Action deployed_act(const typename Env::Observation& o) const noexcept {
    if (baseline_ && !learned_beats_baseline_) return baseline_(o);
    return (cfg_.keep_champion && champion_) ? agent_.act_as(*champion_, o) : agent_.act(o, false);
  }

  // A safe fallback policy (e.g. TWAP). The learned champion is deployed only
  // once it beats the baseline on the held-out scenarios by more than 2
  // standard errors of the paired difference; it's re-checked at every
  // champion evaluation and after every confirmed drift. Measured: in a
  // weak-signal market a Q-learner's champion was 35% *worse* than TWAP;
  // with this guard the deployed policy stays at TWAP until learning pays.
  void set_baseline(std::function<Action(const typename Env::Observation&)> baseline) {
    baseline_ = std::move(baseline);
    learned_beats_baseline_ = false;
  }
  [[nodiscard]] bool learned_policy_deployed() const noexcept { return !baseline_ || learned_beats_baseline_; }
  [[nodiscard]] double deployed_score() {
    return evaluate(env_, [&](const auto& o) { return deployed_act(o); }, cfg_.eval_episodes, cfg_.eval_seed).mean;
  }
  [[nodiscard]] bool has_champion() const noexcept { return champion_.has_value(); }
  // The deployed policy's snapshot (nullptr before the first evaluation);
  // e.g. champion()->net.save(path) for a NeuralQ agent.
  [[nodiscard]] const auto* champion() const noexcept { return champion_ ? &*champion_ : nullptr; }
  [[nodiscard]] std::size_t bank_size() const noexcept { return bank_.size(); }

  // Held-out greedy score of the agent as it is now.
  [[nodiscard]] double score_current() { return score_current_stats().mean; }

 private:
  EvalStats score_current_stats() {
    return evaluate(env_, [&](const auto& o) { return agent_.act(o, false); }, cfg_.eval_episodes, cfg_.eval_seed);
  }

  double score_snapshot(const typename Agent<Env>::Snapshot& s) { return score_snapshot_stats(s).mean; }
  EvalStats score_snapshot_stats(const typename Agent<Env>::Snapshot& s) {
    const auto mine = agent_.snapshot();
    agent_.restore(s);
    const EvalStats v = score_current_stats();
    agent_.restore(mine);
    return v;
  }

  // After a confirmed drift: bank the outgoing champion, then look for a
  // banked policy that fits the new world better than the current champion.
  bool recall_from_bank() {
    if (!cfg_.policy_bank || !champion_) return false;
    bank_.push_back(*champion_);
    if (bank_.size() > cfg_.bank_capacity) bank_.erase(bank_.begin());
    std::size_t best = bank_.size();
    EvalStats best_stats = champion_stats_;  // the champion as re-scored on the new world
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i + 1 < bank_.size(); ++i) {  // the newest entry is the champion itself
      const EvalStats s = score_snapshot_stats(bank_[i]);
      if (s.mean > best_stats.mean + 2.0 * champion_stats_.std_error) {
        best = i;
        best_stats = s;
      }
    }
    if (best == bank_.size()) return false;
    champion_ = bank_[best];
    champion_stats_ = best_stats;
    agent_.restore(*champion_);  // warm start: the learner continues from the recalled policy
    return true;
  }

  // Stage 2 of drift detection: did the frozen champion's held-out score
  // drop? (Exactly reproducible in an unchanged world.)
  // A confirmed change: rebuild the detector's baseline, bank the outgoing
  // champion, and either recall a banked policy or re-explore.
  void handle_drift(TrainReport& rep) {
    drift_.reset();
    rep.drift_alarms.push_back(agent_.episodes());
    if (cfg_.forget_on_drift) agent_.forget_experience();
    if (recall_from_bank()) {
      check_baseline();
      rep.bank_recalls.push_back(agent_.episodes());
      agent_.reexplore(cfg_.recall_epsilon, cfg_.recall_episodes);
    } else {
      agent_.reexplore(cfg_.reexplore_epsilon, cfg_.reexplore_episodes);
      check_baseline();  // the old champion just failed: fall back to the baseline if it's better
    }
  }

  bool confirm_drift() {
    if (!champion_) return true;
    const EvalStats now = score_snapshot_stats(*champion_);
    const bool dropped = now.mean < champion_stats_.mean - 2.0 * champion_stats_.std_error;
    // With a two-sided detector, a significant rise is a changed world too.
    const bool rose = cfg_.drift.two_sided && now.mean > champion_stats_.mean + 2.0 * champion_stats_.std_error;
    if (dropped || rose) champion_stats_ = now;
    return dropped || rose;
  }

  // Paired held-out comparison of the champion with the baseline.
  void check_baseline() {
    if (!baseline_ || !champion_) return;
    const auto mine = agent_.snapshot();
    agent_.restore(*champion_);
    const EvalStats d = compare(env_, [&](const auto& o) { return agent_.act(o, false); }, baseline_, cfg_.eval_episodes,
                                cfg_.eval_seed);
    agent_.restore(mine);
    learned_beats_baseline_ = d.mean > 2.0 * d.std_error;
  }

  EvalPoint check_champion() {
    EvalPoint p = check_champion_inner();
    check_baseline();
    p.learned_deployed = learned_policy_deployed();
    return p;
  }

  EvalPoint check_champion_inner() {
    const EvalStats challenger = score_current_stats();
    EvalPoint p{agent_.episodes(), challenger.mean, 0.0, false, agent_.epsilon()};
    if (!champion_) {
      champion_ = agent_.snapshot();
      champion_stats_ = challenger;
      p.champion = p.challenger;
      p.promoted = true;
      return p;
    }
    const EvalStats before = champion_stats_;
    champion_stats_ = score_snapshot_stats(*champion_);  // re-scored: the world may have changed
    p.champion = champion_stats_.mean;
    if (cfg_.detect_drift && std::abs(champion_stats_.mean - before.mean) > 2.0 * before.std_error) {
      p.world_changed = true;  // keep the old champion this time, so the drift handler banks it
      return p;
    }
    if (p.challenger >= p.champion) {
      champion_ = agent_.snapshot();
      champion_stats_ = challenger;
      p.champion = p.challenger;
      p.promoted = true;
    }
    return p;
  }

  Agent<Env>& agent_;
  Env& env_;
  TrainConfig cfg_;
  Rng rng_;
  DriftDetector drift_;
  std::optional<typename Agent<Env>::Snapshot> champion_;
  EvalStats champion_stats_{};
  std::vector<typename Agent<Env>::Snapshot> bank_;  // champions of past regimes
  std::function<Action(const typename Env::Observation&)> baseline_;
  bool learned_beats_baseline_ = false;
  double last_surprise_ = 0;
};

}  // namespace rag::agent
```

```cpp
// rag/agent/tuning.hpp — hyperparameter optimization with NLopt (optional
// dependency: libnlopt-cxx-dev; CMake target NLopt::nlopt). E18.
//
// maximize() searches a box of parameters, each optionally on a log scale
// and/or integer-valued, with a derivative-free NLopt algorithm (default
// Subplex, a robust Nelder-Mead variant that tolerates the plateaus integer
// parameters create). The objective receives parameters in natural units.
// Every trial is kept, for later analysis (analysis.hpp).
//
// Learning curves are noisy, so make the objective deterministic (fixed
// training seeds) and validate the winner on seeds the search never saw: in
// E18 the tuned score on the search's own seeds was ~10 points higher than
// on held-out seeds (the winner's curse).
#pragma once

#include <nlopt.hpp>

#include <cmath>
#include <functional>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <string>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

namespace rag::agent::tuning {

struct Param {
  std::string name;
  double lo, hi;          // bounds in natural units
  bool log_scale = false;  // search in log space (for step sizes, horizons, ...)
  bool integer = false;    // rounded before the objective sees it
};

struct Trial {
  std::vector<double> values;  // natural units
  double score;
};

struct Result {
  std::vector<double> best;  // natural units
  double best_score = -HUGE_VAL;
  std::vector<Trial> history;
  std::string status;        // NLopt's termination reason
};

namespace detail {
inline double to_search(const Param& p, double v) { return p.log_scale ? std::log(v) : v; }
inline double to_natural(const Param& p, double s) {
  double v = p.log_scale ? std::exp(s) : s;
  if (p.integer) v = std::round(v);
  return std::min(std::max(v, p.lo), p.hi);
}
}  // namespace detail

// Maximize objective(values) over `space`, starting from `start` (natural
// units), with at most `max_evals` evaluations.
inline Result maximize(const std::vector<Param>& space, const std::vector<double>& start,
                       const std::function<double(const std::vector<double>&)>& objective, int max_evals,
                       nlopt::algorithm algorithm = nlopt::LN_SBPLX) {
  const std::size_t n = space.size();
  if (start.size() != n) throw std::invalid_argument("tuning::maximize: start has the wrong size");
  std::vector<double> lo(n), hi(n), x(n), step(n);
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    lo[i] = detail::to_search(space[i], space[i].lo);
    hi[i] = detail::to_search(space[i], space[i].hi);
    x[i] = detail::to_search(space[i], start[i]);
    step[i] = 0.25 * (hi[i] - lo[i]);
    if (space[i].integer && !space[i].log_scale) step[i] = std::max(step[i], 1.0);  // move by whole units
  }
  Result r;
  struct Ctx {
    const std::vector<Param>* space;
    const std::function<double(const std::vector<double>&)>* f;
    Result* r;
  } ctx{&space, &objective, &r};
  nlopt::opt opt(algorithm, static_cast<unsigned>(n));
  opt.set_lower_bounds(lo);
  opt.set_upper_bounds(hi);
  opt.set_maxeval(max_evals);
  opt.set_initial_step(step);
  opt.set_max_objective(
      [](const std::vector<double>& s, std::vector<double>&, void* data) {
        auto& c = *static_cast<Ctx*>(data);
        std::vector<double> v(s.size());
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < s.size(); ++i) v[i] = detail::to_natural((*c.space)[i], s[i]);
        const double score = (*c.f)(v);
        c.r->history.push_back({v, score});
        if (score > c.r->best_score) {
          c.r->best_score = score;
          c.r->best = v;
        }
        return score;
      },
      &ctx);
  double fx = 0;
  try {
    const nlopt::result res = opt.optimize(x, fx);
    r.status = res == nlopt::MAXEVAL_REACHED ? "max evaluations reached" : "converged";
  } catch (const std::exception& e) {
    r.status = e.what();  // e.g. roundoff-limited: the best trial so far is still valid
  }
  return r;
}

// Global, then local: CRS2 (controlled random search with local mutation)
// over the whole box, then Subplex from the best point it found. Use this
// when the score landscape is rugged or noisy: in E18 a local search alone
// found 57% or 70% depending only on its initial step sizes. Reproducible:
// NLopt's random generator is seeded with `seed`.
inline Result maximize_global(const std::vector<Param>& space, const std::vector<double>& start,
                              const std::function<double(const std::vector<double>&)>& objective, int global_evals,
                              int local_evals, unsigned long seed = 1) {
  nlopt::srand(seed);
  Result g = maximize(space, start, objective, global_evals, nlopt::GN_CRS2_LM);
  Result l = maximize(space, g.best.empty() ? start : g.best, objective, local_evals, nlopt::LN_SBPLX);
  Result r = g.best_score >= l.best_score ? g : l;
  r.history = g.history;
  r.history.insert(r.history.end(), l.history.begin(), l.history.end());
  r.status = "global: " + g.status + "; local: " + l.status;
  return r;
}

}  // namespace rag::agent::tuning
```
