// rag/agent/validation.hpp — out-of-sample validation of execution
// strategies (E28).
//
// A strategy that scores well in the simulator it was trained or tuned in
// can still fail in the market it meets. This header measures strategies the
// way a trading desk would before deploying one:
//
//   * on a stress suite: the nominal market and markets that differ from it
//     (impact, signal strength and sign, persistence, volatility, permanent
//     impact, impact shape, fees), each with its own exact optimum (DP);
//   * on sealed test scenarios: a seed range used for nothing else, so no
//     choice made while developing a strategy has seen them;
//   * with paired, per-episode trading metrics against TWAP (common random
//     numbers): mean gain with a bootstrap interval, share of what was
//     achievable in that market, the worst-5% tail (CVaR) and the
//     probability of doing worse than TWAP.
//
//   for (const auto& s : validation::stress_suite(ExecutionParams{})) {
//     const auto m = validation::measure(s.params, strategy, 4000, validation::kSealedSeed);
//   }
#pragma once

#include <cstdint>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "rag/agent/evaluate.hpp"
#include "rag/agent/execution_dp.hpp"

namespace rag::agent::validation {

// Test scenarios start here; training, tuning and earlier evaluations use
// seeds far below (all experiments up to E27 used < 10^8).
inline constexpr std::uint64_t kSealedSeed = 900'000'000;

struct Scenario {
  std::string name;
  ExecutionParams params;
};

// The nominal market first, then one change at a time.
inline std::vector<Scenario> stress_suite(const ExecutionParams& base) {
  std::vector<Scenario> s;
  auto add = [&](std::string name, auto change) {
    ExecutionParams p = base;
    change(p);
    s.push_back({std::move(name), p});
  };
  add("nominal", [](ExecutionParams&) {});
  add("impact x2", [](ExecutionParams& p) { p.impact *= 2; p.terminal_impact *= 2; });
  add("impact x0.5", [](ExecutionParams& p) { p.impact *= 0.5; p.terminal_impact *= 0.5; });
  add("signal x0.5", [](ExecutionParams& p) { p.alpha *= 0.5; });
  add("signal x1.5", [](ExecutionParams& p) { p.alpha *= 1.5; });
  add("signal flipped", [](ExecutionParams& p) { p.alpha = -p.alpha; });
  add("persistence 0.9", [](ExecutionParams& p) { p.signal_rho = 0.9; });
  add("persistence 0.3", [](ExecutionParams& p) { p.signal_rho = 0.3; });
  add("volatility x2", [](ExecutionParams& p) { p.noise_sd *= 2; });
  add("permanent impact", [](ExecutionParams& p) { p.permanent_impact = 0.005; });
  add("impact exponent 1.5", [](ExecutionParams& p) { p.impact_exponent = 1.5; });
  add("fees 0.1 per trade", [](ExecutionParams& p) { p.fixed_cost = 0.1; });
  return s;
}

struct Metrics {
  double gain = 0;          // mean gain over TWAP per episode (price units)
  Interval gain_ci;         // 95% bootstrap interval of the mean gain
  double optimal_gain = 0;  // the scenario's exact optimum's mean gain on the same episodes
  double share = 0;         // gain / optimal_gain (meaningful when optimal_gain > 0)
  double cvar5 = 0;         // mean of the worst 5% of per-episode gains over TWAP
  double p_worse = 0;       // share of episodes that did worse than TWAP
};

// Paired per-episode gains of `policy` over TWAP on episodes seed .. seed+n-1.
template <class Policy>
std::vector<double> gains_over_twap(const ExecutionParams& p, Policy&& policy, std::uint32_t episodes, std::uint64_t seed) {
  const ExecutionEnv env(p);
  auto twap = [](const ExecutionObs&) { return ExecutionEnv::kTwapAction; };
  const auto a = episode_returns(env, policy, episodes, seed);
  const auto b = episode_returns(env, twap, episodes, seed);
  std::vector<double> d(a.size());
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < a.size(); ++i) d[i] = a[i] - b[i];
  return d;
}

// optimal_gain < 0 means "compute it": solve the scenario's DP and score it
// on the same episodes. Pass a precomputed value to measure many strategies.
template <class Policy>
Metrics measure(const ExecutionParams& p, Policy&& policy, std::uint32_t episodes, std::uint64_t seed, double optimal_gain = -1) {
  Metrics m;
  const auto g = gains_over_twap(p, policy, episodes, seed);
  double sum = 0;
  std::size_t worse = 0;
  for (double x : g) {
    sum += x;
    worse += x < 0;
  }
  m.gain = sum / static_cast<double>(g.size());
  m.gain_ci = bootstrap_mean(g, 2000, seed ^ 0x5eed);
  m.cvar5 = cvar(g, 0.05);
  m.p_worse = static_cast<double>(worse) / static_cast<double>(g.size());
  if (optimal_gain < 0) {
    const ExecutionDP dp(p);
    const auto o = gains_over_twap(p, [&](const ExecutionObs& obs) { return dp.act(obs); }, episodes, seed);
    double so = 0;
    for (double x : o) so += x;
    optimal_gain = so / static_cast<double>(o.size());
  }
  m.optimal_gain = optimal_gain;
  m.share = optimal_gain > 0 ? m.gain / optimal_gain : 0;
  return m;
}

}  // namespace rag::agent::validation

// rag/agent/variance_reduction.hpp — remove known-zero-mean noise from
// rewards before a learner sees them (a control variate; E17).
//
// In ExecutionEnv every non-final step's reward contains I' * dS, the
// inventory held through the price move dS = alpha * g + noise. Given the
// state and action, the innovation dS - alpha * g has mean zero, so
//
//     r~ = r - I' * (dS - alpha_hat * g)
//
// has the same expectation as r when alpha_hat = alpha: every policy's value,
// and so the optimal policy, is unchanged, while the dominant source of
// reward noise is gone. What remains is the randomness of the next signal.
//
// alpha_hat is either supplied (an oracle) or estimated online by least
// squares of the observed moves on the signal (market data the agent sees;
// no knowledge of the market is assumed). InnovationControlledEnv wraps
// ExecutionEnv and satisfies the Environment concept, so any learner and the
// Trainer use it unchanged. Score policies on the plain ExecutionEnv.
#pragma once

#include <optional>

#include "rag/agent/env.hpp"

namespace rag::agent {

class InnovationControlledEnv {
 public:
  using Observation = ExecutionObs;
  static constexpr std::size_t kNumActions = ExecutionEnv::kNumActions;
  static constexpr std::size_t kStateDims = ExecutionEnv::kStateDims;
  static constexpr Action kTwapAction = ExecutionEnv::kTwapAction;
  static constexpr std::array<double, 3> kLo = ExecutionEnv::kLo, kHi = ExecutionEnv::kHi;

  explicit InnovationControlledEnv(ExecutionEnv env, std::optional<double> alpha = std::nullopt)
      : env_(std::move(env)), fixed_alpha_(alpha) {}

  Observation reset(Rng& rng) noexcept {
    last_ = env_.reset(rng);
    return last_;
  }

  Step<Observation> step(Action a, Rng& rng) noexcept {
    const double g = last_.signal;
    auto st = env_.step(a, rng);
    const double move = env_.last_move();
    if (move != 0.0 || !st.done) {  // a price move happened while inventory was held
      st.reward -= static_cast<double>(st.obs.inventory) * (move - alpha_hat() * g);
      gm_ += g * move;  // online regression of the move on the signal
      gg_ += g * g;
    }
    last_ = st.obs;
    return st;
  }

  [[nodiscard]] std::array<double, 3> features(const Observation& o) const noexcept { return env_.features(o); }

  // The drift coefficient used for the correction.
  [[nodiscard]] double alpha_hat() const noexcept {
    if (fixed_alpha_) return *fixed_alpha_;
    return gg_ > 0 ? gm_ / gg_ : 0.0;
  }
  [[nodiscard]] const ExecutionEnv& inner() const noexcept { return env_; }
  [[nodiscard]] ExecutionEnv& inner() noexcept { return env_; }

 private:
  ExecutionEnv env_;
  std::optional<double> fixed_alpha_;
  Observation last_{};
  double gm_ = 0, gg_ = 0;
};

static_assert(Environment<InnovationControlledEnv>);

}  // namespace rag::agent

// rag/arena.hpp — monotonic (bump-pointer) arena for document text.
//
// Latency notes:
//  * Allocation is a pointer bump + alignment mask on the common path.
//  * Blocks are never moved or freed until the arena dies, so a pointer handed
//    out once stays valid forever. Readers on other threads can therefore hold
//    std::string_view into the arena without any synchronisation beyond the
//    release/acquire publication of the chunk that references it.
//  * Only the (single) writer thread touches blocks_ / cur_ / end_.
#pragma once

#include <algorithm>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstring>
#include <memory>
#include <string_view>
#include <vector>

#include "rag/common.hpp"

namespace rag {

class Arena {
 public:
  explicit Arena(std::size_t block_bytes = std::size_t{1} << 20) : block_bytes_(block_bytes) {}

  Arena(const Arena&) = delete;
  Arena& operator=(const Arena&) = delete;

  [[nodiscard]] void* allocate(std::size_t bytes, std::size_t align = alignof(std::max_align_t)) {
    // Bounds are checked on integer addresses: forming `p + bytes` past the
    // block (or from the null cur_ of a fresh arena) would itself be UB.
    const auto cur = reinterpret_cast<std::uintptr_t>(cur_);
    const auto end = reinterpret_cast<std::uintptr_t>(end_);
    const auto aligned = (cur + align - 1) & ~(std::uintptr_t{align} - 1);
    if (cur_ != nullptr && aligned <= end && bytes <= end - aligned) [[likely]] {
      auto* p = cur_ + (aligned - cur);
      cur_ = p + bytes;
      used_ += bytes;
      return p;
    }
    return allocate_slow(bytes, align);
  }

  // Copy a string into the arena; the returned view is stable for the arena's lifetime.
  [[nodiscard]] std::string_view copy(std::string_view s) {
    if (s.empty()) return {};
    auto* dst = static_cast<char*>(allocate(s.size(), 1));
    std::memcpy(dst, s.data(), s.size());
    return {dst, s.size()};
  }

  [[nodiscard]] std::size_t bytes_used() const noexcept { return used_; }
  [[nodiscard]] std::size_t blocks() const noexcept { return blocks_.size(); }

 private:
  void* allocate_slow(std::size_t bytes, std::size_t align) {
    const std::size_t size = std::max(block_bytes_, bytes + align);
    blocks_.push_back(make_aligned_array<std::byte>(size, Init::Lazy));
    cur_ = blocks_.back().get();
    end_ = cur_ + size;
    return allocate(bytes, align);
  }

  std::size_t block_bytes_;
  std::vector<AlignedArray<std::byte>> blocks_;
  std::byte* cur_ = nullptr;
  std::byte* end_ = nullptr;
  std::size_t used_ = 0;
};

}  // namespace rag

// rag/bm25.hpp — lexical retrieval: BM25 over a frozen, impact-scored
// inverted index.
//
// Build (cold): Bm25Builder collects (term, doc, tf) triples; freeze() sorts
// them and precomputes, per posting, the full BM25 contribution
//     w = idf(t) * tf * (k1 + 1) / (tf + k1 * (1 - b + b * |d| / avgdl))
// ("impact scoring"). Query-time work per posting is then one gather-add —
// no division, no document-length lookup.
//
// Layout:
//   * term dictionary: open-addressing table (power-of-two capacity, linear
//     probing, load factor <= 0.5) of {hash, offset, len} — one or two
//     cache lines per lookup.
//   * postings: SoA arrays doc_[] (u32) and weight_[] (f32), contiguous per
//     term and sorted by doc id, so accumulation streams sequentially.
// Query scratch (dense accumulator + touched list) lives in Bm25Scratch,
// allocated once per query thread; queries never allocate.
#pragma once

#include <algorithm>
#include <array>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdint>
#include <memory>
#include <span>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <vector>

#include "rag/common.hpp"
#include "rag/topk.hpp"

namespace rag {

struct Bm25Params {
  float k1 = 1.2f;
  float b = 0.75f;
};

// Per-thread query scratch. acc[] is all zero between queries (invariant).
struct Bm25Scratch {
  explicit Bm25Scratch(std::uint32_t max_docs)
      : acc(make_aligned_array<float>(max_docs)), touched(make_aligned_array<std::uint32_t>(max_docs)), capacity(max_docs) {}
  AlignedArray<float> acc;
  AlignedArray<std::uint32_t> touched;
  std::uint32_t capacity;
};

class Bm25Index {
 public:
  static constexpr std::size_t kMaxQueryTerms = 256;

  // `terms`: query term hashes (duplicates allowed; each distinct term counts once).
  // Documents with id >= scratch.capacity are ignored (cannot happen when the
  // scratch was sized from the engine's max_chunks).
  template <class TK>
  void search(std::span<const std::uint64_t> terms, Bm25Scratch& sc, TK& out) const noexcept {
    if (num_docs_ == 0 || terms.empty()) return;
    std::array<std::uint64_t, kMaxQueryTerms> uniq;
    const std::size_t nt = std::min(terms.size(), kMaxQueryTerms);
    std::copy_n(terms.begin(), nt, uniq.begin());
    std::sort(uniq.begin(), uniq.begin() + nt);
    const std::size_t nu = static_cast<std::size_t>(std::unique(uniq.begin(), uniq.begin() + nt) - uniq.begin());

    float* RAG_RESTRICT acc = sc.acc.get();
    std::uint32_t* RAG_RESTRICT touched = sc.touched.get();
    std::uint32_t ntouched = 0;
    for (std::size_t t = 0; t < nu; ++t) {
      const Slot* s = find(uniq[t]);
      if (!s) continue;
      const std::uint32_t* d = doc_.data() + s->offset;
      const float* w = weight_.data() + s->offset;
      for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < s->len; ++i) {
        const std::uint32_t doc = d[i];
        if (doc >= sc.capacity) [[unlikely]] continue;
        // Weights are > 0, so acc == 0 means "first touch this query".
        if (acc[doc] == 0.f) touched[ntouched++] = doc;
        acc[doc] += w[i];
      }
    }
    for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < ntouched; ++i) {  // select + restore the all-zero invariant
      const std::uint32_t doc = touched[i];
      out.push(acc[doc], doc);
      acc[doc] = 0.f;
    }
  }

  [[nodiscard]] std::uint32_t num_docs() const noexcept { return num_docs_; }
  [[nodiscard]] std::size_t num_terms() const noexcept { return num_terms_; }
  [[nodiscard]] std::size_t num_postings() const noexcept { return doc_.size(); }

  // Persistence (see rag/io.hpp). load() checks every offset and doc id, so
  // a damaged file can never produce an out-of-bounds read at query time.
  template <class W>
  void save(W& w) const {
    w.vec(table_);
    w.pod(static_cast<std::uint64_t>(num_terms_));
    w.pod(num_docs_);
    w.vec(doc_);
    w.vec(weight_);
  }
  template <class R>
  void load(R& r) {
    auto table = r.template vec<Slot>();
    const auto nterms = r.template pod<std::uint64_t>();
    const auto ndocs = r.template pod<std::uint32_t>();
    auto doc = r.template vec<std::uint32_t>();
    auto weight = r.template vec<float>();
    const bool pow2 = !table.empty() && (table.size() & (table.size() - 1)) == 0;
    if (!(table.empty() || pow2) || doc.size() != weight.size() || nterms > table.size())
      throw std::runtime_error("Bm25Index::load: inconsistent index");
    std::size_t used = 0;
    for (const Slot& s : table) {
      if (s.key == 0) continue;
      ++used;
      if (std::uint64_t{s.offset} + s.len > doc.size()) throw std::runtime_error("Bm25Index::load: posting range out of bounds");
    }
    if (used != nterms || (!table.empty() && used == table.size()))  // a full table would make lookups loop forever
      throw std::runtime_error("Bm25Index::load: bad term table");
    for (auto d : doc)
      if (d >= ndocs) throw std::runtime_error("Bm25Index::load: doc id out of range");
    // search() relies on every weight being > 0 (acc == 0 marks a first touch,
    // which bounds the touched list); freeze() never produces anything else.
    for (float x : weight)
      if (!(x > 0.f) || !std::isfinite(x)) throw std::runtime_error("Bm25Index::load: bad posting weight");
    table_ = std::move(table);
    mask_ = table_.empty() ? 0 : table_.size() - 1;
    num_terms_ = static_cast<std::size_t>(nterms);
    num_docs_ = ndocs;
    doc_ = std::move(doc);
    weight_ = std::move(weight);
  }

  // Raw lookup (tests / debugging): document frequency of a term.
  [[nodiscard]] std::uint32_t doc_freq(std::uint64_t term) const noexcept {
    const Slot* s = find(term);
    return s ? s->len : 0;
  }

 private:
  friend class Bm25Builder;

  struct Slot {
    std::uint64_t key;  // 0 = empty (real hashes remapped away from 0)
    std::uint32_t offset;
    std::uint32_t len;
  };
  static constexpr std::uint64_t remap(std::uint64_t h) noexcept { return h ? h : 1; }

  const Slot* find(std::uint64_t h) const noexcept {
    if (table_.empty()) return nullptr;
    h = remap(h);
    for (std::size_t i = h & mask_;; i = (i + 1) & mask_) {
      const Slot& s = table_[i];
      if (s.key == h) return &s;
      if (s.key == 0) return nullptr;
    }
  }

  std::vector<Slot> table_;
  std::size_t mask_ = 0;
  std::size_t num_terms_ = 0;
  std::uint32_t num_docs_ = 0;
  std::vector<std::uint32_t> doc_;
  std::vector<float> weight_;
};

class Bm25Builder {
 public:
  // Add one document (chunk). `terms` may contain duplicates (that is the tf).
  void add(std::uint32_t doc, std::span<const std::uint64_t> terms) {
    scratch_.assign(terms.begin(), terms.end());
    std::sort(scratch_.begin(), scratch_.end());
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < scratch_.size();) {
      std::size_t j = i;
      while (j < scratch_.size() && scratch_[j] == scratch_[i]) ++j;
      triples_.push_back({scratch_[i], doc, static_cast<std::uint32_t>(j - i)});
      i = j;
    }
    if (doc >= doc_len_.size()) doc_len_.resize(doc + 1, 0);
    doc_len_[doc] = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(terms.size());
    num_docs_ = std::max(num_docs_, doc + 1);
  }

  [[nodiscard]] Bm25Index freeze(Bm25Params p = {}) const {
    Bm25Index idx;
    idx.num_docs_ = num_docs_;
    if (triples_.empty()) return idx;

    std::vector<Triple> t = triples_;
    std::sort(t.begin(), t.end(), [](const Triple& a, const Triple& b) {
      return a.term != b.term ? a.term < b.term : a.doc < b.doc;
    });

    double total_len = 0;
    for (auto l : doc_len_) total_len += l;
    const double avgdl = std::max(1.0, total_len / std::max<std::uint32_t>(1, num_docs_));
    const double N = num_docs_;

    std::size_t nterms = 0;
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < t.size(); ++i) nterms += (i == 0 || t[i].term != t[i - 1].term);
    std::size_t cap = 16;
    while (cap < nterms * 2) cap <<= 1;
    idx.table_.assign(cap, Bm25Index::Slot{0, 0, 0});
    idx.mask_ = cap - 1;
    idx.num_terms_ = nterms;
    idx.doc_.resize(t.size());
    idx.weight_.resize(t.size());

    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < t.size();) {
      std::size_t j = i;
      while (j < t.size() && t[j].term == t[i].term) ++j;
      const double df = static_cast<double>(j - i);
      const double idf = std::log(1.0 + (N - df + 0.5) / (df + 0.5));  // Lucene BM25: always > 0
      for (std::size_t k = i; k < j; ++k) {
        const double tf = t[k].tf;
        const double norm = p.k1 * (1.0 - p.b + p.b * static_cast<double>(doc_len_[t[k].doc]) / avgdl);
        idx.doc_[k] = t[k].doc;
        idx.weight_[k] = static_cast<float>(idf * tf * (p.k1 + 1.0) / (tf + norm));
      }
      const std::uint64_t key = Bm25Index::remap(t[i].term);
      std::size_t s = key & idx.mask_;
      while (idx.table_[s].key != 0) s = (s + 1) & idx.mask_;
      idx.table_[s] = {key, static_cast<std::uint32_t>(i), static_cast<std::uint32_t>(j - i)};
      i = j;
    }
    return idx;
  }

  [[nodiscard]] std::uint32_t num_docs() const noexcept { return num_docs_; }

  // Persistence (see rag/io.hpp). load() validates every doc id it reads.
  template <class W>
  void save(W& w) const {
    w.vec(triples_);
    w.vec(doc_len_);
    w.pod(num_docs_);
  }
  template <class R>
  void load(R& r) {
    auto t = r.template vec<Triple>();
    auto dl = r.template vec<std::uint32_t>();
    const auto nd = r.template pod<std::uint32_t>();
    if (dl.size() != nd) throw std::runtime_error("Bm25Builder::load: doc length table does not match doc count");
    for (const Triple& x : t)
      if (x.doc >= nd || x.tf == 0) throw std::runtime_error("Bm25Builder::load: invalid posting");
    triples_ = std::move(t);
    doc_len_ = std::move(dl);
    num_docs_ = nd;
  }

 private:
  struct Triple {
    std::uint64_t term;
    std::uint32_t doc;
    std::uint32_t tf;
  };
  std::vector<Triple> triples_;
  std::vector<std::uint32_t> doc_len_;
  std::vector<std::uint64_t> scratch_;  // reused across add() calls
  std::uint32_t num_docs_ = 0;
};

}  // namespace rag

// rag/chunker.hpp — sliding-window chunking over token boundaries.
//
// Chunks are byte ranges into the original text, so chunk text is a
// zero-copy std::string_view into the arena that owns the document.
#pragma once

#include <cstdint>
#include <span>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <string_view>

#include "rag/tokenizer.hpp"

namespace rag {

struct ChunkerConfig {
  std::uint32_t window_tokens = 128;
  std::uint32_t overlap_tokens = 32;

  constexpr void validate() const {
    if (window_tokens == 0 || overlap_tokens >= window_tokens)
      throw std::invalid_argument("ChunkerConfig: need 0 <= overlap < window");
  }
};

constexpr bool is_space(char c) noexcept { return c == ' ' || c == '\n' || c == '\t' || c == '\r' || c == '\f' || c == '\v'; }

struct ChunkRange {
  std::uint32_t token_begin, token_end;  // [begin, end) into the token array
  std::uint32_t byte_begin, byte_end;    // [begin, end) into the source text
};

// Calls emit(ChunkRange) for every window over `toks` (the tokens of `text`).
// Windows advance by (window - overlap) tokens and the last window ends at the
// last token. A chunk's bytes run from its first token up to the next token
// (or end of text), minus trailing whitespace, so trailing punctuation such as
// "." or ")" stays with the sentence it ends.
template <class F>
constexpr void chunk_tokens(std::string_view text, std::span<const Token> toks, const ChunkerConfig& cfg, F&& emit) {
  const auto n = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(toks.size());
  if (n == 0) return;
  const std::uint32_t stride = cfg.window_tokens - cfg.overlap_tokens;
  for (std::uint32_t begin = 0;; begin += stride) {
    const std::uint32_t end = begin + cfg.window_tokens < n ? begin + cfg.window_tokens : n;
    std::uint32_t byte_end = end < n ? toks[end].offset : static_cast<std::uint32_t>(text.size());
    const std::uint32_t min_end = toks[end - 1].offset + toks[end - 1].length;
    while (byte_end > min_end && is_space(text[byte_end - 1])) --byte_end;
    emit(ChunkRange{begin, end, toks[begin].offset, byte_end});
    if (end == n) break;
  }
}

}  // namespace rag

// rag/common.hpp — shared primitives: cache-line constants, aligned buffers, hints.
#pragma once

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <memory>
#include <new>
#include <type_traits>

#if defined(__linux__)
#include <sys/mman.h>
#endif
#if defined(_WIN32)
#include <malloc.h>  // _aligned_malloc / _aligned_free (MSVC has no std::aligned_alloc)
#endif
#if defined(_MSC_VER) && !defined(__clang__) && (defined(_M_X64) || defined(_M_IX86))
#include <xmmintrin.h>  // _mm_prefetch
#endif

namespace rag {

// std::hardware_destructive_interference_size is 64 on every x86-64 part we
// target, but GCC warns that using it in a header is an ABI hazard
// (-Winterference-size), so we spell the value out and check it where we can.
inline constexpr std::size_t kCacheLine = 64;
#if defined(__cpp_lib_hardware_interference_size) && defined(__x86_64__) && !defined(__GNUC__)
static_assert(std::hardware_destructive_interference_size == kCacheLine);
#endif

inline constexpr std::size_t kHugePage = std::size_t{2} << 20;  // 2 MiB

#if defined(__GNUC__) || defined(__clang__)
#define RAG_ALWAYS_INLINE inline __attribute__((always_inline))
#define RAG_RESTRICT __restrict__
#define RAG_PREFETCH(p) __builtin_prefetch((p), 0, 3)
#elif defined(_MSC_VER)
#define RAG_ALWAYS_INLINE __forceinline
#define RAG_RESTRICT __restrict
#if defined(_M_X64) || defined(_M_IX86)
#define RAG_PREFETCH(p) _mm_prefetch(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(p), _MM_HINT_T0)
#else
#define RAG_PREFETCH(p) ((void)0)
#endif
#else
#define RAG_ALWAYS_INLINE inline
#define RAG_RESTRICT
#define RAG_PREFETCH(p) ((void)0)
#endif

// The AVX2 kernels also need FMA. GCC and Clang define __FMA__ (with
// -march=x86-64-v3 or native on any AVX2 CPU); MSVC's /arch:AVX2 generates
// FMA instructions but defines no macro for them.
#if defined(__AVX2__) && (defined(__FMA__) || (defined(_MSC_VER) && !defined(__clang__)))
#define RAG_AVX2_FMA 1
#endif

// Dimensions must be a multiple of 64 so every SIMD kernel runs with no
// scalar tail: 64 fp32 = 4 AVX-512 regs; 64 int8 = 1 AVX-512 reg / 2 AVX2 regs.
template <std::size_t D>
concept ValidDim = (D > 0) && (D % 64 == 0);

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// AlignedArray: one up-front allocation, cache-line (or huge-page) aligned.
//
// Init::Prefault zeroes the whole array now, so every page is mapped before
// the first query. Use it for memory that queries *write* at arbitrary
// offsets (scratch accumulators, prompt buffers), where a first-touch page
// fault would land on a query's latency.
//
// Init::Lazy leaves the memory uninitialised and unmapped until first write.
// Use it for storage the writer always fills before publishing it (vectors,
// chunk metadata, index arrays): readers then never touch an unwritten page,
// pages are faulted in by the writer as it goes, and memory for unused
// capacity is never committed at all.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
enum class Init : std::uint8_t { Prefault, Lazy };

struct FreeDeleter {
  void operator()(void* p) const noexcept {
#if defined(_WIN32)
    _aligned_free(p);
#else
    std::free(p);
#endif
  }
};

template <class T>
using AlignedArray = std::unique_ptr<T[], FreeDeleter>;

template <class T>
[[nodiscard]] AlignedArray<T> make_aligned_array(std::size_t n, Init init = Init::Prefault) {
  static_assert(std::is_trivially_copyable_v<T> && std::is_trivially_destructible_v<T>,
                "AlignedArray holds raw POD storage only");
  const std::size_t bytes = n * sizeof(T);
  // Big buffers (embedding matrices) get 2 MiB alignment so the kernel can
  // back them with transparent huge pages: one TLB entry per 2 MiB instead of
  // 512, which matters when a flat scan streams hundreds of MB.
  const std::size_t align = bytes >= kHugePage ? kHugePage : kCacheLine;
  const std::size_t rounded = ((bytes ? bytes : 1) + align - 1) / align * align;
#if defined(_WIN32)
  void* p = _aligned_malloc(rounded, align);
#else
  void* p = std::aligned_alloc(align, rounded);
#endif
  if (!p) throw std::bad_alloc{};
#if defined(__linux__) && defined(MADV_HUGEPAGE) && !defined(RAG_NO_HUGEPAGES)
  if (align == kHugePage) ::madvise(p, rounded, MADV_HUGEPAGE);
#endif
  if (init == Init::Prefault) std::memset(p, 0, rounded);  // map every page now (cold path)
  return AlignedArray<T>(static_cast<T*>(p));
}

}  // namespace rag

// rag/embedder.hpp — the Embedder concept plus a deterministic, model-free
// reference implementation (signed feature hashing of unigrams + bigrams).
//
// The engine depends only on the concept, so a production deployment swaps
// HashingEmbedder for an ONNX Runtime / llama.cpp / TensorRT sentence
// encoder with the same signature. The hashing embedder is useful in its own
// right: zero model load time, ~100 ns per query, and fully reproducible
// tests.
#pragma once

#include <concepts>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <span>
#include <string_view>

#include "rag/common.hpp"
#include "rag/simd.hpp"
#include "rag/tokenizer.hpp"

namespace rag {

// Writes an L2-normalised D-dim embedding of `text` (whose tokens are
// pre-computed) into `out`. Must not allocate: it runs on the query path.
template <class E>
concept Embedder = requires(const E& e, std::string_view text, std::span<const Token> toks,
                            std::span<float, E::kDim> out) {
  requires ValidDim<E::kDim>;
  { e.embed(text, toks, out) } noexcept;
};

// Identity of an embedding model, stored in index files so that vectors made
// by one model are never searched with queries embedded by another. An
// embedder opts in with `static constexpr std::string_view kName`; bump the
// name whenever its output changes.
template <class E>
constexpr std::uint64_t embedder_tag() noexcept {
  std::uint64_t h = 14695981039346656037ull;
  if constexpr (requires { E::kName; })
    for (char c : std::string_view(E::kName)) h = (h ^ static_cast<unsigned char>(c)) * 1099511628211ull;
  return detail::mix64(h ^ E::kDim);
}

template <std::size_t D>
  requires ValidDim<D>
class HashingEmbedder {
 public:
  static constexpr std::size_t kDim = D;
  static constexpr std::string_view kName = "rag.hashing-unigram-bigram.v1";

  void embed(std::string_view /*text*/, std::span<const Token> toks, std::span<float, D> out) const noexcept {
    for (auto& v : out) v = 0.f;
    std::uint64_t prev = 0;
    for (const Token& t : toks) {
      if (is_stopword(t.hash)) continue;
      add(out, t.hash, 1.0f);
      if (prev) add(out, detail::mix64(prev * 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15ull ^ t.hash), 0.5f);  // bigram
      prev = t.hash;
    }
    simd::normalize(out.data(), D);
  }

 private:
  static RAG_ALWAYS_INLINE void add(std::span<float, D> out, std::uint64_t h, float w) noexcept {
    // Lemire fast-range: maps 32 hash bits into [0, D) without a division.
    const auto idx = static_cast<std::size_t>((std::uint64_t{static_cast<std::uint32_t>(h)} * D) >> 32);
    out[idx] += (h >> 63) ? -w : w;  // signed hashing keeps collisions unbiased
  }
};

static_assert(Embedder<HashingEmbedder<384>>);

}  // namespace rag

// rag/engine.hpp — the RAG pipeline: ingest -> chunk -> embed -> index,
// and query -> embed -> {dense ANN, BM25} -> RRF -> prompt.
//
//   INGEST (single writer, cold-ish path)          QUERY (N readers, hot path, zero alloc)
//   ─────────────────────────────────────          ──────────────────────────────────────────
//   text ─► Arena copy (stable string_view)        query ─► tokenize (stack buffer)
//        ─► tokenize + sliding-window chunk              ─► embed (stack, L1-resident)
//        ─► Embedder ─► VectorStore.append ──┐          ├─► dense: Exact | Int8+rerank | IVF + delta scan
//        ─► Bm25Builder.add                  │          └─► BM25: impact-scored postings
//   commit() ─► build Snapshot{BM25, IVF}    │               ─► RRF fusion (stack)
//            ─► atomic exchange + EBR retire │               ─► prompt into preallocated buffer
//            release-store(size) ────────────┴─► acquire-load(size): new chunks are visible
//                                                 to dense search immediately (NRT), and to
//                                                 BM25/IVF after the next commit().
//
// Thread-safety contract
//   * Writer side, ingest() and commit(): one thread at a time (externally serialised).
//   * query(): any number of threads, concurrently with ingest() AND commit().
//     Each thread owns one QueryContext (at most EpochDomain::kMaxReaders live).
//   * commit() builds a new immutable Snapshot off to the side, publishes it
//     with one atomic exchange, and retires the old one through epoch-based
//     reclamation. Queries never block, and never see a half-built index.
//   * QueryContexts must be destroyed before the engine.
#pragma once

#include <algorithm>
#include <array>
#include <concepts>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdint>
#include <filesystem>
#include <fstream>
#include <limits>
#include <memory>
#include <span>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <unordered_map>
#include <unordered_set>
#include <vector>

#include "rag/arena.hpp"
#include "rag/bm25.hpp"
#include "rag/chunker.hpp"
#include "rag/common.hpp"
#include "rag/embedder.hpp"
#include "rag/epoch.hpp"
#include "rag/fusion.hpp"
#include "rag/io.hpp"
#include "rag/ivf_index.hpp"
#include "rag/prompt.hpp"
#include "rag/tokenizer.hpp"
#include "rag/topk.hpp"
#include "rag/vector_store.hpp"

namespace rag {

enum class DenseMode : std::uint8_t {
  Exact,       // fp32 brute force (SIMD, register-blocked) — ground truth
  Int8Rerank,  // int8 scan -> fp32 rerank of a shortlist: ~4x less memory traffic
  Ivf,         // IVF-Flat over the committed snapshot + exact scan of the uncommitted delta
  IvfInt8,     // IVF-SQ8 shortlist -> fp32 rerank, + exact scan of the uncommitted delta
};

struct EngineConfig {
  std::uint32_t max_chunks = 1u << 16;
  ChunkerConfig chunker{};
  Bm25Params bm25{};
  RrfParams rrf{};
  PromptParams prompt{};
  DenseMode dense_mode = DenseMode::Exact;
  bool hybrid = true;                    // fuse BM25 with dense; false => dense only
  // Dense hits must score strictly above this cosine similarity. The default
  // 0 drops rows that share nothing with the query (orthogonal or opposite),
  // including empty-content chunks whose embedding is all zeros. Use -2 to
  // keep every row, or raise it to demand a minimum relevance.
  float dense_min_score = 0.f;
  std::uint32_t retrieve_depth = 32;     // per-retriever list depth fed to RRF
  std::uint32_t rerank_candidates = 128; // Int8Rerank / IvfInt8 shortlist size
  std::uint32_t nprobe = 8;              // Ivf / IvfInt8 lists probed per query
  IvfParams ivf{};
  std::size_t prompt_capacity = 32 * 1024;
};

// Optional per-document metadata for ingest().
struct IngestOptions {
  // Where the text came from, e.g. a file name. Shown in citations; stored
  // once per distinct value however many chunks share it.
  std::string_view source{};
  // Byte offsets into the text at which each page begins: page_starts[0] must
  // be 0 (page 1), and offsets must increase. Each chunk records the 1-based
  // pages it spans. Empty means the text has no page structure.
  std::span<const std::uint32_t> page_starts{};
};

// What an index file holds, read from its header alone (see RagEngine::inspect).
struct IndexInfo {
  std::uint32_t format_version;
  std::uint32_t dim;
  std::uint32_t chunks;
  std::uint64_t text_bytes;
};

// A generator consumes the assembled prompt (llama.cpp, vLLM over HTTP, ...).
template <class G>
concept Generator = requires(G& g, std::string_view prompt) { g.generate(prompt); };

template <Embedder E, std::size_t MaxK = 64>
class RagEngine {
 public:
  // Everything commit() publishes. Immutable once reachable from snap_.
  struct Snapshot {
    Bm25Index bm25;
    IvfIndex<E::kDim> ivf;
    std::uint32_t covered = 0;  // chunks [0, covered) are in bm25 / ivf
    std::uint64_t version = 0;  // number of commits that produced it
  };

  static constexpr std::size_t D = E::kDim;
  static constexpr std::size_t kMaxK = MaxK;
  static constexpr std::size_t kMaxQueryTokens = 256;
  static constexpr std::size_t kMaxRerank = 1024;

  struct ChunkMeta {
    const char* text;
    std::uint32_t len;
    std::uint32_t doc_id;
    std::uint32_t ordinal;
    std::uint32_t page_first;  // 0 = no page information
    std::uint32_t page_last;
    std::uint32_t source_len;
    const char* source;        // arena-owned, shared by every chunk of the same source
  };

  // All per-query scratch. Create one per query thread, reuse forever.
  class QueryContext {
   public:
    QueryContext(QueryContext&&) noexcept = default;
   private:
    friend class RagEngine;
    QueryContext(EpochDomain::Reader r, std::uint32_t max_chunks, std::size_t prompt_cap)
        : reader(std::move(r)), bm25(max_chunks), prompt_buf(make_aligned_array<char>(prompt_cap)),
          prompt_cap(prompt_cap) {}
    EpochDomain::Reader reader;  // this thread's reclamation slot
    alignas(kCacheLine) std::array<float, D> qvec{};
    alignas(kCacheLine) std::array<std::int8_t, D> qvec_i8{};
    std::array<Token, kMaxQueryTokens> tokens{};
    std::array<std::uint64_t, kMaxQueryTokens> terms{};
    std::array<Hit, MaxK> dense{}, lexical{}, fused{};
    std::size_t nterms = 0;
    bool has_signal = false;
    TopK<kMaxRerank> cand{};
    Bm25Scratch bm25;
    AlignedArray<char> prompt_buf;
    std::size_t prompt_cap;
  };

  struct QueryResult {
    std::span<const Hit> hits;     // fused (or dense-only) ranking, best first
    std::span<const Hit> dense;    // dense retriever's list (cosine scores)
    std::span<const Hit> lexical;  // BM25 list
    PromptResult prompt;
    std::uint64_t snapshot_version = 0;  // which commit the lexical/IVF results came from
  };

  // Pins the current snapshot for as long as it lives, e.g. to run several
  // reads against one consistent index version. Nestable with query() on the
  // same context. Keep it short-lived: it holds back reclamation.
  class PinnedSnapshot {
   public:
    PinnedSnapshot(const RagEngine& e, QueryContext& ctx) noexcept
        : guard_(e.epochs_, *ctx.reader.slot()), snap_(e.snap_.load(std::memory_order_seq_cst)) {}
    const Snapshot& operator*() const noexcept { return *snap_; }
    const Snapshot* operator->() const noexcept { return snap_; }

   private:
    EpochDomain::Guard guard_;  // must be constructed before snap_ is loaded
    const Snapshot* snap_;
  };

  explicit RagEngine(EngineConfig cfg = {}, E embedder = {})
      : cfg_(validated(cfg)), embedder_(std::move(embedder)), store_(cfg_.max_chunks),
        meta_(make_aligned_array<ChunkMeta>(cfg_.max_chunks, Init::Lazy)), snap_(new Snapshot{}) {}

  RagEngine(const RagEngine&) = delete;
  RagEngine& operator=(const RagEngine&) = delete;

  ~RagEngine() {
    delete snap_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    for (auto& r : retired_) delete r.snap;
  }

  // Cold path: claims a reclamation slot and allocates per-thread scratch.
  [[nodiscard]] QueryContext make_context() const {
    return QueryContext(epochs_.register_reader(), cfg_.max_chunks, cfg_.prompt_capacity);
  }
  [[nodiscard]] PinnedSnapshot pin(QueryContext& ctx) const noexcept { return PinnedSnapshot(*this, ctx); }

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- ingest
  // Single writer. Returns the number of chunks added (fewer than the
  // document produced if capacity ran out).
  std::uint32_t ingest(std::string_view text, std::uint32_t doc_id, const IngestOptions& opt = {}) {
    // Validate before mutating anything, so a bad call leaves the engine untouched.
    const auto pages = opt.page_starts;
    if (!pages.empty()) {
      if (pages[0] != 0) throw std::invalid_argument("IngestOptions::page_starts must start at 0");
      for (std::size_t i = 1; i < pages.size(); ++i)
        if (pages[i] <= pages[i - 1]) throw std::invalid_argument("IngestOptions::page_starts must increase");
      if (pages.back() > text.size()) throw std::invalid_argument("IngestOptions::page_starts beyond the text");
    }
    const std::string_view source = intern_source(opt.source);
    // 1-based page holding byte `b`.
    auto page_of = [&](std::uint32_t b) -> std::uint32_t {
      if (pages.empty()) return 0;
      return static_cast<std::uint32_t>(std::upper_bound(pages.begin(), pages.end(), b) - pages.begin());
    };

    const std::string_view doc = arena_.copy(text);
    tokens_.clear();
    for_each_token(doc, [&](const Token& t) { tokens_.push_back(t); });

    std::uint32_t added = 0, ordinal = 0;
    bool full = false;
    chunk_tokens(doc, tokens_, cfg_.chunker, [&](const ChunkRange& r) {
      if (full) return;
      const std::uint32_t id = store_.size();
      if (id >= cfg_.max_chunks) { full = true; return; }
      const std::string_view ctext = doc.substr(r.byte_begin, r.byte_end - r.byte_begin);

      // Rebase token offsets so they are relative to the chunk text (Embedder contract).
      chunk_toks_.clear();
      terms_.clear();
      for (std::uint32_t i = r.token_begin; i < r.token_end; ++i) {
        Token t = tokens_[i];
        t.offset -= r.byte_begin;
        chunk_toks_.push_back(t);
        if (!is_stopword(t.hash)) terms_.push_back(t.hash);
      }
      embedder_.embed(ctext, chunk_toks_, std::span<float, D>(vec_));
      builder_.add(id, terms_);
      meta_[id] = {ctext.data(),     static_cast<std::uint32_t>(ctext.size()),
                   doc_id,           ordinal++,
                   page_of(r.byte_begin), page_of(r.byte_end - 1),
                   static_cast<std::uint32_t>(source.size()), source.data()};
      store_.append(vec_);  // release-publishes meta_[id] and the row together
      ++added;
    });
    return added;
  }

  // Freeze lexical index (and IVF) over everything ingested so far and
  // publish it atomically. Safe to run while queries are in flight: the
  // expensive build happens before the swap, so the readers' only cost is
  // that their next query sees the new snapshot.
  void commit() {
    const std::uint32_t n = store_.size();
    const Snapshot* prev = snap_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);  // writer owns snap_ stores
    auto next = std::make_unique<Snapshot>();
    next->bm25 = builder_.freeze(cfg_.bm25);
    if (uses_ivf(cfg_.dense_mode)) next->ivf.build(store_, n, effective_ivf(cfg_));
    next->covered = n;
    next->version = prev->version + 1;

    const Snapshot* old = snap_.exchange(next.release(), std::memory_order_seq_cst);
    retired_.push_back({old, epochs_.advance()});
    committed_.store(n, std::memory_order_release);
    reclaim();
  }

  // ------------------------------------------------------------ persistence
  // Writer side (same thread as ingest/commit). Queries may keep running.
  // Saves chunk text + metadata, fp32 vectors, BM25 builder state, and the
  // current committed snapshot (frozen BM25 + IVF) with the parameters it
  // was built with. load() reuses that snapshot when the new EngineConfig
  // asks for the same index parameters and it covers every chunk; otherwise
  // it rebuilds from the raw data. Either way the result is identical.
  struct LoadReport {
    bool reused_indexes = false;  // false => BM25 / IVF were rebuilt on load
  };

  void save(const std::filesystem::path& path) const {
    const std::uint32_t n = store_.size();
    io::Writer w(path);
    std::uint64_t text_bytes = 0;
    for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) text_bytes += meta_[i].len;
    FileHeader hdr;  // magic comes from the default member initializer
    hdr.version = io::kFormatVersion;
    hdr.dim = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(D);
    hdr.embedder_tag = embedder_tag<E>();
    hdr.n_chunks = n;
    hdr.reserved = 0;
    hdr.text_bytes = text_bytes;
    w.pod(hdr);
    // Sources are interned, so chunks of one source share a pointer: number
    // the distinct pointers and store each name once.
    std::vector<std::uint64_t> src_offsets{0};
    std::vector<char> src_names;
    std::unordered_map<const char*, std::uint32_t> src_index;
    auto source_id = [&](const ChunkMeta& m) -> std::uint32_t {
      if (m.source_len == 0) return kNoSource;
      auto [it, fresh] = src_index.try_emplace(m.source, static_cast<std::uint32_t>(src_index.size()));
      if (fresh) {
        src_names.insert(src_names.end(), m.source, m.source + m.source_len);
        src_offsets.push_back(src_names.size());
      }
      return it->second;
    };
    std::uint64_t off = 0;
    for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
      const ChunkMeta& m = meta_[i];
      ChunkRecord rec{};
      rec.text_offset = off;
      rec.len = m.len;
      rec.doc_id = m.doc_id;
      rec.ordinal = m.ordinal;
      rec.page_first = m.page_first;
      rec.page_last = m.page_last;
      rec.source = source_id(m);
      w.pod(rec);
      off += m.len;
    }
    for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) w.bytes(meta_[i].text, meta_[i].len);
    w.vec(src_offsets);
    w.vec(src_names);
    for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) w.bytes(store_.row(i), D * sizeof(float));
    builder_.save(w);

    // The writer thread is the only one that replaces or frees snapshots,
    // so it can read the current one without pinning.
    const Snapshot& snap = *snap_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
    IndexRecord rec{};
    rec.k1 = cfg_.bm25.k1;
    rec.b = cfg_.bm25.b;
    rec.has_ivf = snap.ivf.nlist() > 0;
    const IvfParams ip = effective_ivf(cfg_);
    rec.nlist = ip.nlist;
    rec.train_iters = ip.train_iters;
    rec.max_train = ip.max_train_points_per_list;
    rec.storage = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(ip.storage);
    rec.seed = ip.seed;
    rec.covered = snap.covered;
    w.pod(rec);
    snap.bm25.save(w);
    snap.ivf.save(w);
    w.commit();
  }

  // Read an index file's header without loading it (e.g. to size max_chunks).
  [[nodiscard]] static IndexInfo inspect(const std::filesystem::path& path) {
    std::ifstream f(path, std::ios::binary);
    FileHeader h;
    if (!f.read(reinterpret_cast<char*>(&h), sizeof h)) throw io::FormatError("not a rag-cpp index file");
    if (std::memcmp(h.magic, io::kMagic, sizeof h.magic) != 0) throw io::FormatError("not a rag-cpp index file");
    return {h.version, h.dim, h.n_chunks, h.text_bytes};
  }

  // Throws io::FormatError for a damaged file, std::invalid_argument for a
  // file that doesn't fit this engine type or configuration.
  [[nodiscard]] static std::unique_ptr<RagEngine> load(const std::filesystem::path& path, EngineConfig cfg = {},
                                                       E embedder = {}, LoadReport* report = nullptr) {
    io::Reader r(path);
    const auto h = r.pod<FileHeader>();
    if (std::memcmp(h.magic, io::kMagic, sizeof h.magic) != 0) throw io::FormatError("not a rag-cpp index file");
    if (h.version != io::kFormatVersion)
      throw io::FormatError("unsupported index format version " + std::to_string(h.version) + " (this build reads " +
                            std::to_string(io::kFormatVersion) + "; re-index the documents)");
    if (h.dim != D) throw std::invalid_argument("index dimension does not match the engine's embedder");
    if (h.embedder_tag != embedder_tag<E>()) throw std::invalid_argument("index was built with a different embedder");
    if (h.n_chunks > cfg.max_chunks) throw std::invalid_argument("index has more chunks than cfg.max_chunks");

    auto e = std::make_unique<RagEngine>(cfg, std::move(embedder));
    std::vector<ChunkRecord> recs(h.n_chunks);
    for (auto& rec : recs) {
      rec = r.pod<ChunkRecord>();
      // Written so it cannot overflow: offset + len could wrap past 2^64 and pass a naive check.
      if (rec.len > h.text_bytes || rec.text_offset > h.text_bytes - rec.len)
        throw io::FormatError("chunk text out of range");
    }
    if (h.text_bytes > r.remaining()) throw io::FormatError("truncated text section");
    auto* text = static_cast<char*>(e->arena_.allocate(static_cast<std::size_t>(h.text_bytes ? h.text_bytes : 1), 1));
    r.bytes(text, static_cast<std::size_t>(h.text_bytes));  // one block for all chunk text

    const auto src_offsets = r.vec<std::uint64_t>();
    const auto src_names = r.vec<char>();
    if (src_offsets.empty() || src_offsets.front() != 0 || src_offsets.back() != src_names.size() ||
        !std::is_sorted(src_offsets.begin(), src_offsets.end()))
      throw io::FormatError("bad source table");
    const auto n_sources = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(src_offsets.size() - 1);
    std::vector<std::string_view> sources(n_sources);
    for (std::uint32_t s = 0; s < n_sources; ++s)  // re-intern so later ingests share these names
      sources[s] = e->intern_source({src_names.data() + src_offsets[s], static_cast<std::size_t>(src_offsets[s + 1] - src_offsets[s])});
    for (const auto& rec : recs) {
      if (rec.source != kNoSource && rec.source >= n_sources) throw io::FormatError("chunk source out of range");
      if (rec.page_first > rec.page_last || (rec.page_first == 0) != (rec.page_last == 0))
        throw io::FormatError("bad chunk page range");
    }
    alignas(kCacheLine) std::array<float, D> row;
    for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < h.n_chunks; ++i) {
      r.bytes(row.data(), D * sizeof(float));
      const ChunkRecord& c = recs[i];
      const std::string_view src = c.source == kNoSource ? std::string_view{} : sources[c.source];
      e->meta_[i] = {text + c.text_offset, c.len, c.doc_id, c.ordinal, c.page_first, c.page_last,
                     static_cast<std::uint32_t>(src.size()), src.data()};
      e->store_.append(row);
    }
    e->builder_.load(r);
    if (e->builder_.num_docs() != h.n_chunks) throw io::FormatError("lexical index does not match chunk count");

    const auto rec = r.pod<IndexRecord>();
    if (rec.covered > h.n_chunks) throw io::FormatError("saved snapshot covers more chunks than the file holds");
    auto snap = std::make_unique<Snapshot>();
    snap->bm25.load(r);
    snap->ivf.load(r, rec.covered);
    if (snap->bm25.num_docs() != rec.covered || snap->ivf.covered() > rec.covered)
      throw io::FormatError("saved snapshot is inconsistent");
    r.finish();  // checksum verified before anything is published

    const IvfParams ip = effective_ivf(e->cfg_);
    const bool bm25_ok = rec.covered == h.n_chunks && rec.k1 == e->cfg_.bm25.k1 && rec.b == e->cfg_.bm25.b;
    const bool ivf_ok = !uses_ivf(e->cfg_.dense_mode) ||
                        (rec.has_ivf && snap->ivf.covered() == h.n_chunks && rec.nlist == ip.nlist &&
                         rec.train_iters == ip.train_iters && rec.max_train == ip.max_train_points_per_list &&
                         rec.seed == ip.seed && rec.storage == static_cast<std::uint8_t>(ip.storage));
    const bool reuse = bm25_ok && ivf_ok;
    if (reuse) {
      if (!uses_ivf(e->cfg_.dense_mode)) snap->ivf = IvfIndex<D>{};  // not needed in this mode: free it
      snap->covered = h.n_chunks;
      snap->version = 1;
      delete e->snap_.exchange(snap.release(), std::memory_order_seq_cst);  // no readers exist yet
      e->committed_.store(h.n_chunks, std::memory_order_release);
    } else {
      e->commit();
    }
    if (report) report->reused_indexes = reuse;
    return e;
  }

  // Writer: free retired snapshots no reader can still see. commit() calls
  // this itself; call it directly to release memory without committing.
  // Returns the number of snapshots still waiting for readers to move on.
  std::size_t reclaim() {
    std::erase_if(retired_, [&](const Retired& r) {
      if (!epochs_.quiescent_since(r.epoch)) return false;
      delete r.snap;
      return true;
    });
    return retired_.size();
  }

  // ----------------------------------------------------------------- query
  // Hot path: no heap allocation, no locks, no syscalls.
  QueryResult query(std::string_view q, std::uint32_t k, QueryContext& ctx) const noexcept {
    k = std::min<std::uint32_t>(k, MaxK);
    prepare(q, ctx);
    const PinnedSnapshot snap(*this, ctx);    // EBR pin: snapshot can't be freed under us
    const std::uint32_t live = store_.size();  // acquire: sees every published chunk
    TopK<MaxK> dense;
    dense.reset(depth_for(k), dense_floor());
    if (ctx.has_signal) [[likely]] dense_one(*snap, live, ctx, dense);
    return finish(q, k, *snap, dense, ctx);
  }

  // Answer several queries at once. Results are identical to calling query()
  // on each, but in Exact and Int8Rerank modes every group of up to
  // kMaxBatch queries shares ONE pass over the vector matrix, which is what
  // bounds those modes (DRAM bandwidth). IVF modes probe different lists per
  // query, so they run per query. Needs one QueryContext per query; result i
  // points into ctxs[i]. No heap allocation.
  static constexpr std::size_t kMaxBatch = VectorStore<D>::kMaxBatch;

  void query_batch(std::span<const std::string_view> qs, std::uint32_t k, std::span<QueryContext> ctxs,
                   std::span<QueryResult> out) const noexcept {
    k = std::min<std::uint32_t>(k, MaxK);
    const std::size_t n = std::min({qs.size(), ctxs.size(), out.size()});
    for (std::size_t g = 0; g < n; g += kMaxBatch) {
      const std::size_t m = std::min(kMaxBatch, n - g);
      for (std::size_t j = 0; j < m; ++j) prepare(qs[g + j], ctxs[g + j]);
      const PinnedSnapshot snap(*this, ctxs[g]);  // one pin covers the whole group
      const std::uint32_t live = store_.size();
      std::array<TopK<MaxK>, kMaxBatch> dense;
      for (std::size_t j = 0; j < m; ++j) dense[j].reset(depth_for(k), dense_floor());
      dense_batch(*snap, live, ctxs.subspan(g, m), dense);
      for (std::size_t j = 0; j < m; ++j) out[g + j] = finish(qs[g + j], k, *snap, dense[j], ctxs[g + j]);
    }
  }

  // Retrieve, then hand the prompt to a generator.
  template <Generator G>
  QueryResult answer(std::string_view q, std::uint32_t k, QueryContext& ctx, G& gen) const {
    auto r = query(q, k, ctx);
    gen.generate(r.prompt.prompt);
    return r;
  }

  [[nodiscard]] ChunkView chunk(std::uint32_t id) const noexcept {
    const ChunkMeta& m = meta_[id];
    return {{m.text, m.len}, m.doc_id, m.ordinal, {m.source, m.source_len}, m.page_first, m.page_last};
  }
  [[nodiscard]] std::uint32_t size() const noexcept { return store_.size(); }
  [[nodiscard]] std::uint32_t committed() const noexcept { return committed_.load(std::memory_order_acquire); }
  [[nodiscard]] const VectorStore<D>& store() const noexcept { return store_; }
  [[nodiscard]] std::size_t retired_snapshots() const noexcept { return retired_.size(); }  // writer thread
  [[nodiscard]] std::size_t live_readers() const noexcept { return epochs_.readers(); }
  [[nodiscard]] const EngineConfig& config() const noexcept { return cfg_; }
  [[nodiscard]] std::size_t arena_bytes() const noexcept { return arena_.bytes_used(); }

 private:
  // ---------------------------------------------------------- query stages
  std::uint32_t depth_for(std::uint32_t k) const noexcept { return cfg_.hybrid ? cfg_.retrieve_depth : k; }
  // TopK admits score >= floor; the config means strictly greater.
  float dense_floor() const noexcept { return std::nextafter(cfg_.dense_min_score, std::numeric_limits<float>::infinity()); }

  // Tokenize, collect BM25 terms, embed. Writes only ctx.
  void prepare(std::string_view q, QueryContext& ctx) const noexcept {
    const std::size_t ntok = tokenize(q, ctx.tokens);
    ctx.nterms = 0;
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < ntok; ++i)
      if (!is_stopword(ctx.tokens[i].hash)) ctx.terms[ctx.nterms++] = ctx.tokens[i].hash;
    embedder_.embed(q, std::span<const Token>(ctx.tokens.data(), ntok), std::span<float, D>(ctx.qvec));
    // An all-zero query vector carries no signal: dense retrieval is skipped.
    ctx.has_signal = simd::dot(ctx.qvec.data(), ctx.qvec.data(), D) > 0.f;
  }

  void dense_one(const Snapshot& snap, std::uint32_t live, QueryContext& ctx, TopK<MaxK>& dense) const noexcept {
    const float* qv = ctx.qvec.data();
    const std::uint32_t depth = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(dense.k());
    switch (cfg_.dense_mode) {
      case DenseMode::Exact:
        store_.search_exact(qv, 0, live, dense);
        break;
      case DenseMode::Int8Rerank:
        simd::quantize_i8(qv, ctx.qvec_i8.data(), D);
        ctx.cand.reset(std::max(cfg_.rerank_candidates, depth));
        store_.search_two_stage(qv, ctx.qvec_i8.data(), 0, live, ctx.cand, dense);
        break;
      case DenseMode::Ivf: {
        const std::uint32_t base = std::min(snap.ivf.covered(), live);
        snap.ivf.search(qv, cfg_.nprobe, dense);
        store_.search_exact(qv, base, live, dense);  // uncommitted delta segment
        break;
      }
      case DenseMode::IvfInt8: {
        const std::uint32_t base = std::min(snap.ivf.covered(), live);
        simd::quantize_i8(qv, ctx.qvec_i8.data(), D);
        ctx.cand.reset(std::max(cfg_.rerank_candidates, depth));
        snap.ivf.search_int8(qv, ctx.qvec_i8.data(), cfg_.nprobe, ctx.cand);
        for (const Hit& h : ctx.cand.sorted()) dense.push(simd::dot(qv, store_.row(h.id), D), h.id);  // fp32 rerank
        store_.search_exact(qv, base, live, dense);
        break;
      }
    }
  }

  void dense_batch(const Snapshot& snap, std::uint32_t live, std::span<QueryContext> ctxs,
                   std::array<TopK<MaxK>, kMaxBatch>& dense) const noexcept {
    // Gather the queries that have signal; the rest keep empty dense lists.
    std::array<std::size_t, kMaxBatch> idx;
    std::size_t nq = 0;
    for (std::size_t j = 0; j < ctxs.size(); ++j)
      if (ctxs[j].has_signal) idx[nq++] = j;
    if (nq == 0) return;
    if (nq == 1 || cfg_.dense_mode == DenseMode::Ivf || cfg_.dense_mode == DenseMode::IvfInt8) {
      for (std::size_t t = 0; t < nq; ++t) dense_one(snap, live, ctxs[idx[t]], dense[idx[t]]);
      return;
    }
    std::array<TopK<MaxK>*, kMaxBatch> outs;
    if (cfg_.dense_mode == DenseMode::Exact) {
      alignas(kCacheLine) std::array<float, kMaxBatch * D> qs;  // contiguous query matrix (stack)
      for (std::size_t t = 0; t < nq; ++t) {
        std::copy_n(ctxs[idx[t]].qvec.data(), D, qs.data() + t * D);
        outs[t] = &dense[idx[t]];
      }
      std::fill(qs.begin() + static_cast<std::ptrdiff_t>(nq * D), qs.begin() + static_cast<std::ptrdiff_t>(((nq + 3) & ~std::size_t{3}) * D), 0.f);
      store_.search_exact_batch(qs.data(), nq, 0, live, outs.data());
      return;
    }
    // Int8Rerank: one shared int8 pass fills each query's shortlist, then each
    // shortlist is reranked in fp32 exactly as search_two_stage() does.
    std::array<const std::int8_t*, kMaxBatch> qqs;
    std::array<TopK<kMaxRerank>*, kMaxBatch> cands;
    for (std::size_t t = 0; t < nq; ++t) {
      QueryContext& c = ctxs[idx[t]];
      simd::quantize_i8(c.qvec.data(), c.qvec_i8.data(), D);
      c.cand.reset(std::max<std::uint32_t>(cfg_.rerank_candidates, static_cast<std::uint32_t>(dense[idx[t]].k())));
      qqs[t] = c.qvec_i8.data();
      cands[t] = &c.cand;
    }
    store_.search_int8_batch(qqs.data(), nq, 0, live, cands.data());
    for (std::size_t t = 0; t < nq; ++t) {
      const float* qv = ctxs[idx[t]].qvec.data();
      for (const Hit& h : cands[t]->sorted()) dense[idx[t]].push(simd::dot(qv, store_.row(h.id), D), h.id);
    }
  }

  // Lexical retrieval, fusion and prompt assembly for one prepared query.
  QueryResult finish(std::string_view q, std::uint32_t k, const Snapshot& snap, TopK<MaxK>& dense,
                     QueryContext& ctx) const noexcept {
    const auto nd = copy_out(dense.sorted(), ctx.dense);
    QueryResult res;
    res.snapshot_version = snap.version;
    res.dense = {ctx.dense.data(), nd};
    if (cfg_.hybrid) {
      TopK<MaxK> lex(depth_for(k));
      snap.bm25.search(std::span<const std::uint64_t>(ctx.terms.data(), ctx.nterms), ctx.bm25, lex);
      const auto nl = copy_out(lex.sorted(), ctx.lexical);
      res.lexical = {ctx.lexical.data(), nl};
      TopK<MaxK> fused(k);
      rrf_fuse(res.dense, res.lexical, cfg_.rrf, fused);
      res.hits = {ctx.fused.data(), copy_out(fused.sorted(), ctx.fused)};
    } else {
      res.hits = res.dense.first(std::min<std::size_t>(k, nd));
    }
    res.prompt = build_prompt(q, res.hits, [this](std::uint32_t id) { return chunk(id); }, cfg_.prompt,
                              std::span<char>(ctx.prompt_buf.get(), ctx.prompt_cap));
    return res;
  }

  // Writer only: one arena copy per distinct source name.
  std::string_view intern_source(std::string_view s) {
    if (s.empty()) return {};
    auto it = sources_.find(s);
    if (it != sources_.end()) return *it;
    const std::string_view copy = arena_.copy(s);
    sources_.insert(copy);
    return copy;
  }

  static constexpr bool uses_ivf(DenseMode m) noexcept { return m == DenseMode::Ivf || m == DenseMode::IvfInt8; }
  static IvfParams effective_ivf(const EngineConfig& c) noexcept {
    IvfParams ip = c.ivf;
    ip.storage = c.dense_mode == DenseMode::IvfInt8 ? IvfStorage::Int8 : IvfStorage::Fp32;
    return ip;
  }

  static EngineConfig validated(EngineConfig c) {
    c.chunker.validate();
    if (c.max_chunks == 0) throw std::invalid_argument("max_chunks must be > 0");
    if (c.retrieve_depth == 0 || c.retrieve_depth > MaxK) throw std::invalid_argument("retrieve_depth must be in [1, MaxK]");
    if (c.rerank_candidates > kMaxRerank) throw std::invalid_argument("rerank_candidates > kMaxRerank");
    if (c.nprobe == 0) throw std::invalid_argument("nprobe must be > 0");
    // These keep every BM25 posting weight finite and > 0, which Bm25Index::search relies on.
    if (!(c.bm25.k1 >= 0.f) || !std::isfinite(c.bm25.k1) || !(c.bm25.b >= 0.f && c.bm25.b <= 1.f))
      throw std::invalid_argument("bm25 needs a finite k1 >= 0 and b in [0, 1]");
    return c;
  }

  static std::size_t copy_out(std::span<const Hit> src, std::array<Hit, MaxK>& dst) noexcept {
    const std::size_t n = std::min(src.size(), MaxK);
    std::copy_n(src.begin(), n, dst.begin());
    return n;
  }

  EngineConfig cfg_;
  E embedder_;
  VectorStore<D> store_;
  AlignedArray<ChunkMeta> meta_;
  struct Retired {
    const Snapshot* snap;
    std::uint64_t epoch;
  };

  // On-disk layout (see save()).
  struct FileHeader {
    char magic[8] = {'R', 'A', 'G', 'C', 'P', 'P', 'I', 'X'};
    std::uint32_t version;
    std::uint32_t dim;
    std::uint64_t embedder_tag;
    std::uint32_t n_chunks;
    std::uint32_t reserved;
    std::uint64_t text_bytes;
  };
  static constexpr std::uint32_t kNoSource = 0xFFFFFFFFu;
  struct ChunkRecord {
    std::uint64_t text_offset;
    std::uint32_t len, doc_id, ordinal, page_first, page_last, source;
    std::uint64_t reserved;
  };
  struct IndexRecord {  // parameters the saved snapshot was built with
    float k1, b;
    std::uint32_t nlist, train_iters, max_train;
    std::uint8_t storage, has_ivf, reserved8[2];
    std::uint64_t seed;
    std::uint32_t covered, reserved32;
  };
  static_assert(sizeof(FileHeader) == 40 && sizeof(ChunkRecord) == 40 && sizeof(IndexRecord) == 40,
                "file layout must not depend on padding");

  // Read by every query: its own line, never written by queries.
  alignas(kCacheLine) std::atomic<const Snapshot*> snap_;
  std::atomic<std::uint32_t> committed_{0};
  mutable EpochDomain epochs_;     // slots are written by readers (their own lines only)
  std::vector<Retired> retired_;  // writer only

  // Writer-only state (ingest). Vectors are reused, so steady-state ingest
  // stops allocating once they reach the largest document's size.
  Arena arena_;
  Bm25Builder builder_;
  std::vector<Token> tokens_, chunk_toks_;
  std::vector<std::uint64_t> terms_;
  std::unordered_set<std::string_view> sources_;  // views into arena_
  alignas(kCacheLine) std::array<float, D> vec_{};
};

}  // namespace rag

// rag/epoch.hpp — epoch-based reclamation (EBR) for immutable snapshots.
//
// Readers announce "I may be holding a pointer read at epoch e" in a
// per-reader, cache-line-padded slot; the writer frees a retired object only
// once no slot holds an epoch older than the one the object was retired in.
//
// Reader cost per critical section: one load of the global epoch and two
// stores to the reader's *own* cache line. There are no read-modify-write
// atomics and no shared-line writes, so readers never contend with each other.
// Writer cost per reclamation check: one load per slot (kMaxReaders lines).
//
// Correctness (all operations below are seq_cst, so they share one total order):
//   writer: old = ptr.exchange(new) ; e = ++epoch ; ... scan: every slot is 0 or >= e  => free(old)
//   reader: slot = epoch.load()     ; p = ptr.load() ; use p ; slot = 0
// If the writer's scan saw a reader's slot as 0, the reader's slot store comes
// later in the total order, so its ptr.load() also comes after the exchange and
// returns `new`. If the scan saw a value >= e, that reader loaded the epoch after
// the increment, which is again after the exchange. Either way that reader
// cannot be holding `old`. A slot holding a value < e blocks the free.
#pragma once

#include <array>
#include <atomic>
#include <cstdint>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <utility>

#include "rag/common.hpp"

namespace rag {

class EpochDomain {
 public:
  static constexpr std::size_t kMaxReaders = 128;

  struct alignas(kCacheLine) Slot {
    std::atomic<std::uint64_t> active{0};  // 0 = quiescent, else epoch at entry
    std::atomic<bool> in_use{false};       // claimed by a Reader handle
    std::uint32_t depth = 0;               // nesting depth (owning thread only)
  };
  static_assert(sizeof(Slot) == kCacheLine, "one slot per cache line: no false sharing between readers");

  // Registration handle owning one slot. Movable, not copyable. Claiming a slot
  // is a cold-path CAS scan, done once per reader thread.
  class Reader {
   public:
    Reader() = default;
    explicit Reader(Slot* s) noexcept : slot_(s) {}
    Reader(Reader&& o) noexcept : slot_(std::exchange(o.slot_, nullptr)) {}
    Reader& operator=(Reader&& o) noexcept {
      if (this != &o) { release(); slot_ = std::exchange(o.slot_, nullptr); }
      return *this;
    }
    Reader(const Reader&) = delete;
    Reader& operator=(const Reader&) = delete;
    ~Reader() { release(); }
    [[nodiscard]] Slot* slot() const noexcept { return slot_; }

   private:
    void release() noexcept {
      if (slot_) {
        slot_->active.store(0, std::memory_order_release);
        slot_->depth = 0;
        slot_->in_use.store(false, std::memory_order_release);
        slot_ = nullptr;
      }
    }
    Slot* slot_ = nullptr;
  };

  // RAII critical section. Nestable on the same Reader.
  class Guard {
   public:
    Guard(const EpochDomain& d, Slot& s) noexcept : s_(s) {
      if (s_.depth++ == 0) s_.active.store(d.epoch_.load(std::memory_order_seq_cst), std::memory_order_seq_cst);
    }
    Guard(const Guard&) = delete;
    Guard& operator=(const Guard&) = delete;
    ~Guard() {
      if (--s_.depth == 0) s_.active.store(0, std::memory_order_release);
    }

   private:
    Slot& s_;
  };

  [[nodiscard]] Reader register_reader() {
    for (Slot& s : slots_) {
      bool expected = false;
      if (!s.in_use.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) &&
          s.in_use.compare_exchange_strong(expected, true, std::memory_order_acq_rel))
        return Reader(&s);
    }
    throw std::runtime_error("EpochDomain: more than kMaxReaders live QueryContexts");
  }

  // Writer: start a new epoch after unpublishing an object; retire it with the result.
  std::uint64_t advance() noexcept { return epoch_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_seq_cst) + 1; }

  // Writer: true once no reader can still hold an object retired at epoch `e`.
  [[nodiscard]] bool quiescent_since(std::uint64_t e) const noexcept {
    for (const Slot& s : slots_) {
      const std::uint64_t a = s.active.load(std::memory_order_seq_cst);
      if (a != 0 && a < e) return false;
    }
    return true;
  }

  [[nodiscard]] std::size_t readers() const noexcept {
    std::size_t n = 0;
    for (const Slot& s : slots_) n += s.in_use.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    return n;
  }

 private:
  alignas(kCacheLine) std::atomic<std::uint64_t> epoch_{1};  // starts at 1: 0 means quiescent
  std::array<Slot, kMaxReaders> slots_{};
};

}  // namespace rag

```cpp
// rag/fusion.hpp — Reciprocal Rank Fusion of dense and lexical rankings.
//
//   rrf(d) = sum_i  w_i / (k0 + rank_i(d))      (rank is 1-based)
//
// RRF uses ranks only, so it needs no score calibration between cosine
// similarity and BM25 (their scales differ). Inputs are short (<= K hits),
// so a linear id-match on a stack array beats any hash map: everything
// stays in a few L1 lines and there is no allocation.
#pragma once

#include <algorithm>
#include <array>
#include <span>

#include "rag/topk.hpp"

namespace rag {

struct RrfParams {
  float k0 = 60.f;  // Cormack et al. 2009 default
  float w_dense = 1.f;
  float w_lexical = 1.f;
};

inline constexpr std::size_t kMaxFuseInput = 256;

template <class TK>
constexpr void rrf_fuse(std::span<const Hit> dense, std::span<const Hit> lexical, const RrfParams& p, TK& out) noexcept {
  std::array<Hit, 2 * kMaxFuseInput> acc{};
  const std::size_t na = std::min(dense.size(), kMaxFuseInput);
  const std::size_t nb = std::min(lexical.size(), kMaxFuseInput);
  std::size_t n = 0;
  for (std::size_t r = 0; r < na; ++r) acc[n++] = {p.w_dense / (p.k0 + static_cast<float>(r + 1)), dense[r].id};
  for (std::size_t r = 0; r < nb; ++r) {
    const float s = p.w_lexical / (p.k0 + static_cast<float>(r + 1));
    const auto id = lexical[r].id;
    std::size_t j = 0;
    while (j < na && acc[j].id != id) ++j;  // ids are unique within each list
    if (j < na) acc[j].score += s;
    else acc[n++] = {s, id};
  }
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) out.push(acc[i].score, acc[i].id);
}

}  // namespace rag

// rag/io.hpp — binary index file I/O (cold path only).
//
// Format: little-endian, fixed-width PODs, length-prefixed arrays, and a
// trailing 64-bit FNV-1a checksum over every byte before it. The reader
// rejects bad magic, unknown versions, truncation, trailing garbage, and
// checksum mismatches. Array lengths are checked against the bytes actually
// left in the file before anything is allocated, so a corrupted length can't
// trigger a huge allocation.
//
// Saves are crash-safe: data goes to "<path>.tmp", is fsync'ed, and is then
// renamed over <path>, and the directory is fsync'ed so the rename itself is
// durable. A crash or power loss at any point leaves either the complete old
// index or the complete new one under <path>, never a partial file.
#pragma once

#include <bit>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstring>
#include <filesystem>
#include <fstream>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <string>
#include <type_traits>
#include <vector>

#if defined(__unix__) || defined(__APPLE__)
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#elif defined(_WIN32)
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <io.h>  // _wopen, _commit (FlushFileBuffers), _close
#endif

namespace rag::io {

namespace detail {
// Flush a file's (or directory's) contents to stable storage.
inline void fsync_path(const std::filesystem::path& p, bool directory) {
#if defined(__unix__) || defined(__APPLE__)
  const int fd = ::open(p.c_str(), directory ? O_RDONLY | O_DIRECTORY : O_RDONLY);
  if (fd < 0) throw std::runtime_error("rag::io: cannot open " + p.string() + " to sync");
  const int rc = ::fsync(fd);
  ::close(fd);
  if (rc != 0) throw std::runtime_error("rag::io: fsync failed for " + p.string());
#elif defined(_WIN32)
  // Windows has no directory handle to flush; NTFS journals the rename itself.
  if (directory) return;
  const int fd = ::_wopen(p.c_str(), _O_RDWR | _O_BINARY);
  if (fd < 0) throw std::runtime_error("rag::io: cannot open " + p.string() + " to sync");
  const int rc = ::_commit(fd);
  ::_close(fd);
  if (rc != 0) throw std::runtime_error("rag::io: flush failed for " + p.string());
#else
  (void)p; (void)directory;  // portable fallback: rename-only (atomic, not durable)
#endif
}
}  // namespace detail

static_assert(std::endian::native == std::endian::little, "index files are little-endian; add byte swapping to port");

struct FormatError : std::runtime_error {
  using std::runtime_error::runtime_error;
};

inline constexpr char kMagic[8] = {'R', 'A', 'G', 'C', 'P', 'P', 'I', 'X'};
inline constexpr std::uint32_t kFormatVersion = 2;  // 2: chunk source + page range

// Streaming 64-bit checksum, 8 bytes per step. Each step h = mix((h ^ w) * K)
// is a bijection in h, so changing any single word always changes the
// result. Fed byte-at-a-time or in arbitrary chunks, it gives the same
// value: a partial word is buffered until it fills.
class Checksum {
 public:
  void update(const void* p, std::size_t n) noexcept {
    if (n == 0) return;  // p may be null (empty vector): memcpy(dst, nullptr, 0) is UB
    const auto* b = static_cast<const unsigned char*>(p);
    while (n && fill_) {  // top up a partial word left by the previous call
      buf_[fill_++] = *b++;
      --n;
      if (fill_ == 8) { step(load(buf_)); fill_ = 0; }
    }
    for (; n >= 8; b += 8, n -= 8) step(load(b));
    // Here either n == 0, or the buffer is empty and n < 8: the tail fits.
    std::memcpy(buf_ + fill_, b, n);
    fill_ += static_cast<std::uint32_t>(n);
  }
  [[nodiscard]] std::uint64_t value() const noexcept {
    std::uint64_t h = h_;
    if (fill_) {  // fold in the tail, tagged with its length
      unsigned char t[8] = {};
      std::memcpy(t, buf_, fill_);
      h = mix((h ^ load(t) ^ (std::uint64_t{fill_} << 56)) * kMul);
    }
    return mix(h ^ total_bits());
  }

 private:
  static constexpr std::uint64_t kMul = 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15ull;
  static std::uint64_t load(const unsigned char* b) noexcept {
    std::uint64_t w;
    std::memcpy(&w, b, 8);
    return w;
  }
  static constexpr std::uint64_t mix(std::uint64_t x) noexcept { return x ^ (x >> 29); }
  void step(std::uint64_t w) noexcept {
    h_ = mix((h_ ^ w) * kMul);
    ++words_;
  }
  [[nodiscard]] std::uint64_t total_bits() const noexcept { return (words_ * 8 + fill_) * 8; }

  std::uint64_t h_ = 0x243F6A8885A308D3ull;
  std::uint64_t words_ = 0;
  unsigned char buf_[8] = {};
  std::uint32_t fill_ = 0;
};

class Writer {
 public:
  explicit Writer(std::filesystem::path path) : path_(std::move(path)), tmp_(path_.string() + ".tmp") {
    f_.open(tmp_, std::ios::binary | std::ios::trunc);
    if (!f_) throw std::runtime_error("rag::io: cannot open " + tmp_.string() + " for writing");
  }
  Writer(const Writer&) = delete;
  Writer& operator=(const Writer&) = delete;
  ~Writer() {
    if (!committed_) {  // abandoned (exception mid-save): leave the old file alone
      f_.close();
      std::error_code ec;
      std::filesystem::remove(tmp_, ec);
    }
  }

  void bytes(const void* p, std::size_t n) {
    f_.write(static_cast<const char*>(p), static_cast<std::streamsize>(n));
    sum_.update(p, n);
  }
  template <class T>
  void pod(const T& v) {
    static_assert(std::is_trivially_copyable_v<T>);
    bytes(&v, sizeof(T));
  }
  template <class T>
  void vec(const std::vector<T>& v) {
    pod<std::uint64_t>(v.size());
    bytes(v.data(), v.size() * sizeof(T));
  }

  // Append the checksum, flush, and atomically replace the target file.
  void commit() {
    const std::uint64_t h = sum_.value();
    f_.write(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(&h), sizeof h);
    f_.flush();
    if (!f_) throw std::runtime_error("rag::io: write failed for " + tmp_.string());
    f_.close();
    detail::fsync_path(tmp_, false);  // data is on disk before it gets the real name
    std::filesystem::rename(tmp_, path_);
    committed_ = true;
    const auto dir = path_.has_parent_path() ? path_.parent_path() : std::filesystem::path(".");
    detail::fsync_path(dir, true);  // make the rename itself durable
  }

 private:
  std::filesystem::path path_, tmp_;
  std::ofstream f_;
  Checksum sum_;
  bool committed_ = false;
};

class Reader {
 public:
  explicit Reader(const std::filesystem::path& path) : f_(path, std::ios::binary) {
    if (!f_) throw std::runtime_error("rag::io: cannot open " + path.string());
    f_.seekg(0, std::ios::end);
    const auto size = static_cast<std::uint64_t>(f_.tellg());
    f_.seekg(0);
    if (size < sizeof(std::uint64_t)) throw FormatError("rag::io: file too small");
    remaining_ = size - sizeof(std::uint64_t);  // payload bytes before the checksum
  }

  void bytes(void* p, std::size_t n) {
    if (n > remaining_) throw FormatError("rag::io: truncated file");
    f_.read(static_cast<char*>(p), static_cast<std::streamsize>(n));
    if (!f_) throw FormatError("rag::io: read failed");
    remaining_ -= n;
    sum_.update(p, n);
  }
  template <class T>
  [[nodiscard]] T pod() {
    static_assert(std::is_trivially_copyable_v<T>);
    T v;
    bytes(&v, sizeof(T));
    return v;
  }
  template <class T>
  [[nodiscard]] std::vector<T> vec() {
    const auto n = pod<std::uint64_t>();
    if (n > remaining_ / sizeof(T)) throw FormatError("rag::io: array length exceeds file size");
    std::vector<T> v(static_cast<std::size_t>(n));
    bytes(v.data(), v.size() * sizeof(T));
    return v;
  }
  [[nodiscard]] std::uint64_t remaining() const noexcept { return remaining_; }

  // Verify that the payload was consumed exactly and the checksum matches.
  void finish() {
    if (remaining_ != 0) throw FormatError("rag::io: unexpected trailing data");
    std::uint64_t h;
    f_.read(reinterpret_cast<char*>(&h), sizeof h);
    if (!f_ || h != sum_.value()) throw FormatError("rag::io: checksum mismatch (corrupted file)");
  }

 private:
  std::ifstream f_;
  std::uint64_t remaining_ = 0;
  Checksum sum_;
};

}  // namespace rag::io

```
