```cpp
// rag/orderflow/tick_env.hpp — tick scalping (passive, queue-based) on the
// ES simulator, as an Environment for rag::agent learners.
//
// The strategy earns the spread by resting 1-lot limit orders at the best
// bid and/or ask and managing inventory. Every `decide_seconds` it picks a
// quoting mode:
//
//   0 no quotes        cancel everything
//   1 bid only         rest a buy at the best bid
//   2 ask only         rest a sell at the best ask
//   3 both sides
//   4 flatten          cancel quotes, market order back to flat
//
// Between decisions the environment keeps each quoted side at the touch
// every simulator step: if the best price moved away, the order is cancelled
// and rejoins at the back of the new best queue (queue priority is lost, as
// in a real FIFO book). A side is not quoted when a fill would take the
// inventory past +-max_position. Fills come from the simulator's FIFO model:
// an order fills only after the lots ahead of it trade, so adverse
// selection (being filled just before the price moves through you) is real.
//
// Reward: change in mark-to-market equity (at the mid) in ticks, net of
// fees; the episode ends flat. Observation: the 13 order-flow features plus
// queue position on each side, touch sizes, spread, position, open P&L and
// time left.
#pragma once

#include <array>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdint>
#include <optional>
#include <vector>

#include "rag/agent/env.hpp"
#include "rag/orderflow/features.hpp"
#include "rag/orderflow/simulator.hpp"

namespace rag::orderflow {

struct TickParams {
  SimParams sim;
  double decide_seconds = 0.5;
  double episode_seconds = 300;
  double warmup_seconds = 150;
  double start_second = -1;  // session time of the warm-up start; < 0: random each episode
  int max_position = 1;
  double fee_dollars = 1.5;  // per contract per side, passive or aggressive
};

struct TickObs {
  std::array<double, kFeatures> f{};
  double bid_queue = -1, ask_queue = -1;  // lots ahead / displayed size at our level; -1: not quoting
  double bid_size = 0, ask_size = 0;      // log(1 + touch size)
  double spread = 1;                      // ticks
  int position = 0;
  double open_pnl = 0;  // ticks
  double time_left = 1;
};

class TickScalpEnv {
 public:
  using Observation = TickObs;
  static constexpr std::size_t kNumActions = 5;
  static constexpr std::size_t kStateDims = kFeatures + 8;
  static constexpr std::array<double, kStateDims> kLo = [] {
    std::array<double, kStateDims> a{};
    a.fill(-kClip);
    for (std::size_t i = kFeatures; i < kStateDims; ++i) a[i] = -1;
    return a;
  }();
  static constexpr std::array<double, kStateDims> kHi = [] {
    std::array<double, kStateDims> a{};
    a.fill(kClip);
    for (std::size_t i = kFeatures; i < kStateDims; ++i) a[i] = 1;
    return a;
  }();

  explicit TickScalpEnv(const TickParams& p = {}) : p_(p) {}

  // An episode's market before its warm-up: a fresh simulator seeded from
  // `rng` at a random time of day (or start_second). reset() and the
  // diagnostics probe (of10_discovery's episode regime) both build episodes
  // with it, so they see the same markets.
  [[nodiscard]] static EsSimulator make_market(const TickParams& p, rag::agent::Rng& rng) {
    const double latest_start = std::max(0.0, p.sim.session_seconds - p.episode_seconds - p.warmup_seconds);
    const double u = rng.uniform();  // drawn either way: episode seeds don't depend on the setting
    const std::uint64_t seed = rng.next();
    return EsSimulator(p.sim, seed, p.start_second >= 0 ? p.start_second : u * latest_start);
  }

  Observation reset(rag::agent::Rng& rng) {
    sim_.emplace(make_market(p_, rng));
    fb_ = FeatureBuilder(p_.sim.dt);
    for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < steps(p_.warmup_seconds); ++i) advance();
    position_ = 0;
    cash_ = equity_ = fees_ = elapsed_ = 0;
    entry_ = 0;
    bid_id_ = ask_id_ = 0;
    mode_ = 0;
    fills_ = 0;
    return obs();
  }

  rag::agent::Step<Observation> step(rag::agent::Action a, rag::agent::Rng&) {
    step_fills_.clear();
    step_fill_values_.clear();
    double fees = 0;
    if (a == 4) {
      mode_ = 0;
      manage();
      if (position_ != 0) fees += take_to_flat();
    } else {
      mode_ = static_cast<int>(a);
      manage();
    }
    for (std::uint32_t i = 0, n = steps(p_.decide_seconds); i < n; ++i) {
      advance();
      fees += book_fills();
      manage();
    }
    elapsed_ += p_.decide_seconds;
    const bool done = elapsed_ >= p_.episode_seconds - 1e-9;
    if (done) {
      mode_ = 0;
      manage();
      if (position_ != 0) fees += take_to_flat();
    }
    const double eq = cash_ + position_ * sim_->mid();
    const double reward = eq - equity_ - fees;
    equity_ = eq;
    return {obs(), reward, done};
  }

  [[nodiscard]] std::array<double, kStateDims> features(const Observation& o) const noexcept {
    std::array<double, kStateDims> x{};
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < kFeatures; ++i) x[i] = o.f[i];
    x[kFeatures + 0] = std::clamp(o.bid_queue, -1.0, 1.0);
    x[kFeatures + 1] = std::clamp(o.ask_queue, -1.0, 1.0);
    x[kFeatures + 2] = std::clamp(o.bid_size / 8 * 2 - 1, -1.0, 1.0);  // log sizes: ~0..8
    x[kFeatures + 3] = std::clamp(o.ask_size / 8 * 2 - 1, -1.0, 1.0);
    x[kFeatures + 4] = std::clamp(o.spread - 1, 0.0, 1.0);
    x[kFeatures + 5] = static_cast<double>(o.position) / p_.max_position;
    x[kFeatures + 6] = std::clamp(o.open_pnl / 4, -1.0, 1.0);
    x[kFeatures + 7] = o.time_left * 2 - 1;
    return x;
  }

  [[nodiscard]] double net_pnl_ticks() const noexcept { return equity_ - fees_; }
  [[nodiscard]] std::uint32_t fills() const noexcept { return fills_; }
  // Passive fills of the last step() (own-fill markouts); flattening market orders are not included.
  [[nodiscard]] const std::vector<OwnFill>& step_fills() const noexcept { return step_fills_; }
  // DIAGNOSTICS ONLY, hidden state (never an observation): the fair value when
  // each step_fills()[i] filled (EsSimulator::own_fill_hidden_values()).
  [[nodiscard]] const std::vector<double>& step_fill_hidden_values() const noexcept { return step_fill_values_; }
  [[nodiscard]] double fees_ticks() const noexcept { return fees_; }
  [[nodiscard]] const EsSimulator& market() const noexcept { return *sim_; }
  [[nodiscard]] const TickParams& params() const noexcept { return p_; }

 private:
  [[nodiscard]] std::uint32_t steps(double seconds) const {
    return std::max<std::uint32_t>(1, static_cast<std::uint32_t>(std::lround(seconds / p_.sim.dt)));
  }
  void advance() {
    sim_->step();
    for (const auto& t : sim_->trades()) fb_.add_trade(t);
    fb_.end_bucket(sim_->quote());
  }
  [[nodiscard]] const EsSimulator::Resting* find(std::uint64_t id) const {
    if (id == 0) return nullptr;
    for (const auto& r : sim_->resting())
      if (r.id == id) return &r;
    return nullptr;
  }
  void on_fill(Side side, std::int32_t price, std::uint32_t size) {
    const int before = position_;
    const int signed_size = side == Side::Buy ? static_cast<int>(size) : -static_cast<int>(size);
    cash_ -= signed_size * static_cast<double>(price);
    position_ += signed_size;
    if (position_ != 0 && (before == 0 || (before > 0) != (position_ > 0))) entry_ = price;
    if (position_ == 0) entry_ = 0;
    ++fills_;
  }
  // Passive fills from the last simulator step; returns their fees.
  double book_fills() {
    double fees = 0;
    const auto& values = sim_->own_fill_hidden_values();
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < sim_->own_fills().size(); ++i) {
      const OwnFill& f = sim_->own_fills()[i];
      on_fill(f.side, f.price, f.size);
      step_fills_.push_back(f);
      step_fill_values_.push_back(values[i]);
      fees += f.size * p_.fee_dollars / kTickValue;
    }
    fees_ += fees;
    if (!find(bid_id_)) bid_id_ = 0;
    if (!find(ask_id_)) ask_id_ = 0;
    return fees;
  }
  // Keep each wanted side resting at the touch; cancel unwanted ones.
  void manage() {
    const bool want_bid = (mode_ == 1 || mode_ == 3) && position_ < p_.max_position;
    const bool want_ask = (mode_ == 2 || mode_ == 3) && position_ > -p_.max_position;
    auto keep = [&](std::uint64_t& id, bool want, Side side) {
      const auto* r = find(id);
      const std::int32_t best = side == Side::Buy ? sim_->bid() : sim_->ask();
      if (r && (!want || r->price != best)) {
        sim_->cancel(id);
        id = 0;
        r = nullptr;
      }
      if (want && !r) id = sim_->submit_limit(side, best, 1);
    };
    keep(bid_id_, want_bid, Side::Buy);
    keep(ask_id_, want_ask, Side::Sell);
  }
  double take_to_flat() {
    const int diff = -position_;
    const Fill f = sim_->market_order(diff > 0 ? Side::Buy : Side::Sell, static_cast<std::uint32_t>(std::abs(diff)));
    cash_ -= (diff > 0 ? 1.0 : -1.0) * f.filled * f.avg_price;
    position_ += diff > 0 ? static_cast<int>(f.filled) : -static_cast<int>(f.filled);
    if (position_ == 0) entry_ = 0;
    ++fills_;
    const double fee = f.filled * p_.fee_dollars / kTickValue;
    fees_ += fee;
    return fee;
  }
  [[nodiscard]] Observation obs() const {
    Observation o;
    o.f = fb_.values();
    const Quote q = sim_->quote();
    auto queue = [&](std::uint64_t id, std::uint32_t shown) {
      const auto* r = find(id);
      return r ? static_cast<double>(r->ahead) / std::max<std::uint32_t>(1, shown) : -1.0;
    };
    o.bid_queue = queue(bid_id_, q.bid_size[0]);
    o.ask_queue = queue(ask_id_, q.ask_size[0]);
    o.bid_size = std::log1p(q.bid_size[0]);
    o.ask_size = std::log1p(q.ask_size[0]);
    o.spread = q.ask - q.bid;
    o.position = position_;
    o.open_pnl = position_ != 0 ? position_ * (sim_->mid() - entry_) : 0;
    o.time_left = std::max(0.0, 1 - elapsed_ / p_.episode_seconds);
    return o;
  }

  TickParams p_;
  std::optional<EsSimulator> sim_;
  FeatureBuilder fb_{0.1};
  int position_ = 0, mode_ = 0;
  double cash_ = 0, equity_ = 0, fees_ = 0, elapsed_ = 0, entry_ = 0;
  std::uint64_t bid_id_ = 0, ask_id_ = 0;
  std::uint32_t fills_ = 0;
  std::vector<OwnFill> step_fills_;  // passive fills of the last step() (diagnostics)
  std::vector<double> step_fill_values_;  // step_fill_hidden_values(), parallel to step_fills_
};

static_assert(rag::agent::Environment<TickScalpEnv>);

}  // namespace rag::orderflow
```

```cpp
// rag/pdf.hpp — PDF ingestion: text extraction (Poppler), cleanup
// (rag/text_clean.hpp), and page-aware ingestion into a RagEngine.
//
// Requires libpoppler-cpp (Debian/Ubuntu: libpoppler-cpp-dev; link the
// `rag_pdf_support` CMake target). Everything else in rag-cpp stays
// dependency-free; this header is the only one that needs Poppler.
//
//   auto r = rag::pdf::ingest_pdf(engine, "report.pdf", /*doc_id=*/7);
//   // chunks now cite "(report.pdf, p. 12)" in prompts
//
// Scanned PDFs (page images with no text layer) yield empty pages; they are
// counted in the result so callers can warn or route them to OCR. Encrypted
// PDFs are rejected unless they open with an empty password.
#pragma once

#include <poppler-document.h>
#include <poppler-global.h>
#include <poppler-page.h>

#include <cstdint>
#include <filesystem>
#include <memory>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "rag/engine.hpp"
#include "rag/text_clean.hpp"

namespace rag::pdf {

struct PdfError : std::runtime_error {
  using std::runtime_error::runtime_error;
};

struct Document {
  std::vector<std::string> pages;  // cleaned text per page, page 1 first
  std::size_t empty_pages = 0;     // pages with no text after cleanup (often scanned images)
  std::string title;               // from the document info dictionary, if any
};

namespace detail {
inline std::string utf8(const poppler::ustring& s) {
  const auto b = s.to_utf8();
  return {b.begin(), b.end()};
}
// Poppler reports recoverable syntax problems on stderr; collect instead.
inline void quiet(const std::string&, void*) {}
}  // namespace detail

// Extract and clean every page. Throws PdfError if the file is missing, not
// a PDF, or encrypted.
inline Document extract(const std::filesystem::path& path, const text::CleanOptions& clean = {}) {
  poppler::set_debug_error_function(detail::quiet, nullptr);
  if (!std::filesystem::is_regular_file(path)) throw PdfError("no such file: " + path.string());
  std::unique_ptr<poppler::document> doc(poppler::document::load_from_file(path.string()));
  if (!doc) throw PdfError("not a readable PDF: " + path.string());
  if (doc->is_locked()) throw PdfError("encrypted PDF (password required): " + path.string());

  std::vector<std::string> raw;
  const int n = doc->pages();
  raw.reserve(static_cast<std::size_t>(n > 0 ? n : 0));
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    std::unique_ptr<poppler::page> page(doc->create_page(i));
    // Reading order (not physical layout): columns come out one after another.
    raw.push_back(page ? detail::utf8(page->text(poppler::rectf(), poppler::page::non_raw_non_physical_layout))
                       : std::string{});
  }
  Document out;
  out.pages = text::clean_pages(std::move(raw), clean);
  for (const auto& p : out.pages) out.empty_pages += p.empty();
  out.title = detail::utf8(doc->get_title());
  return out;
}

struct IngestResult {
  std::uint32_t pages = 0;
  std::uint32_t empty_pages = 0;
  std::uint32_t chunks = 0;
  std::uint64_t text_bytes = 0;
};

// Ingest an already-extracted document under `source` (shown in citations).
template <class Engine>
IngestResult ingest(Engine& engine, const Document& doc, std::uint32_t doc_id, std::string_view source) {
  const auto joined = text::join_pages(doc.pages);
  IngestResult r;
  r.pages = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(doc.pages.size());
  r.empty_pages = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(doc.empty_pages);
  r.text_bytes = joined.text.size();
  r.chunks = engine.ingest(joined.text, doc_id, IngestOptions{.source = source, .page_starts = joined.page_starts});
  return r;
}

// Extract, clean and ingest a PDF; citations use the file name.
template <class Engine>
IngestResult ingest_pdf(Engine& engine, const std::filesystem::path& path, std::uint32_t doc_id,
                        const text::CleanOptions& clean = {}) {
  return ingest(engine, extract(path, clean), doc_id, path.filename().string());
}

}  // namespace rag::pdf
```

```cpp
// rag/prompt.hpp — context assembly into a caller-owned, fixed-size buffer.
//
// The prompt is written straight into a preallocated char buffer: no
// std::string, no ostringstream, no reallocation. Space for the question
// and footer is reserved up front, so a long context can never push the
// question out of the prompt. Chunks are packed greedily in rank order under
// a token budget; a chunk that does not fit is skipped and smaller,
// lower-ranked chunks may still be used.
#pragma once

#include <algorithm>
#include <charconv>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstring>
#include <span>
#include <string_view>

#include "rag/topk.hpp"

namespace rag {

struct ChunkView {
  std::string_view text;
  std::uint32_t doc_id;
  std::uint32_t ordinal;        // chunk index within the document
  std::string_view source{};    // e.g. "report.pdf"; empty if not given at ingest
  std::uint32_t page_first = 0; // 1-based pages the chunk spans; 0 = unknown
  std::uint32_t page_last = 0;
};

struct PromptParams {
  std::uint32_t max_context_tokens = 1024;
  std::string_view system =
      "You are a precise assistant. Answer using only the context below. "
      "Cite sources as [n]. If the context is insufficient, say so.";
};

struct PromptResult {
  std::string_view prompt;
  std::uint32_t chunks_used = 0;
  std::uint32_t context_tokens = 0;  // estimated
  bool truncated = false;            // some chunk(s) or the whole prompt did not fit
};

// ~4 bytes/token for English BPE vocabularies; swap for a real tokenizer count
// if the generator's limit is tight.
constexpr std::uint32_t estimate_tokens(std::size_t bytes) noexcept {
  return static_cast<std::uint32_t>((bytes + 3) / 4);
}

namespace detail {
class BufWriter {
 public:
  constexpr BufWriter(char* p, std::size_t cap) noexcept : p_(p), cap_(cap) {}
  // Writes are clamped to the buffer. Callers size their output up front, so
  // the clamp never truncates in practice; it guarantees that a budgeting
  // mistake can never become a buffer overflow.
  void put(std::string_view s) noexcept {
    const std::size_t n = std::min(s.size(), cap_ - len_);
    if (n == 0) return;  // an empty view's data() may be null: memcpy(dst, nullptr, 0) is UB
    std::memcpy(p_ + len_, s.data(), n);
    len_ += n;
  }
  void put_u32(std::uint32_t v) noexcept { len_ = static_cast<std::size_t>(std::to_chars(p_ + len_, p_ + cap_, v).ptr - p_); }
  [[nodiscard]] std::size_t len() const noexcept { return len_; }
  [[nodiscard]] std::string_view view() const noexcept { return {p_, len_}; }
 private:
  char* p_;
  std::size_t cap_;
  std::size_t len_ = 0;
};
// Longest source name a citation shows (longer names are cut at a UTF-8
// boundary and marked with "..."), so one odd file name can't eat the budget.
inline constexpr std::size_t kMaxCitedSource = 120;
inline constexpr std::size_t kMaxCitation = kMaxCitedSource + 64;

// Writes "[n] (<where>)\n" into out, where <where> is
//   "doc D, chunk C"          no source, no pages (plain text ingest)
//   "doc D, p. P" / "pp. P-Q" no source, pages
//   "SOURCE, chunk C"         source, no pages
//   "SOURCE, p. P" / "pp. P-Q" source and pages (e.g. PDFs)
// and returns its length. out must hold kMaxCitation bytes.
inline std::size_t format_citation(char* out, std::uint32_t n, const ChunkView& c) noexcept {
  BufWriter w(out, kMaxCitation);
  using namespace std::string_view_literals;
  w.put("["sv);
  w.put_u32(n);
  w.put("] ("sv);
  if (c.source.empty()) {
    w.put("doc "sv);
    w.put_u32(c.doc_id);
  } else if (c.source.size() <= kMaxCitedSource) {
    w.put(c.source);
  } else {
    std::size_t cut = kMaxCitedSource - 3;
    while (cut > 0 && (static_cast<unsigned char>(c.source[cut]) & 0xC0) == 0x80) --cut;  // don't split a UTF-8 sequence
    w.put(c.source.substr(0, cut));
    w.put("..."sv);
  }
  if (c.page_first == 0) {
    w.put(", chunk "sv);
    w.put_u32(c.ordinal);
  } else if (c.page_first == c.page_last) {
    w.put(", p. "sv);
    w.put_u32(c.page_first);
  } else {
    w.put(", pp. "sv);
    w.put_u32(c.page_first);
    w.put("-"sv);
    w.put_u32(c.page_last);
  }
  w.put(")\n"sv);
  return w.len();
}
}  // namespace detail

template <class Lookup>  // Lookup: (std::uint32_t chunk_id) -> ChunkView
PromptResult build_prompt(std::string_view question, std::span<const Hit> hits, Lookup&& lookup,
                          const PromptParams& p, std::span<char> buf) noexcept {
  using namespace std::string_view_literals;
  constexpr auto kCtx = "\n\n### Context\n"sv, kQ = "### Question\n"sv, kA = "\n\n### Answer\n"sv;
  PromptResult r;
  const std::size_t fixed = p.system.size() + kCtx.size() + kQ.size() + question.size() + kA.size();
  if (fixed > buf.size()) { r.truncated = true; return r; }

  detail::BufWriter w(buf.data(), buf.size());
  w.put(p.system);
  w.put(kCtx);
  const std::size_t budget_bytes = buf.size() - fixed;  // reserved for chunk entries
  std::size_t used_bytes = 0;
  for (const Hit& h : hits) {
    const ChunkView c = lookup(h.id);
    const std::uint32_t n = r.chunks_used + 1;
    // "<citation>\n<text>\n\n"
    char cite[detail::kMaxCitation];
    const std::size_t cite_len = detail::format_citation(cite, n, c);
    const std::size_t entry = cite_len + c.text.size() + 2;
    const std::uint32_t tok = estimate_tokens(c.text.size());
    if (used_bytes + entry > budget_bytes || r.context_tokens + tok > p.max_context_tokens) {
      r.truncated = true;
      continue;
    }
    w.put({cite, cite_len}); w.put(c.text); w.put("\n\n"sv);
    used_bytes += entry;
    r.context_tokens += tok;
    r.chunks_used = n;
  }
  w.put(kQ);
  w.put(question);
  w.put(kA);
  r.prompt = w.view();
  return r;
}

}  // namespace rag
```

```cpp
// rag/simd.hpp — similarity kernels: fp32 dot, 4-row register-blocked dot,
// int8 dot (AVX-512 VNNI / AVX-512BW / AVX2), quantisation, normalisation.
//
// Dispatch is compile-time (build with -march=native or an explicit target):
// the best kernel is inlined straight into the scan loops, so there is no
// function-pointer call per row. Every ISA variant stays callable by name for
// benchmarking and for differential tests against the scalar reference.
//
// Preconditions: n % 64 == 0 for every SIMD variant (enforced at the type
// level by ValidDim<D>); scalar variants accept any n.
#pragma once

#include <cmath>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

#if defined(__AVX2__) || defined(__AVX512F__)
#include <immintrin.h>
#endif

#include "rag/common.hpp"

namespace rag::simd {

// ------------------------------- scalar ------------------------------------
inline float dot_scalar(const float* RAG_RESTRICT a, const float* RAG_RESTRICT b, std::size_t n) noexcept {
  float s = 0.f;
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) s += a[i] * b[i];
  return s;
}

inline std::int32_t dot_i8_scalar(const std::int8_t* a, const std::int8_t* b, std::size_t n) noexcept {
  std::int32_t s = 0;
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) s += std::int32_t{a[i]} * std::int32_t{b[i]};
  return s;
}

// -------------------------------- AVX2 --------------------------------------
#if defined(RAG_AVX2_FMA)
RAG_ALWAYS_INLINE float hsum256(__m256 v) noexcept {
  __m128 lo = _mm256_castps256_ps128(v), hi = _mm256_extractf128_ps(v, 1);
  lo = _mm_add_ps(lo, hi);
  lo = _mm_add_ps(lo, _mm_movehl_ps(lo, lo));
  lo = _mm_add_ss(lo, _mm_movehdup_ps(lo));
  return _mm_cvtss_f32(lo);
}
RAG_ALWAYS_INLINE std::int32_t hsum256_i32(__m256i v) noexcept {
  __m128i s = _mm_add_epi32(_mm256_castsi256_si128(v), _mm256_extracti128_si256(v, 1));
  s = _mm_add_epi32(s, _mm_shuffle_epi32(s, 0x4E));
  s = _mm_add_epi32(s, _mm_shuffle_epi32(s, 0xB1));
  return _mm_cvtsi128_si32(s);
}

// 4 independent accumulators hide the 4-cycle FMA latency.
RAG_ALWAYS_INLINE float dot_avx2(const float* a, const float* b, std::size_t n) noexcept {
  __m256 s0 = _mm256_setzero_ps(), s1 = s0, s2 = s0, s3 = s0;
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; i += 32) {
    s0 = _mm256_fmadd_ps(_mm256_loadu_ps(a + i), _mm256_loadu_ps(b + i), s0);
    s1 = _mm256_fmadd_ps(_mm256_loadu_ps(a + i + 8), _mm256_loadu_ps(b + i + 8), s1);
    s2 = _mm256_fmadd_ps(_mm256_loadu_ps(a + i + 16), _mm256_loadu_ps(b + i + 16), s2);
    s3 = _mm256_fmadd_ps(_mm256_loadu_ps(a + i + 24), _mm256_loadu_ps(b + i + 24), s3);
  }
  return hsum256(_mm256_add_ps(_mm256_add_ps(s0, s1), _mm256_add_ps(s2, s3)));
}

// Register blocking: each query vector load is reused against 4 rows,
// cutting query-side load traffic 4x relative to 4 separate dot() calls.
RAG_ALWAYS_INLINE void dot4_avx2(const float* q, const float* r, std::size_t stride, std::size_t n,
                                 float* out) noexcept {
  __m256 a0 = _mm256_setzero_ps(), a1 = a0, a2 = a0, a3 = a0;
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; i += 8) {
    const __m256 qv = _mm256_loadu_ps(q + i);
    a0 = _mm256_fmadd_ps(_mm256_load_ps(r + i), qv, a0);
    a1 = _mm256_fmadd_ps(_mm256_load_ps(r + stride + i), qv, a1);
    a2 = _mm256_fmadd_ps(_mm256_load_ps(r + 2 * stride + i), qv, a2);
    a3 = _mm256_fmadd_ps(_mm256_load_ps(r + 3 * stride + i), qv, a3);
  }
  out[0] = hsum256(a0); out[1] = hsum256(a1); out[2] = hsum256(a2); out[3] = hsum256(a3);
}

// int8 x int8 via the sign trick: |a| (u8) * sign(b, a) (s8) -> maddubs.
// Requires values in [-127, 127] (quantize_i8 guarantees it) so that neither
// |a| nor the sign flip of b can overflow, and so maddubs' i16 pair sum
// (max 2*127*127 = 32258) never saturates.
RAG_ALWAYS_INLINE std::int32_t dot_i8_avx2(const std::int8_t* a, const std::int8_t* b, std::size_t n) noexcept {
  const __m256i ones = _mm256_set1_epi16(1);
  __m256i acc0 = _mm256_setzero_si256(), acc1 = acc0;
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; i += 64) {
    const __m256i va0 = _mm256_loadu_si256(reinterpret_cast<const __m256i*>(a + i));
    const __m256i vb0 = _mm256_loadu_si256(reinterpret_cast<const __m256i*>(b + i));
    const __m256i va1 = _mm256_loadu_si256(reinterpret_cast<const __m256i*>(a + i + 32));
    const __m256i vb1 = _mm256_loadu_si256(reinterpret_cast<const __m256i*>(b + i + 32));
    const __m256i p0 = _mm256_maddubs_epi16(_mm256_abs_epi8(va0), _mm256_sign_epi8(vb0, va0));
    const __m256i p1 = _mm256_maddubs_epi16(_mm256_abs_epi8(va1), _mm256_sign_epi8(vb1, va1));
    acc0 = _mm256_add_epi32(acc0, _mm256_madd_epi16(p0, ones));
    acc1 = _mm256_add_epi32(acc1, _mm256_madd_epi16(p1, ones));
  }
  return hsum256_i32(_mm256_add_epi32(acc0, acc1));
}
#endif

// ------------------------------- AVX-512 ------------------------------------
#if defined(__AVX512F__)
RAG_ALWAYS_INLINE float dot_avx512(const float* a, const float* b, std::size_t n) noexcept {
  __m512 s0 = _mm512_setzero_ps(), s1 = s0, s2 = s0, s3 = s0;
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; i += 64) {
    s0 = _mm512_fmadd_ps(_mm512_loadu_ps(a + i), _mm512_loadu_ps(b + i), s0);
    s1 = _mm512_fmadd_ps(_mm512_loadu_ps(a + i + 16), _mm512_loadu_ps(b + i + 16), s1);
    s2 = _mm512_fmadd_ps(_mm512_loadu_ps(a + i + 32), _mm512_loadu_ps(b + i + 32), s2);
    s3 = _mm512_fmadd_ps(_mm512_loadu_ps(a + i + 48), _mm512_loadu_ps(b + i + 48), s3);
  }
  return _mm512_reduce_add_ps(_mm512_add_ps(_mm512_add_ps(s0, s1), _mm512_add_ps(s2, s3)));
}

RAG_ALWAYS_INLINE void dot4_avx512(const float* q, const float* r, std::size_t stride, std::size_t n,
                                   float* out) noexcept {
  __m512 a0 = _mm512_setzero_ps(), a1 = a0, a2 = a0, a3 = a0;
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; i += 16) {
    const __m512 qv = _mm512_loadu_ps(q + i);
    a0 = _mm512_fmadd_ps(_mm512_load_ps(r + i), qv, a0);
    a1 = _mm512_fmadd_ps(_mm512_load_ps(r + stride + i), qv, a1);
    a2 = _mm512_fmadd_ps(_mm512_load_ps(r + 2 * stride + i), qv, a2);
    a3 = _mm512_fmadd_ps(_mm512_load_ps(r + 3 * stride + i), qv, a3);
  }
  out[0] = _mm512_reduce_add_ps(a0); out[1] = _mm512_reduce_add_ps(a1);
  out[2] = _mm512_reduce_add_ps(a2); out[3] = _mm512_reduce_add_ps(a3);
}
#endif

#if defined(__AVX512BW__)
// Same sign trick as AVX2. AVX-512 has no vpsignb, so the sign transfer is a
// masked subtract driven by the sign bits of a.
RAG_ALWAYS_INLINE std::int32_t dot_i8_avx512(const std::int8_t* a, const std::int8_t* b, std::size_t n) noexcept {
  const __m512i zero = _mm512_setzero_si512();
  __m512i acc = zero;
#if !defined(__AVX512VNNI__)
  const __m512i ones = _mm512_set1_epi16(1);
#endif
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; i += 64) {
    const __m512i va = _mm512_loadu_si512(a + i);
    const __m512i vb = _mm512_loadu_si512(b + i);
    const __m512i ua = _mm512_abs_epi8(va);
    const __m512i sb = _mm512_mask_sub_epi8(vb, _mm512_movepi8_mask(va), zero, vb);
#if defined(__AVX512VNNI__)
    acc = _mm512_dpbusd_epi32(acc, ua, sb);  // u8*s8, 4-way sum into i32, one uop
#else
    acc = _mm512_add_epi32(acc, _mm512_madd_epi16(_mm512_maddubs_epi16(ua, sb), ones));
#endif
  }
  return _mm512_reduce_add_epi32(acc);
}
#endif

// ----------------------- best-available front ends --------------------------
RAG_ALWAYS_INLINE float dot(const float* a, const float* b, std::size_t n) noexcept {
#if defined(__AVX512F__)
  return dot_avx512(a, b, n);
#elif defined(RAG_AVX2_FMA)
  return dot_avx2(a, b, n);
#else
  return dot_scalar(a, b, n);
#endif
}

// out[j] = <q, r + j*stride>, j = 0..3. Rows must be 64-byte aligned.
RAG_ALWAYS_INLINE void dot4(const float* q, const float* r, std::size_t stride, std::size_t n, float* out) noexcept {
#if defined(__AVX512F__)
  dot4_avx512(q, r, stride, n, out);
#elif defined(RAG_AVX2_FMA)
  dot4_avx2(q, r, stride, n, out);
#else
  for (int j = 0; j < 4; ++j) out[j] = dot_scalar(q, r + j * stride, n);
#endif
}

// One lane of dot4: identical summation order (single accumulator, same
// vector width, same horizontal reduction), so dot1(q, r) is bit-identical to
// the matching dot4 output. Scans use it for tail rows so that a row's score
// never depends on where it fell in a 4-row block, or on batching. Note that
// dot() above uses four accumulators and does NOT match dot4 bitwise.
RAG_ALWAYS_INLINE float dot1(const float* q, const float* r, std::size_t n) noexcept {
#if defined(__AVX512F__)
  __m512 a = _mm512_setzero_ps();
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; i += 16) a = _mm512_fmadd_ps(_mm512_loadu_ps(r + i), _mm512_loadu_ps(q + i), a);
  return _mm512_reduce_add_ps(a);
#elif defined(RAG_AVX2_FMA)
  __m256 a = _mm256_setzero_ps();
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; i += 8) a = _mm256_fmadd_ps(_mm256_loadu_ps(r + i), _mm256_loadu_ps(q + i), a);
  return hsum256(a);
#else
  return dot_scalar(q, r, n);
#endif
}

RAG_ALWAYS_INLINE std::int32_t dot_i8(const std::int8_t* a, const std::int8_t* b, std::size_t n) noexcept {
#if defined(__AVX512BW__)
  return dot_i8_avx512(a, b, n);
#elif defined(__AVX2__)
  return dot_i8_avx2(a, b, n);
#else
  return dot_i8_scalar(a, b, n);
#endif
}

// Symmetric per-vector int8 quantisation into [-127, 127].
// Returns the dequantisation scale s such that x[i] ~= s * q[i].
inline float quantize_i8(const float* in, std::int8_t* out, std::size_t n) noexcept {
  float maxabs = 0.f;
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) maxabs = std::fmax(maxabs, std::fabs(in[i]));
  if (maxabs == 0.f) {
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) out[i] = 0;
    return 0.f;
  }
  const float inv = 127.f / maxabs;
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    const float v = std::nearbyint(in[i] * inv);
    out[i] = static_cast<std::int8_t>(std::fmin(127.f, std::fmax(-127.f, v)));
  }
  return maxabs / 127.f;
}

// In-place L2 normalisation; leaves an all-zero vector untouched.
inline void normalize(float* v, std::size_t n) noexcept {
  const float nn = dot_scalar(v, v, n);
  if (nn <= 0.f) return;
  const float inv = 1.f / std::sqrt(nn);
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) v[i] *= inv;
}

}  // namespace rag::simd
```

```cpp
// rag/text_clean.hpp — cleanup for text extracted from paginated documents
// (PDFs), before it is chunked and indexed. No dependencies; cold path.
//
// Text extracted from a PDF has artifacts that hurt retrieval:
//   * typographic ligatures: "ﬁnance" is U+FB01 + "nance", which never
//     matches the query "finance";
//   * words hyphenated across line ends ("micro-" / "structure");
//   * hard line breaks in the middle of every sentence;
//   * running headers, footers and page numbers repeated on every page,
//     which pollute every chunk and dominate BM25 statistics;
//   * soft hyphens, zero-width spaces, BOMs, non-breaking and other Unicode
//     spaces, and control characters.
// clean_pages() fixes all of these, page by page, keeping the page structure
// so that chunks can still be cited by page.
#pragma once

#include <algorithm>
#include <cctype>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <map>
#include <set>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <vector>

namespace rag::text {

struct CleanOptions {
  bool dehyphenate = true;   // "micro-\nstructure" -> "microstructure"
  bool join_lines = true;    // single line breaks inside a paragraph become spaces
  bool strip_repeated_lines = true;  // running headers, footers, page numbers
  // A line is "running" if, in at least this share of pages, a line with the
  // same shape (see line_key) is among the first or last
  // `edge_lines` non-empty lines of the page...
  double repeated_line_fraction = 0.5;
  std::size_t edge_lines = 2;
  // ...and the document has at least this many pages. A repeat always needs
  // at least two pages, so in a 2-page document the line must be on both.
  std::size_t min_pages_for_repeats = 2;
};

// Character-level normalisation of one page:
//   ligatures U+FB00..FB06 -> ff fi fl ffi ffl st st
//   U+2010 / U+2011 (hyphen, non-breaking hyphen) -> '-'
//   NBSP, U+2000..200A, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000 -> ' '
//   soft hyphen, zero-width space/joiners, BOM -> removed
//   CR LF / CR / form feed / vertical tab -> '\n'; tab -> ' '
//   other ASCII control characters -> removed
// Anything else (including invalid UTF-8) passes through unchanged.
inline std::string normalize_chars(std::string_view in) {
  std::string out;
  out.reserve(in.size());
  const auto* p = reinterpret_cast<const unsigned char*>(in.data());
  const std::size_t n = in.size();
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < n;) {
    const unsigned char c = p[i];
    if (c < 0x80) {
      if (c == '\r') {
        out += '\n';
        i += (i + 1 < n && p[i + 1] == '\n') ? 2 : 1;
        continue;
      }
      if (c == '\f' || c == '\v') out += '\n';
      else if (c == '\t') out += ' ';
      else if (c >= 0x20 || c == '\n') out += static_cast<char>(c);
      // other control characters (NUL, ESC, ...) are dropped
      ++i;
      continue;
    }
    if (c == 0xC2 && i + 1 < n) {
      if (p[i + 1] == 0xA0) { out += ' '; i += 2; continue; }  // NBSP
      if (p[i + 1] == 0xAD) { i += 2; continue; }              // soft hyphen
    }
    if (c == 0xE2 && i + 2 < n && p[i + 1] == 0x80 && p[i + 2] >= 0x80 && p[i + 2] <= 0xBF) {
      const unsigned char d = p[i + 2];  // a real continuation byte: U+2000..U+203F
      if (d <= 0x8A || d == 0xAF) { out += ' '; i += 3; continue; }  // U+2000..200A, U+202F spaces
      if (d >= 0x8B && d <= 0x8D) { i += 3; continue; }              // zero-width space / non-joiner / joiner
      if (d == 0x90 || d == 0x91) { out += '-'; i += 3; continue; }  // hyphen, non-breaking hyphen
    }
    if (c == 0xE2 && i + 2 < n && p[i + 1] == 0x81 && p[i + 2] == 0x9F) { out += ' '; i += 3; continue; }  // U+205F
    if (c == 0xE3 && i + 2 < n && p[i + 1] == 0x80 && p[i + 2] == 0x80) { out += ' '; i += 3; continue; }  // U+3000
    if (c == 0xEF && i + 2 < n && p[i + 1] == 0xBB && p[i + 2] == 0xBF) { i += 3; continue; }  // BOM / ZWNBSP
    // Ligatures U+FB00..FB06. The third byte must be a real continuation byte
    // (>= 0x80): indexing kLig with a smaller one would underflow.
    if (c == 0xEF && i + 2 < n && p[i + 1] == 0xAC && p[i + 2] >= 0x80 && p[i + 2] <= 0x86) {
      static constexpr std::string_view kLig[] = {"ff", "fi", "fl", "ffi", "ffl", "st", "st"};
      out += kLig[p[i + 2] - 0x80];
      i += 3;
      continue;
    }
    out += static_cast<char>(c);
    ++i;
  }
  return out;
}

namespace detail {

inline bool is_hspace(char c) { return c == ' ' || c == '\t'; }

inline std::string_view trim(std::string_view s) {
  while (!s.empty() && is_hspace(s.front())) s.remove_prefix(1);
  while (!s.empty() && is_hspace(s.back())) s.remove_suffix(1);
  return s;
}

inline std::vector<std::string_view> split_lines(std::string_view s) {
  std::vector<std::string_view> lines;
  std::size_t start = 0;
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i <= s.size(); ++i)
    if (i == s.size() || s[i] == '\n') {
      lines.push_back(s.substr(start, i - start));
      start = i + 1;
    }
  return lines;
}

}  // namespace detail

// The "shape" of a line for header/footer detection: ASCII case-folded and
// whitespace collapsed. In short lines (<= kDigitBlindMaxWords words), every
// run of digits also becomes '#', so "Page 3 of 10" and "Page 4 of 10" share
// the key "page # of #". Longer lines must repeat exactly: otherwise body
// sentences that differ only in numbers ("Q3 revenue grew 12% ...",
// "Q4 revenue grew 15% ...") would look like one running header.
inline constexpr std::size_t kDigitBlindMaxWords = 6;

inline std::string line_key(std::string_view line) {
  const std::string_view t = detail::trim(line);
  std::size_t words = 0;
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < t.size(); ++i)
    if (!detail::is_hspace(t[i]) && (i == 0 || detail::is_hspace(t[i - 1]))) ++words;
  const bool digit_blind = words <= kDigitBlindMaxWords;
  std::string k;
  bool space = false, digit = false;
  for (char ch : t) {
    const auto c = static_cast<unsigned char>(ch);
    if (detail::is_hspace(ch)) { space = true; digit = false; continue; }
    if (space && !k.empty()) k += ' ';
    space = false;
    if (digit_blind && std::isdigit(c)) {
      if (!digit) k += '#';
      digit = true;
      continue;
    }
    digit = false;
    k += (c < 0x80) ? static_cast<char>(std::tolower(c)) : ch;
  }
  return k;
}

// Remove running headers/footers: lines whose key occurs near the top or
// bottom of enough pages (see CleanOptions). Only lines in those edge
// positions are removed; the same text in the body of a page is kept.
inline void strip_repeated_lines(std::vector<std::string>& pages, const CleanOptions& o) {
  if (pages.size() < std::max<std::size_t>(o.min_pages_for_repeats, 2)) return;
  // Edge line indices of every page.
  std::vector<std::vector<std::size_t>> edges(pages.size());
  std::vector<std::vector<std::string_view>> lines(pages.size());
  std::map<std::string, std::size_t> pages_with;
  for (std::size_t pg = 0; pg < pages.size(); ++pg) {
    lines[pg] = detail::split_lines(pages[pg]);
    std::vector<std::size_t> nonempty;
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < lines[pg].size(); ++i)
      if (!detail::trim(lines[pg][i]).empty()) nonempty.push_back(i);
    std::set<std::size_t> e;
    for (std::size_t j = 0; j < nonempty.size() && j < o.edge_lines; ++j) e.insert(nonempty[j]);
    for (std::size_t j = 0; j < nonempty.size() && j < o.edge_lines; ++j) e.insert(nonempty[nonempty.size() - 1 - j]);
    edges[pg].assign(e.begin(), e.end());
    std::set<std::string> keys;
    for (std::size_t i : edges[pg]) keys.insert(line_key(lines[pg][i]));
    for (const auto& k : keys) ++pages_with[k];
  }
  const auto needed = std::max<std::size_t>(
      2, static_cast<std::size_t>(std::ceil(o.repeated_line_fraction * static_cast<double>(pages.size()))));
  for (std::size_t pg = 0; pg < pages.size(); ++pg) {
    std::set<std::size_t> drop;
    for (std::size_t i : edges[pg])
      if (pages_with[line_key(lines[pg][i])] >= needed) drop.insert(i);
    if (drop.empty()) continue;
    std::string kept;
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < lines[pg].size(); ++i) {
      if (drop.count(i)) continue;
      if (!kept.empty()) kept += '\n';
      kept += lines[pg][i];
    }
    pages[pg] = std::move(kept);
  }
}

// Rebuild paragraphs from hard-wrapped lines. Lines are trimmed and inner
// whitespace collapsed; blank lines separate paragraphs ("\n\n" in the
// output). With dehyphenate, a line ending in letter + '-' followed by a line
// starting with a lowercase letter is joined without the hyphen.
inline std::string reflow(std::string_view page, const CleanOptions& o) {
  std::string out;
  bool in_paragraph = false, pending_break = false;
  for (std::string_view raw : detail::split_lines(page)) {
    // Trim and collapse runs of horizontal whitespace.
    std::string line;
    bool sp = false;
    for (char ch : detail::trim(raw)) {
      if (detail::is_hspace(ch)) { sp = true; continue; }
      if (sp) line += ' ';
      sp = false;
      line += ch;
    }
    if (line.empty()) {
      if (in_paragraph) pending_break = true;
      continue;
    }
    if (!in_paragraph) {
      out += line;
      in_paragraph = true;
      continue;
    }
    if (pending_break || !o.join_lines) {
      out += pending_break ? "\n\n" : "\n";
      out += line;
      pending_break = false;
      continue;
    }
    const bool hyphen_break = o.dehyphenate && out.size() >= 2 && out.back() == '-' &&
                              std::isalpha(static_cast<unsigned char>(out[out.size() - 2])) &&
                              std::islower(static_cast<unsigned char>(line.front()));
    if (hyphen_break) out.pop_back();
    else out += ' ';
    out += line;
  }
  return out;
}

// The full pipeline for one document: normalize characters on every page,
// strip running headers/footers across pages, then reflow each page.
inline std::vector<std::string> clean_pages(std::vector<std::string> pages, const CleanOptions& o = {}) {
  for (auto& p : pages) p = normalize_chars(p);
  if (o.strip_repeated_lines) strip_repeated_lines(pages, o);
  for (auto& p : pages) p = reflow(p, o);
  return pages;
}

// Join cleaned pages into one text (pages separated by a blank line) plus the
// byte offset at which each page starts, ready for IngestOptions::page_starts.
struct PagedText {
  std::string text;
  std::vector<std::uint32_t> page_starts;
};

inline PagedText join_pages(const std::vector<std::string>& pages) {
  PagedText r;
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < pages.size(); ++i) {
    // Always separate, even around empty pages: page starts then strictly
    // increase, and no page's bytes are ever attributed to a neighbour.
    if (i > 0) r.text += "\n\n";
    r.page_starts.push_back(static_cast<std::uint32_t>(r.text.size()));
    r.text += pages[i];
  }
  return r;
}

}  // namespace rag::text
```

```cpp
// rag/tokenizer.hpp — allocation-free ASCII/UTF-8 word tokenizer with
// compile-time hashing and a compile-time stopword table.
//
// Latency notes:
//  * One 256-entry constexpr lookup table classifies + lowercases each byte:
//    a single L1-resident load per byte, no locale, no branches on ranges.
//  * Terms are identified by a 64-bit hash computed in the same pass, so no
//    std::string is ever built. Hashes are constexpr, which lets the stopword
//    set be a sorted std::array baked into .rodata at compile time.
//  * Bytes >= 0x80 are treated as word characters, so UTF-8 words survive
//    intact (no Unicode case folding — documented limitation).
#pragma once

#include <algorithm>
#include <array>
#include <cstdint>
#include <span>
#include <string_view>

#include "rag/common.hpp"

namespace rag {

struct Token {
  std::uint32_t offset;  // byte offset into the source text
  std::uint32_t length;  // byte length
  std::uint64_t hash;    // term id (lower-cased FNV-1a + avalanche)
};

namespace detail {

// 0 => separator; otherwise the lower-cased byte value.
inline constexpr std::array<std::uint8_t, 256> kCharMap = [] {
  std::array<std::uint8_t, 256> t{};
  for (int c = 0; c < 256; ++c) {
    if (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') t[c] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(c);
    else if (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') t[c] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(c - 'A' + 'a');
    else if (c >= '0' && c <= '9') t[c] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(c);
    else if (c >= 0x80) t[c] = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(c);
  }
  return t;
}();

inline constexpr std::uint64_t kFnvOffset = 14695981039346656037ull;
inline constexpr std::uint64_t kFnvPrime = 1099511628211ull;

// splitmix64 finaliser: FNV-1a's low bits are weak, and we index hash tables
// and embedding buckets with them.
constexpr std::uint64_t mix64(std::uint64_t x) noexcept {
  x ^= x >> 30; x *= 0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9ull;
  x ^= x >> 27; x *= 0x94d049bb133111ebull;
  x ^= x >> 31;
  return x;
}

}  // namespace detail

// Hash of a single term, case-insensitive. constexpr: usable in static_assert.
constexpr std::uint64_t hash_term(std::string_view s) noexcept {
  std::uint64_t h = detail::kFnvOffset;
  for (char ch : s) {
    const auto c = detail::kCharMap[static_cast<std::uint8_t>(ch)];
    h = (h ^ c) * detail::kFnvPrime;
  }
  return detail::mix64(h);
}

// Streaming tokenizer: calls f(Token) for every word. No allocation.
template <class F>
RAG_ALWAYS_INLINE void for_each_token(std::string_view text, F&& f) noexcept(noexcept(f(Token{}))) {
  const auto* p = reinterpret_cast<const std::uint8_t*>(text.data());
  const std::uint32_t n = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(text.size());
  std::uint32_t i = 0;
  while (i < n) {
    while (i < n && detail::kCharMap[p[i]] == 0) ++i;  // skip separators
    if (i >= n) break;
    const std::uint32_t start = i;
    std::uint64_t h = detail::kFnvOffset;
    std::uint8_t c;
    while (i < n && (c = detail::kCharMap[p[i]]) != 0) {
      h = (h ^ c) * detail::kFnvPrime;
      ++i;
    }
    f(Token{start, i - start, detail::mix64(h)});
  }
}

// Bounded tokenizer into a caller-owned buffer (hot path: query text).
// Returns the number of tokens written; silently truncates when out is full.
inline std::size_t tokenize(std::string_view text, std::span<Token> out) noexcept {
  std::size_t n = 0;
  const std::size_t cap = out.size();
  // Early exit once full: overlong queries are truncated, never overflow.
  const auto* p = reinterpret_cast<const std::uint8_t*>(text.data());
  const std::uint32_t len = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(text.size());
  std::uint32_t i = 0;
  while (i < len && n < cap) {
    while (i < len && detail::kCharMap[p[i]] == 0) ++i;
    if (i >= len) break;
    const std::uint32_t start = i;
    std::uint64_t h = detail::kFnvOffset;
    std::uint8_t c;
    while (i < len && (c = detail::kCharMap[p[i]]) != 0) { h = (h ^ c) * detail::kFnvPrime; ++i; }
    out[n++] = Token{start, i - start, detail::mix64(h)};
  }
  return n;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Compile-time stopword set: sorted hashes in .rodata, binary-searched.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
inline constexpr auto kStopwords = [] {
  constexpr std::string_view words[] = {
      "a",    "an",   "and",  "are",   "as",   "at",    "be",   "but",  "by",    "for",
      "from", "has",  "have", "how",   "i",    "if",    "in",   "into", "is",    "it",
      "its",  "of",   "on",   "or",    "that", "the",   "their","then", "there", "these",
      "they", "this", "to",   "was",   "we",   "were",  "what", "when", "where", "which",
      "who",  "why",  "will", "with",  "you",  "your",  "does", "do",   "can",   "about"};
  std::array<std::uint64_t, std::size(words)> h{};
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < h.size(); ++i) h[i] = hash_term(words[i]);
  std::ranges::sort(h);
  return h;
}();

constexpr bool is_stopword(std::uint64_t h) noexcept {
  return std::ranges::binary_search(kStopwords, h);
}

static_assert(hash_term("Order") == hash_term("oRDER"), "hashing must be case-insensitive");
static_assert(is_stopword(hash_term("The")) && !is_stopword(hash_term("orderbook")));

}  // namespace rag
```

```cpp
// rag/topk.hpp — fixed-capacity top-K selection on the stack.
//
// Latency notes:
//  * Storage is std::array<Hit, Cap>: no allocation, lives in the caller's frame.
//  * A cached admission threshold turns the common case (candidate worse
//    than the current K-th best) into one compare + a well-predicted branch;
//    after warm-up nearly every candidate takes the [[likely]] reject path.
//  * The heap is a min-heap on "goodness", so the root is the worst kept hit.
//  * Ordering is total (score desc, then id asc) so results are deterministic
//    even with tied scores — important for reproducible retrieval tests.
#pragma once

#include <algorithm>
#include <array>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <limits>
#include <span>

namespace rag {

struct Hit {
  float score;
  std::uint32_t id;
  friend constexpr bool operator==(const Hit&, const Hit&) = default;
};

// a ranks ahead of b
constexpr bool better(const Hit& a, const Hit& b) noexcept {
  return a.score > b.score || (a.score == b.score && a.id < b.id);
}

template <std::size_t Cap>
class TopK {
  static_assert(Cap > 0);

 public:
  static constexpr std::size_t kCapacity = Cap;

  constexpr explicit TopK(std::size_t k = Cap) noexcept { reset(k); }

  // `min_score`: candidates must score >= min_score to be admitted at all.
  // It is folded into the admission threshold, so it costs nothing per push.
  constexpr void reset(std::size_t k, float min_score = -std::numeric_limits<float>::infinity()) noexcept {
    k_ = std::min(k, Cap);
    size_ = 0;
    sorted_ = false;
    // k == 0: a NaN threshold makes `score >= threshold_` false for every
    // input, so nothing is ever admitted and the heap is never touched.
    threshold_ = k_ ? min_score : std::numeric_limits<float>::quiet_NaN();
  }

  // Scores strictly below threshold() can never be admitted (NaN when k == 0).
  [[nodiscard]] constexpr float threshold() const noexcept { return threshold_; }

  constexpr void push(float score, std::uint32_t id) noexcept {
    // Written as !(>=) so NaN scores are rejected too. Ties with the threshold
    // pass through to the id tie-break below.
    if (!(score >= threshold_)) [[likely]] return;
    if (sorted_) [[unlikely]] {  // push after sorted(): restore heap order first
      std::make_heap(heap_.begin(), heap_.begin() + size_, better);
      sorted_ = false;
    }
    const Hit h{score, id};
    if (size_ < k_) {
      heap_[size_++] = h;
      std::push_heap(heap_.begin(), heap_.begin() + size_, better);
      if (size_ == k_) threshold_ = heap_[0].score;
    } else if (better(h, heap_[0])) {
      std::pop_heap(heap_.begin(), heap_.begin() + size_, better);
      heap_[size_ - 1] = h;
      std::push_heap(heap_.begin(), heap_.begin() + size_, better);
      threshold_ = heap_[0].score;
    }
  }

  // Sort in place (best first) and return a view. Idempotent; a later
  // push() transparently rebuilds the heap.
  [[nodiscard]] constexpr std::span<const Hit> sorted() noexcept {
    if (!sorted_) {
      std::sort_heap(heap_.begin(), heap_.begin() + size_, better);
      sorted_ = true;
    }
    return {heap_.data(), size_};
  }

  [[nodiscard]] constexpr std::size_t size() const noexcept { return size_; }
  [[nodiscard]] constexpr std::size_t k() const noexcept { return k_; }

 private:
  std::array<Hit, Cap> heap_{};
  std::size_t size_ = 0;
  std::size_t k_ = 0;
  float threshold_ = 0.f;
  bool sorted_ = false;
};

}  // namespace rag
```

```cpp
// rag/vector_store.hpp — fixed-capacity, append-only embedding store with
// single-writer / multi-reader lock-free publication.
//
// Layout (Struct of Arrays, each array one aligned allocation):
//   f32_    [capacity][D]  fp32 rows, 64 B aligned      -> exact scoring / rerank
//   i8_     [capacity][D]  int8 rows, 64 B aligned      -> 4x less memory traffic
//   scale_  [capacity]     dequantisation scale per row
//
// Concurrency protocol (SWMR):
//   writer: fill row n in all three arrays  ->  size_.store(n + 1, release)
//   reader: m = size_.load(acquire)         ->  rows [0, m) are fully visible
// Rows are never modified after publication, so readers need no locks, no
// retries, and never observe a torn row. size_ sits on its own cache line so
// the writer's stores do not invalidate the lines holding the read-only
// pointers that every reader touches (no false sharing).
#pragma once

#include <atomic>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <span>

#include "rag/common.hpp"
#include "rag/simd.hpp"
#include "rag/topk.hpp"

namespace rag {

template <std::size_t D>
  requires ValidDim<D>
class VectorStore {
 public:
  static constexpr std::size_t kDim = D;

  explicit VectorStore(std::size_t capacity)
      : capacity_(capacity),
        // Lazy: rows are written by append() before size_ publishes them, so
        // readers never fault, and unused capacity costs no physical memory.
        f32_(make_aligned_array<float>(capacity * D, Init::Lazy)),
        i8_(make_aligned_array<std::int8_t>(capacity * D, Init::Lazy)),
        scale_(make_aligned_array<float>(capacity, Init::Lazy)) {}

  // Single writer only. Returns false when full. `v` should be L2-normalised.
  bool append(std::span<const float, D> v) noexcept {
    const std::uint32_t n = size_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);  // writer owns size_
    if (n >= capacity_) [[unlikely]] return false;
    float* dst = f32_.get() + std::size_t{n} * D;
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < D; ++i) dst[i] = v[i];
    scale_[n] = simd::quantize_i8(dst, i8_.get() + std::size_t{n} * D, D);
    size_.store(n + 1, std::memory_order_release);  // publish
    return true;
  }

  [[nodiscard]] std::uint32_t size() const noexcept { return size_.load(std::memory_order_acquire); }
  [[nodiscard]] std::size_t capacity() const noexcept { return capacity_; }
  [[nodiscard]] const float* row(std::uint32_t i) const noexcept { return f32_.get() + std::size_t{i} * D; }
  [[nodiscard]] const std::int8_t* qrow(std::uint32_t i) const noexcept { return i8_.get() + std::size_t{i} * D; }
  [[nodiscard]] float qscale(std::uint32_t i) const noexcept { return scale_[i]; }

  // Exact cosine (= dot, rows normalised) over rows [begin, end).
  // `end` must come from size() on this thread (acquire) or be <= it.
  template <class TK>
  void search_exact(const float* q, std::uint32_t begin, std::uint32_t end, TK& out) const noexcept {
    std::uint32_t i = begin;
    float s[4];
    for (; i + 4 <= end; i += 4) {  // register-blocked: one q load feeds 4 rows
      simd::dot4(q, row(i), D, D, s);
      out.push(s[0], i); out.push(s[1], i + 1); out.push(s[2], i + 2); out.push(s[3], i + 3);
    }
    for (; i < end; ++i) out.push(simd::dot1(q, row(i), D), i);  // bit-identical to a dot4 lane
  }

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- batched
  // Score nq <= kMaxBatch queries in ONE pass over rows [begin, end). The
  // scans are DRAM-bound, so streaming each row once for all queries
  // multiplies throughput: the row is loaded from memory once and then
  // reused from L1 against every query.
  static constexpr std::size_t kMaxBatch = 8;

  // `qs`: nq_padded fp32 query rows, contiguous with stride D, 64 B aligned,
  // nq_padded = nq rounded up to a multiple of 4 (pad rows may hold anything;
  // their scores are discarded). outs[j] receives query j's hits.
  // Each score is bit-identical to search_exact() on the same query.
  template <class TK>
  void search_exact_batch(const float* qs, std::size_t nq, std::uint32_t begin, std::uint32_t end,
                          TK* const* outs) const noexcept {
    const std::size_t padded = (nq + 3) & ~std::size_t{3};
    float s[kMaxBatch];
    for (std::uint32_t i = begin; i < end; ++i) {
      const float* r = row(i);
      for (std::size_t j = 0; j < padded; j += 4) simd::dot4(r, qs + j * D, D, D, s + j);  // row x 4 queries
      for (std::size_t j = 0; j < nq; ++j) outs[j]->push(s[j], i);
    }
  }

  // Batched int8 scan: qqs[j] is query j's int8 vector.
  template <class TK>
  void search_int8_batch(const std::int8_t* const* qqs, std::size_t nq, std::uint32_t begin, std::uint32_t end,
                         TK* const* outs) const noexcept {
    for (std::uint32_t i = begin; i < end; ++i) {
      const std::int8_t* r = qrow(i);
      RAG_PREFETCH(r + 8 * D);
      const float sc = scale_[i];
      for (std::size_t j = 0; j < nq; ++j) outs[j]->push(static_cast<float>(simd::dot_i8(qqs[j], r, D)) * sc, i);
    }
  }

  // Approximate scan over int8 rows. Scores are dequantised dot products;
  // the query scale is a positive constant so it is folded out of ranking.
  template <class TK>
  void search_int8(const std::int8_t* qq, std::uint32_t begin, std::uint32_t end, TK& out) const noexcept {
    for (std::uint32_t i = begin; i < end; ++i) {
      RAG_PREFETCH(qrow(i) + 8 * D);  // stay ~8 rows (3 KiB @ D=384) ahead of the stream
      out.push(static_cast<float>(simd::dot_i8(qq, qrow(i), D)) * scale_[i], i);
    }
  }

  // Two-stage search: int8 scan keeps `cand` candidates, fp32 reranks them.
  // Recall is close to exact while the bulk scan moves 4x fewer bytes.
  template <class TKCand, class TK>
  void search_two_stage(const float* q, const std::int8_t* qq, std::uint32_t begin, std::uint32_t end,
                        TKCand& cand, TK& out) const noexcept {
    search_int8(qq, begin, end, cand);
    for (const Hit& h : cand.sorted()) out.push(simd::dot(q, row(h.id), D), h.id);
  }

 private:
  std::size_t capacity_;
  AlignedArray<float> f32_;
  AlignedArray<std::int8_t> i8_;
  AlignedArray<float> scale_;
  alignas(kCacheLine) std::atomic<std::uint32_t> size_{0};
  [[maybe_unused]] char pad_[kCacheLine - sizeof(std::atomic<std::uint32_t>)]{};
};

}  // namespace rag

```

```cpp
// agent_demo — a self-learning execution agent, end to end.
//
//   1. the task and its baselines (TWAP, a hand-written rule, the DP optimum)
//   2. learning from scratch, measured against the optimum on unseen scenarios
//   3. what the agent learned (its policy next to the optimal one)
//   4. two kinds of learner: parametric vs episodic memory
//   5. the world changes: drift detection, re-exploration, recovery
//   6. learning a model instead, and checking whether the model is right
#include <cstdio>
#include <string>

#include "rag/agent/execution_dp.hpp"
#include "rag/agent/model_based.hpp"
#include "rag/agent/trainer.hpp"

using namespace rag::agent;

namespace {

constexpr std::uint64_t kHeldOut = 50'000'000;  // scenarios never used for training
constexpr std::uint32_t kEvalN = 2000;

auto twap = [](const ExecutionObs&) { return ExecutionEnv::kTwapAction; };

template <class Policy>
EvalStats gain_vs_twap(const ExecutionEnv& env, Policy&& p) {
  return compare(env, p, twap, kEvalN, kHeldOut);
}

void rule(const char* title) { std::printf("\n== %s %.*s\n", title, static_cast<int>(70 - std::string(title).size()), "======================================================================"); }

}  // namespace

int main() {
  ExecutionParams p;
  ExecutionEnv env(p);
  const ExecutionDP dp(p);
  auto optimal = [&](const ExecutionObs& o) { return dp.act(o); };
  auto sign_rule = [](const ExecutionObs& o) { return o.signal < 0 ? Action{3} : Action{1}; };

  rule("1. The task");
  std::printf("Sell %u lots in %u steps. Fast selling costs impact (%.2f x lots^2 per step);\n"
              "slow selling risks the price. A noisy signal predicts the next move, but the\n"
              "agent is not told that: it sees (time, inventory, signal) and a reward.\n\n",
              p.lots, p.horizon, p.impact);
  const auto g_opt = gain_vs_twap(env, optimal);
  const auto g_rule = gain_vs_twap(env, sign_rule);
  std::printf("  %-34s %+7.2f\n", "TWAP (sell evenly)", 0.0);
  std::printf("  %-34s %+7.2f +- %.2f   (%4.1f%% of optimal)\n", "rule: sell faster if signal < 0", g_rule.mean, g_rule.std_error,
              100 * g_rule.mean / g_opt.mean);
  std::printf("  %-34s %+7.2f +- %.2f   (knows the model)\n", "DP optimum", g_opt.mean, g_opt.std_error);
  std::printf("  (gain over TWAP per episode on %u held-out scenarios, in price units)\n", kEvalN);

  rule("2. Learning from scratch");
  AgentConfig<3> cfg;
  cfg.eps_decay_episodes = 20000;
  Agent<ExecutionEnv> agent(env, cfg);
  Trainer<ExecutionEnv> trainer(agent, env, {.eval_every = 5000, .eval_episodes = 1000});
  std::printf("  %8s  %6s  %6s  %22s  %s\n", "episode", "eps", "alpha", "gain vs TWAP", "champion");
  trainer.run(40000, [&](const EvalPoint& e) {
    const auto g = gain_vs_twap(env, [&](const ExecutionObs& o) { return agent.act(o, false); });  // the learner
    std::printf("  %8llu  %6.3f  %6.4f  %+7.2f (%5.1f%% of opt)  %s\n", static_cast<unsigned long long>(e.episode), e.epsilon,
                agent.step_size(), g.mean, 100 * g.mean / g_opt.mean, e.promoted ? "promoted" : "kept");
  });
  auto deployed = [&](const ExecutionObs& o) { return trainer.deployed_act(o); };
  const auto g_agent = gain_vs_twap(env, deployed);
  std::printf("  deployed (champion): %+.2f +- %.2f = %.1f%% of the optimal gain\n", g_agent.mean, g_agent.std_error,
              100 * g_agent.mean / g_opt.mean);

  rule("3. What it learned");
  std::printf("Lots sold at step 10 with 50 lots left, by signal (in standard deviations):\n\n  %-8s", "signal");
  const double sigs[] = {-2, -1.5, -1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2};
  for (double s : sigs) std::printf("%6.1f", s);
  for (int who = 0; who < 2; ++who) {
    std::printf("\n  %-8s", who ? "optimal" : "agent");
    for (double s : sigs) {
      const ExecutionObs o{10, 50, s * p.signal_sd};
      std::printf("%6u", env.lots_for(who ? dp.act(o) : trainer.deployed_act(o), 50));
    }
  }
  std::printf("\n\nThe agent discovered on its own that a negative signal means \"sell now\".\n");

  rule("4. Parametric vs episodic learning");
  std::printf("Share of the optimal gain after N training episodes:\n\n  %-10s %10s %10s\n", "episodes", "TileQ", "Episodic");
  for (std::uint32_t n : {500u, 1000u, 2000u}) {
    double share[2];
    for (int k = 0; k < 2; ++k) {
      AgentConfig<3> c;
      c.learner = k ? LearnerKind::Episodic : LearnerKind::TileQ;
      c.eps_decay_episodes = n / 2;
      ExecutionEnv e(p);
      Agent<ExecutionEnv> a(e, c);
      Trainer<ExecutionEnv> t(a, e, {.eval_every = 0, .detect_drift = false});
      t.run(n);
      share[k] = 100 * compare(e, [&](const ExecutionObs& o) { return a.act(o, false); }, twap, 500, kHeldOut).mean / g_opt.mean;
    }
    std::printf("  %-10u %9.1f%% %9.1f%%\n", n, share[0], share[1]);
  }
  std::printf("\nEpisodic memory reuses single good episodes immediately; the parametric\n"
              "learner generalizes better and wins with more data (65-72%% at 40k+).\n");

  rule("5. The world changes");
  ExecutionParams flipped = p;
  flipped.alpha = -p.alpha;
  const ExecutionDP dp2(flipped);
  ExecutionEnv env_off = env;
  Agent<ExecutionEnv> stubborn = agent;  // same knowledge, no drift detection
  env.set_alpha(flipped.alpha);
  env_off.set_alpha(flipped.alpha);
  // Same supervision (evaluation, champion), drift detection off.
  Trainer<ExecutionEnv> trainer_off(stubborn, env_off, {.eval_every = 5000, .eval_episodes = 1000, .detect_drift = false});
  const double opt2 = compare(env, [&](const ExecutionObs& o) { return dp2.act(o); }, twap, 1000, kHeldOut).mean;
  auto share2 = [&](Trainer<ExecutionEnv>& t) {
    return 100 * compare(env, [&](const ExecutionObs& o) { return t.deployed_act(o); }, twap, 1000, kHeldOut).mean / opt2;
  };
  std::printf("The signal's meaning flips: it now predicts the opposite move.\n");
  std::printf("Right after the flip the agent captures %.0f%% of the new optimum (negative: harmful).\n\n", share2(trainer));
  std::printf("  %10s %20s %20s\n", "episodes", "with drift detection", "without");
  for (std::uint32_t done = 0; done < 40000;) {
    const auto rep = trainer.run(5000);
    trainer_off.run(5000);
    done += 5000;
    std::string note;
    for (auto at : rep.drift_alarms) note += "  <- drift detected " + std::to_string(at - 40000) + " episodes after the flip";
    std::printf("  %10u %19.1f%% %19.1f%%%s\n", done, share2(trainer), share2(trainer_off), note.c_str());
  }
  std::printf("\nOn an alarm the trainer raises exploration and step size and clears the\n"
              "replay buffer; the champion is re-scored on the new world and replaced.\n");

  rule("6. Learning a model instead");
  std::printf("A model-based agent assumes the *form* of the market and learns only its\n"
              "numbers, by regression on what it observes; then it plans with the DP.\n\n");
  {
    ModelBasedExecutionAgent mb(p, {.cost_model = CostModel::Shrunk});
    ExecutionEnv e(p);
    Rng rng(7);
    train_model_based(mb, e, 50, rng);
    mb.replan();
    const ModelEstimate m = mb.model();
    std::printf("  after 50 episodes:  impact %.4f (true %.4f)  alpha %.3f (%.3f)  rho %.3f (%.3f)\n", m.impact, p.impact, m.alpha,
                p.alpha, m.rho, p.signal_rho);
    const auto g = gain_vs_twap(ExecutionEnv(p), [&](const ExecutionObs& o) { return mb.act(o, false); });
    std::printf("  its plan: %.1f%% of the optimal gain (the model-free agent needed 40,000 episodes for %.0f%%)\n",
                100 * g.mean / g_opt.mean, 100 * g_agent.mean / g_opt.mean);
  }
  ExecutionParams perm = p;
  perm.permanent_impact = 0.01;
  const ExecutionEnv pe(perm);
  const ExecutionDP pdp(perm);
  const double opt3 = compare(pe, [&](const ExecutionObs& o) { return pdp.act(o); }, twap, 1000, kHeldOut).mean;
  std::printf("\nNow a market with permanent impact: each lot sold lowers the price of\n"
              "everything still held. 300 episodes each:\n\n");
  for (bool term : {false, true}) {
    ModelBasedExecutionAgent mb(perm, {.cost_model = CostModel::Shrunk, .learn_permanent_impact = term});
    ExecutionEnv e(perm);
    Rng rng(7);
    train_model_based(mb, e, 300, rng);
    mb.replan();
    const ModelCheck check = mb.check_model(pe, 100, kHeldOut + 1'000'000);
    const double share = 100 * compare(pe, [&](const ExecutionObs& o) { return mb.act(o, false); }, twap, 1000, kHeldOut).mean / opt3;
    std::printf("  %-34s %5.0f%% of optimal   model check: z = %+5.1f  %s\n",
                term ? "model with a permanent-impact term" : "model without it", share, check.z,
                check.z > 4 ? "-> the model is wrong" : "(consistent)");
  }
  std::printf("\nThe check compares the gain over TWAP the model predicts for its own plan\n"
              "with the gain measured on real scenarios, paired. A wrong model is\n"
              "optimistic: its planner picks the actions its errors flatter. When the\n"
              "missing term isn't known, distill the plan into a model-free learner and\n"
              "fine-tune it under a guard (docs/ai/EXPERIMENTS.md, E7).\n");
}
```

```cpp
// demo.cpp — end-to-end usage: ingest, commit, query, hand prompt to a generator.
#include <cstdio>

#include "rag.hpp"

namespace {
// Stand-in for an LLM client (llama.cpp, vLLM/TGI over HTTP, ...). Anything
// with generate(std::string_view) satisfies rag::Generator.
struct PrintGenerator {
  void generate(std::string_view prompt) { std::printf("----- prompt sent to generator -----\n%.*s\n", int(prompt.size()), prompt.data()); }
};
}  // namespace

int main() {
  rag::EngineConfig cfg;
  cfg.max_chunks = 4096;
  cfg.chunker = {48, 12};
  cfg.dense_mode = rag::DenseMode::Int8Rerank;
  rag::RagEngine<rag::HashingEmbedder<384>> engine(cfg);

  const char* docs[] = {
      "Order flow imbalance (OFI) is the net change in queued size at the best bid minus the best ask. "
      "Positive OFI indicates buying pressure and tends to precede upticks in the mid price over short horizons.",
      "A feed handler normalises exchange multicast packets into book updates. Gaps in sequence numbers "
      "trigger a snapshot recovery from the replay channel before the book is marked healthy again.",
      "VWAP algorithms split a parent order according to the expected intraday volume profile, trading "
      "more during the open and close when liquidity is deepest.",
      "Pre-trade risk checks validate price collars, maximum order quantity and credit limits in the "
      "order gateway, typically in under a microsecond using precomputed limits.",
  };
  for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < std::size(docs); ++i) engine.ingest(docs[i], i);
  engine.commit();

  auto ctx = engine.make_context();
  PrintGenerator gen;
  const auto r = engine.answer("What happens when the feed handler detects a sequence gap?", 3, ctx, gen);
  std::printf("----- hits -----\n");
  for (const auto& h : r.hits) {
    const auto c = engine.chunk(h.id);
    std::printf("  rrf=%.4f doc=%u chunk=%u  %.60s...\n", h.score, c.doc_id, c.ordinal, c.text.data());
  }
}
```

```cpp
// of_backtest — walk-forward backtest of order-flow scalping strategies on
// recorded ticks (CSV format: rag/orderflow/tick_csv.hpp). The tape is cut
// into consecutive windows (default 10 minutes, each with a 150 s feature
// warm-up); every strategy trades every window with 1 contract, market
// orders, 100 ms latency, the recorded spread and depth, and fees.
//
//   of_backtest <ticks.csv> [--tick 0.25] [--time ns|us|ms|s] [--window 600] [--fee 1.5] [NET...]
//
// NETs are networks saved by experiments/of3_rl.cpp (ScalpEnv agents).
// Reports per strategy: windows, mean net ticks per window (and $), t-stat,
// Sharpe per window, share of winning windows, total, and the maximum
// drawdown of the cumulative P&L across windows.
#include <algorithm>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <functional>
#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include "rag/agent/agent.hpp"
#include "rag/orderflow/replay_env.hpp"

using namespace rag::agent;
using namespace rag::orderflow;

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
  if (argc < 2) {
    std::fprintf(stderr, "usage: of_backtest <ticks.csv> [--tick 0.25] [--time ns] [--window 600] [--fee 1.5] [NET...]\n");
    return 2;
  }
  TickCsvOptions co;
  ReplayParams rp;
  std::vector<std::string> nets;
  for (int i = 2; i < argc; ++i) {
    const std::string a = argv[i];
    if (a == "--tick" && i + 1 < argc) co.tick_size = std::atof(argv[++i]);
    else if (a == "--time" && i + 1 < argc) co.time_unit = argv[++i];
    else if (a == "--window" && i + 1 < argc) rp.window_seconds = std::atof(argv[++i]);
    else if (a == "--fee" && i + 1 < argc) rp.fee_dollars = std::atof(argv[++i]);
    else nets.push_back(a);
  }
  auto tape = std::make_shared<const TickTape>(TickTape::from_csv(argv[1], co));
  const auto& st = tape->stats();
  std::printf("tape: %zu buckets (%.1f h), %zu trades, %zu quotes, %zu lines skipped, %zu gaps\n", tape->size(),
              static_cast<double>(tape->size()) * tape->bucket_seconds() / 3600, st.trades, st.quotes, st.skipped, st.gaps);
  ReplayScalpEnv probe(tape, rp);
  const std::size_t windows = probe.windows();
  std::printf("%zu windows of %.0f s\n", windows, rp.window_seconds);
  if (windows == 0) return 1;

  std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Agent<ReplayScalpEnv>>> agents;
  for (const auto& path : nets) {
    AgentConfig<ReplayScalpEnv::kStateDims> c;
    c.learner = LearnerKind::NeuralQ;
    c.bins.fill(1);
    c.double_q = true;
    c.nn_polyak = 1e-4;
    auto a = std::make_unique<Agent<ReplayScalpEnv>>(probe, c);
    auto s = a->snapshot();
    s.net = Mlp::load(path);
    a->restore(s);
    agents.push_back(std::move(a));
  }
  const auto n_of = [](const std::vector<double>& v) { return static_cast<double>(v.size()); };
  std::vector<std::pair<std::string, std::function<Action(const ScalpObs&)>>> strategies = {
      {"flat", [](const ScalpObs&) -> Action { return 1; }},
      {"delta 30 s rule", [](const ScalpObs& o) -> Action { return o.f[1] > 1.5 ? 2 : o.f[1] < -1.5 ? 0 : static_cast<Action>(o.position + 1); }},
  };
  for (std::size_t i = 0; i < agents.size(); ++i)
    strategies.push_back({nets[i].substr(nets[i].find_last_of("/\\") + 1), [&, i](const ScalpObs& o) { return agents[i]->act(o, false); }});

  std::printf("%-22s %8s %9s %8s %7s %8s %6s %9s %8s\n", "strategy", "windows", "ticks/win", "$/win", "t", "Sharpe", "win%", "total", "max DD");
  for (auto& [name, policy] : strategies) {
    std::vector<double> pnl;
    double orders = 0;
    for (std::size_t w = 0; w < windows; ++w) {
      ReplayScalpEnv env(tape, rp);
      Rng r(1);
      auto o = env.seek(w);
      for (;;) {
        const auto s = env.step(policy(o), r);
        o = s.obs;
        if (s.done) break;
      }
      pnl.push_back(env.net_pnl_ticks());
      orders += env.orders();
    }
    double m = 0, v = 0, wins = 0, cum = 0, peak = 0, dd = 0;
    for (double x : pnl) {
      m += x;
      wins += x > 0;
      cum += x;
      peak = std::max(peak, cum);
      dd = std::max(dd, peak - cum);
    }
    m /= n_of(pnl);
    for (double x : pnl) v += (x - m) * (x - m);
    const double sd = pnl.size() > 1 ? std::sqrt(v / (n_of(pnl) - 1)) : 0;
    std::printf("%-22s %8zu %+9.2f %+8.1f %+7.2f %+8.3f %5.1f%% %+9.1f %8.1f   (%.1f orders/win)\n", name.c_str(), pnl.size(), m, m * kTickValue,
                sd > 0 ? m / (sd / std::sqrt(n_of(pnl))) : 0.0, sd > 0 ? m / sd : 0.0, 100 * wins / n_of(pnl), cum, dd, orders / n_of(pnl));
  }
}
```
